words.enDefinition: An example used to identify the letter A clearly by saying a familiar word beginning with it.

examples.en: I said “A as in apple” because the receptionist thought the first letter was E.
examples.zh: 接待员以为第一个字母是 E，我就说「A，apple 的首字母」。

examples.en: Could you confirm “A as in apple” for the first letter of our booking code?
examples.zh: 预约代码的第一个字母能确认一下吗，是「apple 开头的那个 A」？

collocations: say A as in apple
confirm A as in apple
clarify with A as in apple

words.enDefinition: help that takes a lot of time or effort to provide

examples.en: I know it's a big favour to ask you to water all these plants.
examples.zh: 我知道，请你给这些植物都浇水，是要你「帮一个挺大的忙」。

examples.en: She asked for a big favour before explaining how many boxes she had.
examples.zh: 她先说要我「帮一个挺大的忙」，再解释她有多少个箱子。

collocations: ask for a big favour
do me a big favour
know it is a big favour

words.enDefinition: A duplicate of the written complaint you sent, kept so that you or someone else can refer to it.

examples.en: I brought a copy of my complaint so we could check the dates together at reception.
examples.zh: 我带了「自己投诉材料的副本」，这样我们可以在接待处一起核对日期。

examples.en: Could you send me a copy of my complaint before the manager calls me back tomorrow?
examples.zh: 经理明天回电话之前，您能把「我的投诉副本」发给我吗？

collocations: keep a copy of my complaint
ask for a copy of my complaint
bring a copy of my complaint

words.enDefinition: An amount that is reasonable for someone to receive or contribute

examples.en: Everyone should get a fair share of the table space for their display materials.
examples.zh: 每个人都应该「公平地分到一块」桌面来摆展示材料。

examples.en: I offered to do a fair share of the cleanup after the evening session.
examples.zh: 我主动提出在晚上那场结束后「承担自己该做的那份清理工作」。

collocations: do a fair share of the work
give everyone a fair share
a fair share of the space

words.enDefinition: a brief failure to think clearly or make a sound decision

examples.en: I called it a lapse in judgment after realising I had repeated a rumour.
examples.zh: 我发现自己转述了传言，承认那是「一时判断失误」。

examples.en: The chair said a lapse in judgment had led her to share the draft too early.
examples.zh: 主席说，自己「一时判断失误」，把草稿发得太早了。

collocations: admit a lapse in judgment
apologise for a lapse in judgment
a brief lapse in judgment

words.enDefinition: A short period when nobody is speaking during an exchange.

examples.en: I waited for a pause in the conversation before asking about the return time.
examples.zh: 我等到「对话出现停顿」，才问什么时间回来。

examples.en: There was a pause in the conversation while our friend opened the map again.
examples.zh: 朋友重新打开地图时，「对话出现了停顿」。

collocations: wait for a pause in the conversation
listen for a pause in the conversation
take advantage of a pause in the conversation

words.enDefinition: a brief, often private conversation requested before raising a matter

examples.en: Could I have a quick word before everyone starts putting the chairs away?
examples.zh: 大家开始收椅子之前，我能和你「简短地聊几句」吗？

examples.en: My roommate asked for a quick word while the others were still outside.
examples.zh: 其他人还在外面时，室友想和我「简短地聊几句」。

collocations: have a quick word
ask for a quick word
could we have a quick word

words.enDefinition: to signal that you recognise and are willing to receive someone's expression of regret

examples.en: You can accept an apology and still ask for time before working together again.
examples.zh: 你可以「接受道歉」，同时表示重新一起做事之前需要一段时间。

examples.en: I found it easier to accept an apology once we had discussed what happened openly.
examples.zh: 我们坦诚谈过事情的经过之后，我觉得更容易「接受道歉」。

collocations: choose to accept an apology
be ready to accept an apology
graciously accept an apology

words.enDefinition: To let someone know that their complaint has been received.

examples.en: The manager called to acknowledge a complaint that our group had submitted the previous afternoon.
examples.zh: 经理打来电话，「确认收到我们小组的投诉」，那是前一天下午提交的。

examples.en: A receptionist can acknowledge a complaint even if someone else will look into the matter.
examples.zh: 就算之后由其他人调查，接待员也可以先「确认收到投诉」。

collocations: acknowledge a complaint in writing
promptly acknowledge a complaint
fail to acknowledge a complaint

words.enDefinition: to openly recognise the effect that an action or decision had on other people

examples.en: The editor wanted to acknowledge the impact of the error on the students named.
examples.zh: 编辑想「承认造成的影响」，也就是那处错误怎样波及了被点名的学生。

examples.en: Before explaining my reasons, I tried to acknowledge the impact on the rest of the group.
examples.zh: 解释原因之前，我先试着「承认造成的影响」，包括给其他组员添的麻烦。

collocations: acknowledge the impact on others
fail to acknowledge the impact
openly acknowledge the impact

words.enDefinition: to recognise openly that someone acted wrongly, especially in an official or serious situation

examples.en: The committee voted to acknowledge wrongdoing in its response to the former volunteers that week.
examples.zh: 委员会投票决定，在当周给前志愿者的回应中「承认行为不当」。

examples.en: I thought the statement should acknowledge wrongdoing before it explained the new event rules.
examples.zh: 我认为那份声明应该先「承认行为不当」，再解释新活动规则。

collocations: publicly acknowledge wrongdoing
refuse to acknowledge wrongdoing
fail to acknowledge wrongdoing

words.enDefinition: to act honestly and sincerely, without trying to deceive or take unfair advantage

examples.en: Both organisers agreed to act in good faith while checking the facts about the booking.
examples.zh: 两名组织者同意，在核对预订的实际情况时「本着诚意行事」。

examples.en: I think she did act in good faith when she passed along the wrong date.
examples.zh: 虽然她传错了日期，但我认为她的确是「本着诚意行事」。

collocations: agree to act in good faith
believe both sides act in good faith
be expected to act in good faith

words.enDefinition: Information specific enough to help someone decide what to change or improve.

examples.en: Our group gave actionable feedback about where to put the signs for late arrivals.
examples.zh: 我们小组就迟到访客的指示牌该放在哪里，给出了「能据此改进的反馈」。

examples.en: The manager asked for actionable feedback because the first note simply said the visit was frustrating.
examples.zh: 第一张便条只说这次来访令人沮丧，所以经理希望收到「能据此改进的反馈」。

collocations: give actionable feedback
request actionable feedback
turn comments into actionable feedback

words.zhGloss: 行动比言语更有说服力
words.enDefinition: a proverb meaning that behaviour reveals commitment more clearly than promises do
acceptedZhAnswers: 行动比言语更有说服力

examples.en: Actions speak louder than words, so I waited to see whether he kept his promise.
examples.zh: 「行动比言语更有说服力」，所以我等着看他是否守诺。

examples.en: Our tutor reminded us that actions speak louder than words when a team is rebuilding trust.
examples.zh: 导师提醒我们，团队重新建立信任时，「行动比言语更有说服力」。

collocations: remember that actions speak louder than words
prove that actions speak louder than words
as they say, actions speak louder than words

words.zhGloss: 把这一点补充到我的投诉里
words.enDefinition: To ask that additional details are included with a complaint already made.
acceptedZhAnswers: 把这一点补充到我的投诉里

examples.en: Could you add this to my complaint about the entrance before the supervisor reads it?
examples.zh: 主管看之前，您能「把这一点补充到我的投诉里」吗？是关于入口的那次投诉。

examples.en: I called to add this to my complaint because I had found the original confirmation email.
examples.zh: 我找到了最早的确认邮件，所以打电话想「把这一点补充到我的投诉里」。

collocations: please add this to my complaint
ask someone to add this to my complaint
could you add this to my complaint

words.enDefinition: To give attention to a concern and respond to what the person needs or is worried about.

examples.en: The manager agreed to address a concern about the instructions given to visitors with appointments.
examples.zh: 经理同意「处理提出的问题」，具体涉及向预约访客提供的指引。

examples.en: A staff member came over to address a concern our group had raised about the entrance.
examples.zh: 一位工作人员过来「处理我们提出的问题」，这件事和入口有关。

collocations: address a concern about access
address a concern raised by visitors
take steps to address a concern

words.enDefinition: To deal with the underlying reason for a problem so that it is less likely to recur.

examples.en: The manager wanted to address the root cause of the booking mix-up before reopening the hall.
examples.zh: 经理想先「处理预订混乱的根本原因」，再开放大厅。

examples.en: The two teams met to address the root cause after noticing the same error three times.
examples.zh: 同样的错误出现三次后，两个团队开会「处理根本原因」。

collocations: take steps to address the root cause
look for ways to address the root cause
try to address the root cause

words.enDefinition: to acknowledge that something went wrong because of one's actions or omissions

examples.en: The organiser chose to admit fault after realising she had sent two conflicting dates.
examples.zh: 组织者发现自己发了两个互相矛盾的日期，决定「承认有过错」。

examples.en: I was ready to admit fault once we checked the records from both meetings.
examples.zh: 我们核对两次会议的记录后，我愿意「承认有过错」。

collocations: willing to admit fault
refuse to admit fault
choose to admit fault

words.enDefinition: Used to say you will wait until the other person completes what they are saying.

examples.en: I'll ask my question after you finish telling us what happened at the entrance.
examples.zh: 「等你讲完入口发生的事以后」，我再问问题。

examples.en: I can mention the bus times after you finish explaining where to meet everyone.
examples.zh: 「等你讲完大家该在哪里集合以后」，我再讲公交车时间。

collocations: ask after you finish
speak after you finish
check one thing after you finish

words.enDefinition: Accept the main idea without settling all the practical details

examples.en: We agree in principle to share the studio, but we haven't decided which evenings yet.
examples.zh: 我们「原则上同意」共用工作室，不过还没定在周几晚上。

examples.en: Can we agree in principle and settle the number of volunteers at the next meeting?
examples.zh: 我们能先「原则上同意」，下次开会再定志愿者人数吗？

collocations: agree in principle to a change
be prepared to agree in principle
agree in principle with the proposal

words.enDefinition: Reach shared understanding about the most important parts of a plan

examples.en: We need to agree on the essentials before anyone orders materials for the display.
examples.zh: 给展示订材料之前，我们得「先把关键事项谈妥」。

examples.en: Once we agree on the essentials, we'll let each team choose its own layout.
examples.zh: 「关键事项达成一致」后，各组就可以自行选布局。

collocations: agree on the essentials first
agree on the essentials before booking
fail to agree on the essentials

words.enDefinition: Used before saying the only part of a message you were able to hear.

examples.en: All I heard was the word Friday before the loudspeaker cut off in the hallway.
examples.zh: 走廊的扬声器没声以前，「我只听到了」星期五这个词。

examples.en: All I heard was the room number, so I still need to know the building.
examples.zh: 「我只听到了」房间号，所以还得知道是哪一栋楼。

collocations: all I heard was the start
all I heard was the word Tuesday
all I heard was the end

words.enDefinition: often light-heartedly says that a mistake has been forgiven and is no longer an issue

examples.en: All is forgiven, my friend said when I showed up with the missing snacks.
examples.zh: 我带着之前忘拿的零食出现时，朋友说：「过去的错就不计较了」。

examples.en: We both laughed when the organiser said all is forgiven and handed me the new schedule.
examples.zh: 组织者说「过去的错就不计较了」，把新时间表递给我，我们俩都笑了。

collocations: say all is forgiven
all is forgiven now
all is forgiven this time

words.enDefinition: Decide who will be responsible for particular tasks or outcomes

examples.en: We met to allocate responsibility for opening the room and collecting the keys afterwards.
examples.zh: 我们开会「划分责任」，确定谁来开门、最后谁收钥匙。

examples.en: We need to allocate responsibility before the other group hands us the equipment.
examples.zh: 另一组把设备交给我们之前，我们得先「划分责任」。

collocations: allocate responsibility for each task
allocate responsibility among team members
agree on how to allocate responsibility

words.enDefinition: Give each person or activity a reasonable portion of available time

examples.en: We can allocate time fairly by giving every speaker the same number of minutes.
examples.zh: 我们可以让每个人讲一样久，来「公平分配时间」。

examples.en: The teams met to allocate time fairly between rehearsal and setting up the stage.
examples.zh: 各组开会商量怎么在排练和布置舞台之间「公平分配时间」。

collocations: try to allocate time fairly
allocate time fairly among the speakers
agree on how to allocate time fairly

words.zhGloss: 我这样理解那句话对吗
words.enDefinition: A question checking whether your interpretation of written information is right.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我这样理解那句话对吗

examples.en: Am I reading that correctly on the sign about where to leave the spare chairs?
examples.zh: 牌子上说了备用椅子放哪儿，「我这样理解那句话对吗」？

examples.en: Am I reading that correctly, or does it mean the room only closes on weekends?
examples.zh: 「我这样理解那句话对吗」，还是它的意思是房间只在周末关闭？

collocations: am I reading that correctly on the sign
am I reading that correctly this time
ask am I reading that correctly

words.enDefinition: it is appropriate or necessary for someone to apologise

examples.en: I think an apology is in order after we left your name off the poster.
examples.zh: 海报漏印了你的名字，我觉得「应该道个歉」。

examples.en: The committee agreed that an apology is in order for the way volunteers were treated.
examples.zh: 委员会认为，那样对待志愿者，「应该道个歉」。

collocations: an apology is in order for the delay
perhaps an apology is in order
an apology is in order here

words.enDefinition: an error made without intending to deceive or harm anyone

examples.en: It was an honest mistake, but I still needed to correct the sign-up list.
examples.zh: 虽然是「无心之失」，我还是得把报名名单纠正过来。

examples.en: She called it an honest mistake after seeing the two event names looked similar.
examples.zh: 她发现两个活动名字很像，就说那是「无心之失」。

collocations: make an honest mistake
recognise an honest mistake
explain that it was an honest mistake

words.enDefinition: a polite way to acknowledge that you failed to notice or do something

examples.en: It was an oversight on my part to leave the last volunteer off the list.
examples.zh: 我漏掉了最后一位志愿者的名字，「是我疏忽了」。

examples.en: That was an oversight on my part, and I'll send you the corrected timetable today.
examples.zh: 「是我疏忽了」，今天我会把改好的时间表发给你。

collocations: it was an oversight on my part
acknowledge that it was an oversight on my part
explain that it was an oversight on my part

words.enDefinition: Comments or suggestions submitted without giving the person's name.

examples.en: I left anonymous feedback about the lack of signs between the station and the venue.
examples.zh: 从车站到场馆的路上缺少指示牌，我为此留了「匿名反馈」。

examples.en: The centre collected anonymous feedback from everyone who attended its first month of workshops.
examples.zh: 中心向首月参加工作坊的人收集了「匿名反馈」。

collocations: collect anonymous feedback
submit anonymous feedback
read anonymous feedback

words.enDefinition: an additional person needed to help with a practical task

examples.en: We needed another pair of hands to carry the boxes across the courtyard.
examples.zh: 我们需要「多一个人搭把手」，把箱子搬到院子另一头。

examples.en: Could we get another pair of hands before moving this big table downstairs?
examples.zh: 把大桌子搬下楼前，能不能找人来「多搭把手」？

collocations: need another pair of hands
get another pair of hands
ask for another pair of hands

words.enDefinition: introduces an informal request when availability is uncertain

examples.en: Any chance you could leave this by the door on your way out?
examples.zh: 「你能不能帮忙」出门时把这个放在门边？

examples.en: Any chance you could carry one of the bags to the common room?
examples.zh: 「方便帮忙把其中一个包拿到公共休息室吗」？

collocations: any chance you could help
any chance you could check
any chance you could bring it later

words.enDefinition: Invite people to voice opposition before the group proceeds

examples.en: Before I tell the rest of the club, any objections to that plan?
examples.zh: 我去告诉社团其他成员之前，先问一句「有人反对这个方案吗」？

examples.en: I can reserve the hall this afternoon, but first, any objections to that plan?
examples.zh: 我今天下午可以去订大厅，不过先问一下，「有人反对这个方案吗」？

collocations: any objections to that plan before we start
ask if there are any objections to that plan
have any objections to that plan

words.enDefinition: to tell a particular person that you are sorry for something you did

examples.en: I had to apologize to someone I had interrupted during our first committee meeting.
examples.zh: 第一次委员会会议上我打断了一个人，后来得「向那个人道歉」。

examples.en: How do you apologize to someone when you realise you called them by the wrong name?
examples.zh: 发现叫错了别人的名字时，你该怎么「向对方道歉」？

collocations: apologize to someone in person
apologize to someone privately
apologize to someone directly

words.enDefinition: a short direct response acknowledging that you accept what a person has said in apology

examples.en: Apology accepted, my teammate said after I returned the equipment to the correct cupboard.
examples.zh: 我把器材放回正确的柜子后，队友说：「我接受道歉」。

examples.en: She said apology accepted, and we agreed to talk about the schedule the next morning.
examples.zh: 她说「我接受道歉」，我们约好第二天早上再谈时间表。

collocations: apology accepted, thanks for explaining
apology accepted, let's leave it there
okay, apology accepted

words.enDefinition: a short written message expressing regret for something you did

examples.en: I left an apology note after forgetting to put the shared scissors back that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午我忘了把共用剪刀放回去，留了条「简短的道歉留言」。

examples.en: My roommate found the apology note beside the mug I had chipped the night before.
examples.zh: 室友在我前一晚碰掉一角的杯子旁找到了那条「简短的道歉留言」。

collocations: write an apology note
leave an apology note
receive an apology note

words.expression: are we all happy with that
words.lemma: are we all happy with that
words.enDefinition: Check whether everyone is comfortable accepting a proposed arrangement
acceptedEnVariants: are we all happy with that

examples.en: We could swap the two sessions, but are we all happy with that before I ask the speakers?
examples.zh: 我们可以把两场对调，不过在我去问发言人之前，先确认一下「大家都接受吗」？

examples.en: Before we tell the volunteers about the shorter shifts, are we all happy with that?
examples.zh: 告诉志愿者班次缩短之前，先问问「大家都接受吗」？

collocations: are we all happy with that date
are we all happy with that as a starting point
are we all happy with that so far

words.enDefinition: asks whether tension between two people has eased after a disagreement or apology

examples.en: After we discussed the missed rehearsal, I asked my partner, Are we okay now?
examples.zh: 我们谈过错过排练的事后，我问搭档：「我们现在和好了吗」？

examples.en: Are we okay now, or would you rather give it another day before we talk?
examples.zh: 「我们现在和好了吗」，还是你想再等一天才谈？

collocations: are we okay now after talking it through
are we okay now or do you need more time
are we okay now about what happened

words.enDefinition: Only if the preferred ways of handling something all fail

examples.en: We can use the corridor as a last resort if both meeting rooms are booked.
examples.zh: 如果两个会议室都被订了，我们「实在没办法才用」走廊。

examples.en: Let's keep the early slot as a last resort because half the team has labs.
examples.zh: 小组有一半人要上实验课，所以早一点的时段「只作为最后的办法」。

collocations: use something as a last resort
consider something as a last resort
keep something as a last resort

words.expression: as long as you put it back
words.lemma: as long as you put it back
words.enDefinition: allows something on the condition that the item is returned
acceptedEnVariants: as long as you put it back

examples.en: You can use my ruler as long as you put it back before we go to lunch.
examples.zh: 你可以用我的尺子，「只要你午饭前放回去」就行。

examples.en: Take the spare chair as long as you put it back when the session is over.
examples.zh: 可以拿备用椅子，「只要你用完放回去」，活动结束就还原。

collocations: use it as long as you put it back
take it as long as you put it back
agree as long as you put it back

words.enDefinition: to get someone's permission before you start using the item

examples.en: Please ask before using it if you're not sure whose charger it is.
examples.zh: 如果不确定充电器是谁的，请「用之前先问一声」。

examples.en: The tape belongs to my roommate, so ask before using it this time.
examples.zh: 胶带是我室友的，所以这次「用之前先问一声」。

collocations: remember to ask before using it
need to ask before using it
please ask before using it

words.enDefinition: To ask for a decision or response to be checked again after the first review.

examples.en: We decided to ask for a second review because the first response missed our main point.
examples.zh: 第一次答复漏掉了我们最关心的问题，所以我们决定「请求再次复核」。

examples.en: Could I ask for a second review if the booking confirmation shows a different date?
examples.zh: 如果预约确认单上是另一个日期，我能「请求再次复核」吗？

collocations: choose to ask for a second review
ask for a second review of the decision
wish to ask for a second review

words.enDefinition: to tell someone that you would like them to apologise for what happened

examples.en: I decided to ask for an apology after a joke misrepresented what I had said.
examples.zh: 有人开玩笑时曲解了我的话，我决定「要求对方道歉」。

examples.en: The chair explained that students may ask for an apology without making a formal complaint.
examples.zh: 主席解释，学生可以「要求对方道歉」，无需提出正式投诉。

collocations: decide to ask for an apology
ask for an apology in private
ask for an apology from the organiser

words.enDefinition: to ask someone not to keep feeling anger or blame for something wrong you did

examples.en: I wanted to ask for forgiveness after repeating something my friend had told me privately.
examples.zh: 我把朋友私下告诉我的事说了出去，想「请求原谅」。

examples.en: He chose to ask for forgiveness once the other volunteers had heard his full explanation.
examples.zh: 其他志愿者听完他的解释后，他选择「请求原谅」。

collocations: choose to ask for forgiveness
ask for forgiveness directly
be ready to ask for forgiveness

words.enDefinition: to seek information or approval from whoever is responsible locally

examples.en: We decided to ask the person in charge before setting our display outside the room.
examples.zh: 把展板摆到屋外前，我们决定「问一下负责人」。

examples.en: You can ask the person in charge about using the empty chairs next door.
examples.zh: 关于能不能用隔壁的空椅子，你可以「问一下负责人」。

collocations: remember to ask the person in charge
decide to ask the person in charge
ask the person in charge first

words.expression: asking again won't change my answer
words.lemma: asking again won't change my answer
words.enDefinition: a way to make clear that repeated requests will not change your decision
acceptedEnVariants: asking again won't change my answer

examples.en: “Asking again won't change my answer,” I said when my classmate brought up the survey again.
examples.zh: 同学又提起那份问卷时，我说：“「再问我也不会改口」。”

examples.en: When Ben repeated the invitation that evening, I told him, “Asking again won't change my answer.”
examples.zh: 本当晚又邀了一次，我跟他说：“「再问我也不会改口」。”

collocations: just so we're clear, asking again won't change my answer
asking again won't change my answer about the trip
asking again tomorrow won't change my answer

words.enDefinition: responsible for an error, problem or harmful result

examples.en: We looked at both messages before deciding who was at fault for the confusion.
examples.zh: 我们查看了两条消息，才判断谁对这场混乱「负有过错」。

examples.en: I knew I was at fault when I saw the outdated timetable in my email.
examples.zh: 看到邮件里那份过时的时间表，我知道自己「负有过错」。

collocations: be partly at fault
find someone at fault
decide who is at fault

words.enDefinition: Available again for consideration after being set aside or rejected

examples.en: Moving the stall outdoors is back on the table now that we've found a sheltered spot.
examples.zh: 我们找到了有遮挡的地方，现在「又可以考虑」把摊位搬到室外了。

examples.en: The early session was suddenly back on the table when two people changed their shifts.
examples.zh: 两个人换了班，于是早一点的活动场次突然又「可以考虑了」。

collocations: put an option back on the table
now back on the table
an idea is back on the table

words.enDefinition: to push someone into a position where they feel they have no acceptable choice

examples.en: We discussed how repeated requests can back someone into a corner during a group meeting.
examples.zh: 我们聊到在小组会上反复提出要求会怎样「逼得某人没有选择」。

examples.en: A public vote can back someone into a corner if everyone expects them to agree.
examples.zh: 如果大家都等着某人同意，公开投票可能会「逼得那个人没有选择」。

collocations: don't back someone into a corner
back someone into a corner with an ultimatum
back someone into a corner by asking in public

words.enDefinition: Support the suggested plan during a discussion or decision

examples.en: Our team will back the proposal if there's a quiet room for recording interviews.
examples.zh: 如果有间安静的房间可以录采访，我们小组就会「支持这个提议」。

examples.en: Will both groups back the proposal if we leave the stage setup as it is?
examples.zh: 如果舞台布置维持原样，两个小组都会「支持这个提议」吗？

collocations: agree to back the proposal
refuse to back the proposal
ask both teams to back the proposal

words.enDefinition: lasting hostility or bitterness between people who have had a disagreement

examples.en: There was still bad blood between the two groups when they shared the rehearsal hall.
examples.zh: 两个小组共用排练厅时，彼此之间仍有「旧怨」。

examples.en: We wanted to resolve the booking issue before it created bad blood among the volunteers.
examples.zh: 我们想处理好预约问题，免得志愿者之间结下「怨隙」。

collocations: there is bad blood between them
create bad blood
leave bad blood

words.enDefinition: Used to mark that you want to say or check something before the speaker continues.

examples.en: Before you go on, can you tell me how far that stop is from campus?
examples.zh: 「在你接着说之前」，你能先告诉我那个站离校园多远吗？

examples.en: Before you go on to the next step, I'll make sure my tablet is ready.
examples.zh: 「在你接着讲下一步之前」，我先确认我的平板准备好了。

collocations: before you go on, can I check
before you go on, let me ask
before you go on to the next step

words.enDefinition: an apology offered later than expected or after a long delay

examples.en: His belated apology arrived two weeks after the group had finished working together on the report.
examples.zh: 我们小组合作完成报告两周后，才收到他「迟来的道歉」。

examples.en: I appreciated the belated apology, although it came months after the comments in class.
examples.zh: 虽然那些课堂评论已经过去几个月，我还是感谢这份「迟来的道歉」。

collocations: offer a belated apology
receive a belated apology
a belated apology for the remark

words.enDefinition: Combine parts of two proposals into a single plan

examples.en: Could we blend the two ideas by keeping the short talk and adding a group activity?
examples.zh: 我们能把「两种想法结合一下」，保留短讲，再加个小组活动吗？

examples.en: We tried to blend the two ideas without asking either group to change its presentation date.
examples.zh: 我们试着「融合两种想法」，同时不让任何一组改展示日期。

collocations: try to blend the two ideas
find a way to blend the two ideas
see if we can blend the two ideas

words.zhGloss: 没有按预约时间提供服务
words.enDefinition: Used to say an organisation failed to keep the appointment time it had agreed to.
acceptedZhAnswers: 没有按预约时间提供服务

examples.en: Our booked time was not honoured, so some of us had to leave before the tour began.
examples.zh: 对方「没有按预约时间提供服务」，我们中有人不得不在导览开始前离开。

examples.en: The manager asked which desk we approached after our booked time was not honoured that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午对方「没有按预约时间提供服务」，经理问我们之后去了哪个服务台。

collocations: explain why the booked time was not honoured
report that the booked time was not honoured
ask why the booked time was not honoured

words.enDefinition: to fail to do what you had definitely said you would do

examples.en: I did not want to break a promise to help her move during the weekend.
examples.zh: 我答应周末帮她搬家，我不想「不守承诺」。

examples.en: It feels worse to break a promise when other people have planned around your help.
examples.zh: 别人已经按你会来帮忙做好计划时，「不守承诺」会更让人难受。

collocations: break a promise to someone
admit you broke a promise
apologise for breaking a promise

words.expression: bring an issue to your attention
words.lemma: bring an issue to your attention
words.enDefinition: To tell someone about a problem they may need to know about or address.
acceptedEnVariants: bring an issue to your attention

examples.en: I'd like to bring an issue to your attention about yesterday's workshop registration process.
examples.zh: 我想「向您反映一个问题」，是关于昨天工作坊报名流程的。

examples.en: Before the next class, I need to bring an issue to your attention concerning the shared laptops.
examples.zh: 下次上课前，我需要「向您反映一个问题」，和共用的笔记本电脑有关。

collocations: bring an issue to your attention privately
bring an issue to your attention today
need to bring an issue to your attention

words.enDefinition: asks someone to return an item immediately after using it

examples.en: You can use the tape, but please bring it straight back after class.
examples.zh: 胶带可以用，但下课后请「用完马上拿回来」。

examples.en: Just bring it straight back when you're done checking the names on it.
examples.zh: 核对上面的名字之后，「用完马上拿回来」。

collocations: remember to bring it straight back
please bring it straight back
ask someone to bring it straight back

words.enDefinition: To react to a complaint as if it were unimportant and needs no serious attention.

examples.en: The manager seemed to brush off a complaint about the broken lockers at the pool.
examples.zh: 对于泳池储物柜损坏的事，经理好像就是在「对投诉敷衍了事」。

examples.en: Staff training includes examples of how people can brush off a complaint without meaning to.
examples.zh: 员工培训会举例说明，人有时如何无意间「对投诉敷衍了事」。

collocations: try to brush off a complaint
appear to brush off a complaint
brush off a complaint as a minor issue

words.enDefinition: Design a plan so participants can change it when necessary

examples.en: We could build in some flexibility by offering the volunteers two setup times each week.
examples.zh: 我们可以每周给志愿者两个布置时段可选，「留一点调整余地」。

examples.en: Let's build in some flexibility so teammates can swap roles before the event starts.
examples.zh: 我们「留一点调整余地」吧，这样队员能在活动开始前互换分工。

collocations: build in some flexibility at the start
build in some flexibility around deadlines
build in some flexibility for late arrivals

words.expression: build our plan around the deadline
words.lemma: build our plan around the deadline
words.enDefinition: Make the completion date the main reference point for planning work
acceptedEnVariants: build our plan around the deadline

examples.en: Let's build our plan around the deadline by setting aside Tuesday for a first review.
examples.zh: 我们把周二留出来做第一轮检查，「按截止时间来安排计划」。

examples.en: We can build our plan around the deadline once we know when the finished files are due.
examples.zh: 等知道最终文件什么时候要交，就能「围绕截止时间安排计划」。

collocations: help us build our plan around the deadline
need to build our plan around the deadline
build our plan around the deadline on Monday

words.expression: can I borrow it until tomorrow
words.lemma: can i borrow it until tomorrow
words.enDefinition: asks permission to keep something borrowed until the next day
acceptedEnVariants: can I borrow it until tomorrow

examples.en: Can I borrow it until tomorrow? The library won't open before my early class starts.
examples.zh: 「能借我用到明天吗」？明天早课开始前图书馆不开门。

examples.en: Can I borrow it until tomorrow if you're not planning to use it again tonight?
examples.zh: 如果你今晚没打算再用，「能借我用到明天吗」？

collocations: can I borrow it until tomorrow morning
can I borrow it until tomorrow afternoon
ask if I can borrow it until tomorrow

words.expression: can I change it a little
words.lemma: can i change it a little
words.enDefinition: asks whether making a small change is acceptable
acceptedEnVariants: can I change it a little

examples.en: Can I change it a little before everyone sees where we put the two labels?
examples.zh: 大家看到这两张标签的位置之前，「我能稍微改一下吗」？

examples.en: Can I change it a little? A darker colour would be easier to see from here.
examples.zh: 「我能稍微改一下吗」？从这儿看，深一点的颜色更清楚。

collocations: can I change it a little first
can I change it a little before we show them
ask if I can change it a little

words.expression: can I jump in for a second
words.lemma: can i jump in for a second
words.enDefinition: A casual request to take a short turn in a conversation already in progress.
acceptedEnVariants: can I jump in for a second

examples.en: Can I jump in for a second before we decide where to meet tomorrow?
examples.zh: 决定明天见面地点前，「我能插一句吗」？

examples.en: Can I jump in for a second because I think we've got two different room numbers?
examples.zh: 我觉得我们记的是两个不同的房间号，「我能插一句吗」？

collocations: can I jump in for a second about that date
can I jump in for a second here
can I jump in for a second before we move on

words.expression: can I keep the spare one
words.lemma: can i keep the spare one
words.zhGloss: 多出来的那个我能留着吗
words.enDefinition: asks whether you can keep an extra item permanently
acceptedZhAnswers: 多出来的那个我能留着吗
acceptedEnVariants: can I keep the spare one

examples.en: Can I keep the spare one? It would fit the frame I have at home.
examples.zh: 「多出来的那个我能留着吗」？它正好能配我家里的相框。

examples.en: Can I keep the spare one when everyone else has taken one for their folders?
examples.zh: 其他人都拿了一个放进文件夹后，「多出来的那个我能留着吗」？

collocations: can I keep the spare one for myself
can I keep the spare one after class
ask if I can keep the spare one

words.expression: can I leave this with you
words.lemma: can i leave this with you
words.enDefinition: asks someone to keep an item for you temporarily
acceptedEnVariants: can I leave this with you

examples.en: Can I leave this with you while I carry the rest of the bags upstairs?
examples.zh: 我把剩下的包拿上楼时，「这个能先放你这儿吗」？

examples.en: Can I leave this with you until I've found the person who asked me to bring it?
examples.zh: 等我找到请我带它过来的人之前，「这个能先放你这儿吗」？

collocations: can I leave this with you for now
can I leave this with you until later
ask if I can leave this with you

words.expression: can I lend it to someone else
words.lemma: can i lend it to someone else
words.enDefinition: asks permission to let another person use something you borrowed
acceptedEnVariants: can I lend it to someone else

examples.en: Can I lend it to someone else if my roommate needs it for the same poster?
examples.zh: 如果室友做同一张海报也需要用，「我能再转借给别人吗」？

examples.en: Can I lend it to someone else, or should I bring it straight back to you?
examples.zh: 「我能再转借给别人吗」？还是该马上还给你？

collocations: can I lend it to someone else in our group
can I lend it to someone else after class
ask if I can lend it to someone else

words.expression: can I make a copy of this
words.lemma: can i make a copy of this
words.enDefinition: asks permission to reproduce a copy of a document or page
acceptedEnVariants: can I make a copy of this

examples.en: Can I make a copy of this to put on the noticeboard outside our common room?
examples.zh: 我想在公共休息室外的布告栏贴一份，「我能复印一份吗」？

examples.en: Can I make a copy of this before I give the original back to you tomorrow?
examples.zh: 明天把原件还你之前，「我能复印一份吗」？

collocations: can I make a copy of this page
can I make a copy of this for myself
ask if I can make a copy of this

words.zhGloss: 这把椅子我能挪一下吗
words.enDefinition: asks whether moving a chair is acceptable to others
acceptedZhAnswers: 这把椅子我能挪一下吗

examples.en: Can I move this chair closer to the table so I can see the map?
examples.zh: 「这把椅子我能往桌边挪一下吗」？我想看地图。

examples.en: Can I move this chair for a minute while my friend clears the space?
examples.zh: 朋友在腾地方，「这把椅子我能先挪一下吗」？

collocations: can I move this chair over here
can I move this chair out of the way
ask if I can move this chair

words.enDefinition: asks whether you may connect a device to an outlet nearby

examples.en: Can I plug in here while I finish the last two pages on my laptop?
examples.zh: 我还要用笔记本电脑看完最后两页，「能用这里的插座吗」？

examples.en: Can I plug in here? That outlet is closer to my side of the table.
examples.zh: 「我能用这里的插座吗」？那个插座离我这边更近。

collocations: ask if I can plug in here
can I plug in here for a while
can I plug in here next to you

words.expression: can I show it to the others
words.lemma: can i show it to the others
words.enDefinition: asks permission to let additional people see something you received
acceptedEnVariants: can I show it to the others

examples.en: Can I show it to the others before you decide which sketch you want to use?
examples.zh: 在你选定想用哪张草图之前，「我能给其他人看看吗」？

examples.en: Can I show it to the others? Your example might help them understand how the pieces fit.
examples.zh: 「我能给其他人看看吗」？你的例子能帮他们理解零件怎么拼装。

collocations: can I show it to the others later
can I show it to the others in class
ask if I can show it to the others

words.expression: can I take a quick look
words.lemma: can i take a quick look
words.enDefinition: asks someone to let you look at something briefly
acceptedEnVariants: can I take a quick look

examples.en: Can I take a quick look at the sketch before you put it back in your folder?
examples.zh: 你把草图放回文件夹之前，「我能看一眼吗」？

examples.en: Can I take a quick look so I can check how the pieces fit together?
examples.zh: 「我能看一眼吗」？我想确认这些零件怎么拼在一起。

collocations: can I take a quick look at that
can I take a quick look inside
ask if I can take a quick look

words.expression: can I take a second one
words.lemma: can i take a second one
words.enDefinition: asks permission to take one more item of the same kind
acceptedEnVariants: can I take a second one

examples.en: Can I take a second one for the student who is still fetching her bag?
examples.zh: 给那位还在拿包的同学，「我能再拿一个吗」？

examples.en: Can I take a second one? My first badge got soaked on the walk over.
examples.zh: 「我能再拿一个吗」？第一枚徽章在路上淋湿了。

collocations: can I take a second one for my roommate
can I take a second one later
ask if I can take a second one

words.expression: can I take it from here
words.lemma: can i take it from here
words.enDefinition: A request to take over an explanation or task at its current point.
acceptedEnVariants: can I take it from here

examples.en: Can I take it from here now that you've reached the part about the map?
examples.zh: 你已经讲到地图那部分了，「接下来能换我来说吗」？

examples.en: Can I take it from here and explain how the second group should come in?
examples.zh: 「接下来能换我来说吗」？我来解释第二组该怎么进来。

collocations: can I take it from here with the map
can I take it from here for a moment
ask can I take it from here

words.zhGloss: 我能把这个带到外面吗
words.enDefinition: asks permission to move something from indoors to outdoors
acceptedZhAnswers: 我能把这个带到外面吗

examples.en: Can I take this outside to get a better look at the colour in daylight?
examples.zh: 「我能把这个带到外面吗」？想在日光下看清颜色。

examples.en: Can I take this outside while we wait for the room to be free again?
examples.zh: 等房间重新空出来时，「我能把这个带到外面吗」？

collocations: can I take this outside for a minute
can I take this outside with me
ask if I can take this outside

words.expression: can I use your side of the table
words.lemma: can i use your side of the table
words.zhGloss: 我能用你那边的桌面吗
words.enDefinition: asks to work on the part of a table someone occupies
acceptedZhAnswers: 我能用你那边的桌面吗
acceptedEnVariants: can I use your side of the table

examples.en: Can I use your side of the table while you put those books back on the shelf?
examples.zh: 你把那些书放回书架的时候，「我能用你那边的桌面吗」？

examples.en: Can I use your side of the table? There's more room there for the map than here.
examples.zh: 「我能用你那边的桌面吗」？那边比这边更有地方摊地图。

collocations: can I use your side of the table for a second
can I use your side of the table while you pack
ask if I can use your side of the table

words.zhGloss: 我们能换个安静一点的地方吗
words.enDefinition: A request to continue a conversation somewhere with less noise so people can hear.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们能换个安静一点的地方吗

examples.en: Can we move somewhere quieter so I can hear the instructions for tomorrow morning?
examples.zh: 「我们能换个安静一点的地方吗」？我想听清明天上午的安排。

examples.en: Can we move somewhere quieter to talk where the sound of the fan won't distract us?
examples.zh: 「我们能换个安静一点的地方吗」？免得说话时一直被风扇声打扰。

collocations: can we move somewhere quieter to talk
can we move somewhere quieter for this call
ask can we move somewhere quieter

words.expression: can you give me a bit more room
words.lemma: can you give me a bit more room
words.enDefinition: asks another person to make slightly more space for you
acceptedEnVariants: can you give me a bit more room

examples.en: Can you give me a bit more room so I can spread my notes across the table?
examples.zh: 我想把笔记在桌上摊开，「能给我多留点地方吗」？

examples.en: Can you give me a bit more room while I turn this chair to face the window?
examples.zh: 我把椅子转向窗户时，「能给我多留点地方吗」？

collocations: can you give me a bit more room here
can you give me a bit more room please
ask if you can give me a bit more room

words.enDefinition: A request to reduce the possible meanings, times, places, or other choices to a smaller set.

examples.en: Can you narrow it down to a day so I know when to be home?
examples.zh: 「你能缩小到具体哪一天吗」？这样我就知道什么时候要在家。

examples.en: Can you narrow it down a little so we know which building to look in?
examples.zh: 「你能把范围缩小一点吗」？这样我们就知道到哪栋楼去找。

collocations: can you narrow it down to a day
can you narrow it down to two choices
can you narrow it down a little

words.expression: can you show me the word
words.lemma: can you show me the word
words.zhGloss: 你能给我看看那个词吗
words.enDefinition: A request to see a word written down so you can identify or understand it.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你能给我看看那个词吗
acceptedEnVariants: can you show me the word

examples.en: Can you show me the word on your screen so I know which spelling you mean?
examples.zh: 「你能给我看看屏幕上的那个词吗」？我想知道你说的是哪种拼法。

examples.en: Can you show me the word in the guide before we start looking for the sign?
examples.zh: 开始找牌子前，「你能给我看看指南里的那个词吗」？

collocations: can you show me the word in the guide
can you show me the word on your screen
can you show me the word on the label

words.expression: can you show me where it goes
words.lemma: can you show me where it goes
words.enDefinition: asks someone to indicate the proper place for something
acceptedEnVariants: can you show me where it goes

examples.en: Can you show me where it goes before I move the box out of the way?
examples.zh: 我把箱子挪开之前，「能指给我该放哪儿吗」？

examples.en: Can you show me where it goes? I don't want to put it with the wrong supplies.
examples.zh: 「能指给我该放哪儿吗」？我不想放到别的用品堆里。

collocations: can you show me where it goes before you leave
can you show me where it goes first
ask if you can show me where it goes

words.expression: can you take a bit of the weight
words.lemma: can you take a bit of the weight
words.zhGloss: 能帮我分担一点重量吗
words.enDefinition: asks someone to support part of a load you are carrying
acceptedZhAnswers: 能帮我分担一点重量吗
acceptedEnVariants: can you take a bit of the weight

examples.en: Can you take a bit of the weight while I put the board down on the bench?
examples.zh: 我把板子放到长凳上时，「能帮我分担一点重量吗」？

examples.en: Can you take a bit of the weight? I'll hold the side with the loose handle myself.
examples.zh: 「能帮我分担一点重量吗」？把手松了的那边我拿着。

collocations: can you take a bit of the weight please
ask if you can take a bit of the weight
can you take a bit of the weight here

words.enDefinition: The largest number of people a space can hold at once

examples.en: The capacity limit for the studio means we can't run both groups together.
examples.zh: 这个工作室的「人数上限」意味着我们不能让两组同时进去。

examples.en: Let's check the capacity limit before offering any of the spare tickets to friends.
examples.zh: 把多余的票送给朋友之前，我们先看一下「人数上限」。

collocations: check the capacity limit
a capacity limit of fifty people
stay within the capacity limit

words.enDefinition: Approve a formal proposal by receiving enough support in a vote

examples.en: The students needed one more vote to carry the motion at the club meeting.
examples.zh: 社团会议上，同学们还差一票才能「通过动议」。

examples.en: We managed to carry the motion after both teams agreed on how to share equipment.
examples.zh: 两个小组就设备怎么共用达成一致后，我们成功「通过了动议」。

collocations: enough votes to carry the motion
carry the motion by a narrow margin
fail to carry the motion

words.enDefinition: to make people feel insulted, disrespected or upset

examples.en: I did not expect that remark to cause offence during such an informal conversation.
examples.zh: 我没想到那句话在这么随意的聊天中也会「冒犯别人」。

examples.en: The editor removed a joke that might cause offence to some readers of the paper.
examples.zh: 编辑删掉了一个可能「冒犯部分读者」的玩笑。

collocations: cause offence to someone
not intend to cause offence
words that may cause offence

words.enDefinition: In British English, to contact an organisation again to ask what it has done about a complaint.

examples.en: I had to chase up a complaint when our next appointment was only two days away.
examples.zh: 离下次预约只剩两天，我只得「催问投诉进展」。

examples.en: The adviser offered to chase up a complaint our group had made about the booking desk.
examples.zh: 顾问提出帮我们「催问投诉进展」，我们小组投诉的是预订服务台。

collocations: ring to chase up a complaint
need to chase up a complaint
chase up a complaint with reception

words.enDefinition: requires the other person to consult you before acting

examples.en: You can use the room later, but check with me first before you start.
examples.zh: 那间屋子待会儿可以用，不过开始前「先跟我确认一下」。

examples.en: Please check with me first if you plan to give the spare copy away.
examples.zh: 如果打算把多印的那份送人，请「先跟我确认一下」。

collocations: remember to check with me first
please check with me first
ask students to check with me first

words.enDefinition: to get agreement from the person who owns an item

examples.en: We should check with the owner first before moving the bicycle across the yard.
examples.zh: 把自行车搬到院子另一边之前，应该「先问问物主」。

examples.en: Could you check with the owner first before we use the spare folding table?
examples.zh: 用备用折叠桌之前，你能「先问问物主」吗？

collocations: remember to check with the owner first
need to check with the owner first
please check with the owner first

words.enDefinition: To mark a complaint as no longer active in an organisation's records.

examples.en: The centre asked its manager to close a complaint once the visitor received a written response.
examples.zh: 访客收到书面答复后，中心请经理「结束投诉处理」。

examples.en: I asked whether they could close a complaint while the revised booking was still unconfirmed.
examples.zh: 预约变更还没得到确认，我问这种情况下能不能「结束投诉处理」。

collocations: decide to close a complaint
close a complaint after responding
ask when staff can close a complaint

words.enDefinition: Bring a discussion to an end after people have spoken

examples.en: We can close the discussion if nobody has anything else to add about the rota.
examples.zh: 要是没人想补充关于轮班表的意见，我们就可以「结束这场讨论」。

examples.en: Before we close the discussion, let's check that the recording team has seen the plan.
examples.zh: 「结束讨论」前，我们先确认录制小组看过方案了。

collocations: agree to close the discussion
move to close the discussion
close the discussion on that item

words.enDefinition: asks someone to collect an item as they are leaving

examples.en: Could you collect it when you go past the welcome desk on Tuesday afternoon?
examples.zh: 周二下午你经过迎新服务台时，能「走的时候顺便领一下」吗？

examples.en: Please collect it when you go down to the room where we left the bags.
examples.zh: 下楼去放包的房间时，请「走的时候顺便领一下」。

collocations: could you collect it when you go
remember to collect it when you go
ask someone to collect it when you go

words.enDefinition: to admit the truth about something that you had been keeping secret

examples.en: I decided to come clean about why the volunteer certificates had not been printed yet.
examples.zh: 我决定「把隐瞒的实情说出来」，解释志愿者证书为什么还没印。

examples.en: Our talk made it easier for me to come clean about deleting the original schedule.
examples.zh: 谈过之后，我比较能「把隐瞒的实情说出来」，承认是我删了原时间表。

collocations: come clean about a mistake
decide to come clean
come clean to someone

words.enDefinition: to make a firm promise to improve one's future behaviour or performance

examples.en: I wanted to commit to doing better by including new volunteers in our planning discussions.
examples.zh: 我想「承诺今后改进」，让新志愿者也能参与我们的筹备讨论。

examples.en: The team decided to commit to doing better instead of treating the complaint as resolved.
examples.zh: 团队决定「承诺今后改进」，不把收到投诉就算作问题解决。

collocations: choose to commit to doing better
publicly commit to doing better
be ready to commit to doing better

words.enDefinition: Agree to carry out a proposed arrangement and follow through

examples.en: Before we tell the volunteers, can both team leaders commit to the plan for Saturday?
examples.zh: 在通知志愿者之前，两位组长能「承诺按周六的计划来」吗？

examples.en: Rita said she'd commit to the plan if the later group had enough chairs.
examples.zh: 丽塔说，如果晚一点的组有够用的椅子，她就「承诺按计划来」。

collocations: be ready to commit to the plan
ask everyone to commit to the plan
wait before you commit to the plan

words.enDefinition: Compare choices using equivalent features or conditions for a fair judgment

examples.en: Let's compare like with like and count the setup time for both room choices.
examples.zh: 我们把两个房间方案的布置时间都算进去，「按同样的条件来比较」。

examples.en: It's easier to compare like with like when each team starts with the same budget.
examples.zh: 各组起始预算一样，就更容易「按同样的条件比较」。

collocations: make sure we compare like with like
try to compare like with like
compare like with like across the two plans

words.enDefinition: To express dissatisfaction with the way a service was provided.

examples.en: I decided to complain about the service after being sent to three different desks.
examples.zh: 我被指去三个不同的服务台后，决定「对服务提出投诉」。

examples.en: We were reluctant to complain about the service because the volunteers had tried to help.
examples.zh: 志愿者已经尽力帮忙，我们不太愿意「对服务提出投诉」。

collocations: call to complain about the service
write to complain about the service
decide to complain about the service

words.enDefinition: A form for providing details about a problem that you want an organisation to address.

examples.en: The receptionist gave me a complaint form after I described what happened during our visit.
examples.zh: 我说了我们来访时发生的事，接待员随后给了我一张「投诉表」。

examples.en: I used the complaint form to explain why our group had missed the last shuttle.
examples.zh: 我在「投诉表」上说明了小组错过末班接驳车的原因。

collocations: fill in a complaint form
submit a complaint form
ask for a complaint form

words.enDefinition: The way an organisation receives, investigates, and responds to complaints.

examples.en: The manager said complaint handling would be covered at the next volunteer training session.
examples.zh: 经理说，下次志愿者培训会讲「投诉处理」。

examples.en: I commented on complaint handling because two people gave me different answers about what happened next.
examples.zh: 两个人对下一步流程的说法不同，所以我对「投诉处理」提了意见。

collocations: review complaint handling
improve complaint handling
staff training in complaint handling

words.enDefinition: A record used to list complaints and keep basic details about them.

examples.en: The receptionist checked the complaint log to see when our group first called the venue.
examples.zh: 接待员查了「投诉登记簿」，看看我们小组第一次是什么时候给场馆打的电话。

examples.en: The complaint log showed that several visitors had reported the same problem with the entrance.
examples.zh: 「投诉登记簿」显示，几位访客都反映过入口的同一个问题。

collocations: maintain a complaint log
check the complaint log
enter details in the complaint log

words.enDefinition: an outcome indicating that a review found insufficient grounds to support the complaint

examples.en: The letter said “Complaint not upheld” because the booking records did not support our claim.
examples.zh: 信上写着「投诉不成立」，因为预约记录无法支持我们的说法。

examples.en: I asked the centre to explain why the final decision said “Complaint not upheld”.
examples.zh: 我请中心解释为什么最终决定是「投诉不成立」。

collocations: an outcome marked complaint not upheld
a notice labelled complaint not upheld
see complaint not upheld on the decision

words.enDefinition: A status saying a complaint is on record and a final response has yet to be made.

examples.en: The booking page still showed “Complaint pending” after I uploaded the notes from our meeting.
examples.zh: 我上传会议笔记后，预订页面仍显示「投诉仍待处理」。

examples.en: The “Complaint pending” label stayed on the page until the centre sent its final response.
examples.zh: 中心发出最终答复之前，页面上一直显示「投诉仍待处理」。

collocations: status shows complaint pending
the complaint pending label
a notice marked complaint pending

words.enDefinition: A status or confirmation saying that a complaint has reached the organisation responsible for it.

examples.en: I saw “Complaint received” beside the message I had sent about our visit last week.
examples.zh: 我看到关于上周来访的问题的留言旁显示着「投诉已收悉」。

examples.en: The “Complaint received” notice included the date we had submitted the form at the centre.
examples.zh: 「投诉已收悉」的通知写明了我们是哪天在中心提交表格的。

collocations: a complaint received notice
a message marked complaint received
status shows complaint received

words.enDefinition: A number assigned to a complaint to help people find it again or check its progress.

examples.en: I wrote down the complaint reference number so I could ask about it again on Friday.
examples.zh: 我记下了「投诉查询编号」，好在周五再问问处理进度。

examples.en: The adviser used my complaint reference number to find the details of our conversation last week.
examples.zh: 顾问用我的「投诉查询编号」找到了我们上周谈话的详细记录。

collocations: give a complaint reference number
quote your complaint reference number
check the complaint reference number

words.enDefinition: an outcome indicating that a review found grounds to support the complaint

examples.en: The centre's letter was marked “Complaint upheld” and explained why the entry arrangements had been incorrect.
examples.zh: 中心的信写着「投诉成立」，并说明了入场安排为什么有误。

examples.en: I read “Complaint upheld” on the notice before looking for what the manager would change.
examples.zh: 我先在通知上读到了「投诉成立」，再找经理会改哪些地方。

collocations: an outcome marked complaint upheld
a decision labelled complaint upheld
see complaint upheld in a response

words.enDefinition: The department of an organisation responsible for handling complaints from people who use its services.

examples.en: The complaints department called me after I wrote about our experience at the venue.
examples.zh: 我写信反映我们在场馆的经历后，「投诉处理部门」给我打了电话。

examples.en: We asked the complaints department to explain which office had checked the visitor records.
examples.zh: 我们请「投诉处理部门」说明是哪个办公室核查了访客记录。

collocations: contact the complaints department
refer an issue to the complaints department
hear back from the complaints department

words.enDefinition: A person appointed to receive, investigate, or respond to complaints for an organisation.

examples.en: The complaints officer asked what the receptionist had said when we showed our passes.
examples.zh: 「投诉处理专员」问，我们出示通行证时接待员说了什么。

examples.en: I spoke to a complaints officer about the change to our tour's access arrangements.
examples.zh: 我就导览参观的入场安排变更一事，和一位「投诉处理专员」谈了谈。

collocations: contact a complaints officer
speak with the complaints officer
meet the complaints officer

words.enDefinition: An organisation's published rules about whose complaints it accepts and how it handles them.

examples.en: I checked the complaints policy to see whether someone could speak on our group's behalf.
examples.zh: 我查了「投诉处理规定」，看看能不能由一人代表我们小组说明情况。

examples.en: The manager pointed me to the complaints policy when I asked how the review worked.
examples.zh: 我问复核是怎么进行的，经理把「投诉处理规定」指给我看。

collocations: check the complaints policy
publish a complaints policy
review the complaints policy

words.enDefinition: a statement of apology that depends on whether an event happened or someone was harmed

examples.en: The mediator asked how a conditional apology could leave the other person feeling unheard.
examples.zh: 调解员问，「附带条件的道歉」为什么会让对方觉得自己的感受没被听见。

examples.en: The editor's conditional apology left open whether the article had caused any actual harm.
examples.zh: 编辑「附带条件的道歉」没有说清那篇报道是否真的造成了伤害。

collocations: give a conditional apology
phrase something as a conditional apology
a conditional apology beginning with if

words.enDefinition: To check that both people agree on what was said or arranged in an earlier conversation.

examples.en: Could you confirm the details we discussed before I send the information to our group?
examples.zh: 我把信息发给小组之前，您能「确认我们谈过的细节」吗？

examples.en: I'll call tomorrow to confirm the details we discussed about the replacement session this morning.
examples.zh: 我明天会打电话「确认我们谈过的细节」，是今天上午说到的补办场次。

collocations: could you confirm the details we discussed
write to confirm the details we discussed
confirm the details we discussed at the desk

words.enDefinition: Details from different people or sources that cannot all be correct at the same time.

examples.en: I received conflicting information about where to pick up the keys for our meeting room.
examples.zh: 关于去哪里领会议室钥匙，我收到了「相互矛盾的信息」。

examples.en: The manager checked why visitors had been given conflicting information at the two reception desks.
examples.zh: 经理核查了为什么访客在两个接待处得到「相互矛盾的信息」。

collocations: receive conflicting information
check conflicting information
give conflicting information about a booking

words.enDefinition: A decision made when the group generally accepts the same outcome

examples.en: The group made a consensus decision after everyone suggested changes to the original plan.
examples.zh: 每个人都对原计划提了修改建议后，小组「达成共识并定下了方案」。

examples.en: Sharing the studio was a consensus decision after we discussed everyone's class schedules.
examples.zh: 大家讨论过各自的课表，最终就共用工作室「达成了共识」。

collocations: make a consensus decision
work toward a consensus decision
record a consensus decision

words.enDefinition: To regard the issue as finished and expect no further discussion or action on it.

examples.en: We can consider the matter closed now that everyone has received the corrected hall passes.
examples.zh: 大家都收到了更正后的大厅通行证，现在可以「把这件事了结了」。

examples.en: I wasn't ready to consider the matter closed until the office corrected the record in writing.
examples.zh: 办公室书面纠正记录之前，我还不能「认为此事已经了结」。

collocations: consider the matter closed after a reply
say you consider the matter closed
ready to consider the matter closed

words.enDefinition: An arrangement prepared in advance for a possible unexpected problem

examples.en: We drew up a contingency plan for the fair in case it rained.
examples.zh: 我们为集市拟了一份下雨时用的「应变计划」。

examples.en: Do both teams know the contingency plan if their meeting room is suddenly unavailable?
examples.zh: 如果会议室突然不能用，两个小组都知道「应变计划」吗？

collocations: make a contingency plan
put a contingency plan in place
agree on a contingency plan for bad weather

words.enDefinition: to provide accurate information after someone has formed the wrong idea about a situation

examples.en: I wanted to correct a false impression after my message sounded more critical than intended.
examples.zh: 我的消息听着比本意更像批评，我想「纠正错误印象」。

examples.en: We held a short meeting to correct a false impression about who approved the changes.
examples.zh: 我们开了个短会，「纠正关于谁批准了修改的错误印象」。

collocations: try to correct a false impression
correct a false impression about someone
write to correct a false impression

words.enDefinition: To fix an incorrect statement or detail in a record or previous account.

examples.en: I asked the office to correct the record after showing the original appointment confirmation.
examples.zh: 我出示了原先的预约确认单，请办公室「纠正记录中的错误」。

examples.en: We needed to correct the record because the notes said our group had cancelled.
examples.zh: 记录说是我们小组取消的，所以我们得「纠正记录中的错误」。

collocations: ask someone to correct the record
correct the record in writing
correct the record about the date

words.enDefinition: A step taken to correct a problem or help prevent it happening again.

examples.en: The response described the corrective action the venue would take after reviewing our booking error.
examples.zh: 答复说明了场馆复核我们的预订错误后会采取哪些「纠正措施」。

examples.en: The team agreed on corrective action before printing new signs for the front entrance.
examples.zh: 团队先商定了「纠正措施」，再给正门印新的指示牌。

collocations: take corrective action
recommend corrective action
explain the corrective action

words.enDefinition: asks permission to make a personal request of someone

examples.en: Could I ask a favour? I left my notebook on the table upstairs today.
examples.zh: 「能请你帮个忙吗」？我今天把笔记本落在楼上那张桌子上了。

examples.en: Could I ask a favour while you are here and the others are packing up?
examples.zh: 你还在这儿，其他人在收东西，「能请你帮个忙吗」？

collocations: could I ask a favour before you go
could I ask a favour of you
could I ask a favour for this afternoon

words.enDefinition: asks permission to use someone else's charger temporarily

examples.en: Could I borrow your charger until my phone has enough power to show the map?
examples.zh: 「能借用你的充电器吗」？我只需要把手机充到能看地图。

examples.en: Could I borrow your charger? I forgot mine when we moved to this room.
examples.zh: 「能借用你的充电器吗」？换到这个房间时，我忘了拿自己的。

collocations: could I borrow your charger for a minute
could I borrow your charger until lunch
ask if I could borrow your charger

words.enDefinition: asks someone to let you walk past where they are

examples.en: Could I get past? I need to get to the shelf behind you.
examples.zh: 「能让我过去吗」？我得去你身后的架子那儿。

examples.en: Could I get past with this box once you've finished moving your chair?
examples.zh: 你把椅子挪完之后，「能让我抱着箱子过去吗」？

collocations: could I get past here
could I get past you please
ask if I could get past

words.enDefinition: A polite way to pause another person's explanation at a particular point, often to clarify it.

examples.en: Could I stop you there to check which gate the coach is leaving from?
examples.zh: 「我能先打断你一下吗」？我想确认长途车从哪个门口出发。

examples.en: Could I stop you there for a moment while I write down the new date?
examples.zh: 「我能先打断你一下吗」？让我先记下新日期。

collocations: could I stop you there for a moment
could I stop you there to check something
could I stop you there before we go on

words.enDefinition: asks for permission to test something before deciding or using it

examples.en: Could I try it first on a bit of scrap paper before using the poster?
examples.zh: 「我能先在废纸上试一下吗」？试过了再用在海报上。

examples.en: Could I try it first? I want to check whether my hands can reach both handles.
examples.zh: 「我能先试一下吗」？我想看看两只手能不能够到两边的把手。

collocations: could I try it first then decide
could I try it first on a spare page
ask if I could try it first

words.expression: could I try it on my own
words.lemma: could i try it on my own
words.enDefinition: asks whether you can attempt something without another person's help
acceptedEnVariants: could I try it on my own

examples.en: Could I try it on my own now that you have shown me where the pieces go?
examples.zh: 你已经告诉我零件该放在哪儿了，「我能自己试试看吗」？

examples.en: Could I try it on my own? I think I can put the display together now.
examples.zh: 「我能自己试试看吗」？我觉得现在可以把展台搭好了。

collocations: could I try it on my own first
could I try it on my own this time
ask if I could try it on my own

words.expression: could we do one at a time
words.lemma: could we do one at a time
words.enDefinition: asks to handle items or tasks individually rather than together
acceptedEnVariants: could we do one at a time

examples.en: Could we do one at a time so we don't put the wrong label on anything?
examples.zh: 「能不能一次做一个」？这样就不会把标签贴错。

examples.en: Could we do one at a time? There isn't enough space to spread everything out here.
examples.zh: 「能不能一次做一个」？这儿没地方把所有东西都摊开。

collocations: could we do one at a time here
ask if we could do one at a time
could we do one at a time for now

words.expression: could we leave that until later
words.lemma: could we leave that until later
words.zhGloss: 那件事能留到晚点再做吗
words.enDefinition: suggests postponing a shared task to a later time
acceptedZhAnswers: 那件事能留到晚点再做吗
acceptedEnVariants: could we leave that until later

examples.en: Could we leave that until later? We need to get these boxes off the stairs first.
examples.zh: 「那件事能留到晚点再做吗」？我们得先把这些箱子从楼梯上搬开。

examples.en: Could we leave that until later when both of us have finished work on the poster?
examples.zh: 等咱俩都做完海报，「那件事能留到晚点再做吗」？

collocations: could we leave that until later today
could we leave that until later this week
ask if we could leave that until later

words.expression: could we use the same terms
words.lemma: could we use the same terms
words.zhGloss: 我们能用同一套说法吗
words.enDefinition: A request to use the same words for things so people can follow the discussion consistently.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们能用同一套说法吗
acceptedEnVariants: could we use the same terms

examples.en: Could we use the same terms on both lists so people know which boxes match?
examples.zh: 「两份清单能都用同一套说法吗」？这样大家知道哪些箱子是对应的。

examples.en: Could we use the same terms from now on when we mention the two entrances?
examples.zh: 之后提到两个入口时，「我们能用同一套说法吗」？

collocations: could we use the same terms on both lists
could we use the same terms from now on
ask could we use the same terms

words.enDefinition: A polite request for precise details instead of a broad or general statement.

examples.en: Could you be more specific about which cupboard you want us to leave empty?
examples.zh: 「你能说得具体一点吗」？哪个柜子需要我们腾空？

examples.en: Could you be more specific about which set of cables goes with this projector?
examples.zh: 「你能说得具体一点吗」？哪一套线跟这台投影仪配套？

collocations: could you be more specific about the time
could you be more specific about what changed
could you be more specific for us

words.expression: could you bring it a little closer
words.lemma: could you bring it a little closer
words.enDefinition: asks someone to move an object slightly closer to you
acceptedEnVariants: could you bring it a little closer

examples.en: Could you bring it a little closer so I can read the writing on the label?
examples.zh: 「能再拿近一点吗」？我想看清标签上的字。

examples.en: Could you bring it a little closer? I can't reach it from this side of the bench.
examples.zh: 「能再拿近一点吗」？我从长凳这头够不着。

collocations: could you bring it a little closer please
could you bring it a little closer to me
ask if you could bring it a little closer

words.enDefinition: asks someone to stop a door closing while you pass through

examples.en: Could you catch the door while I push this little cart into the room?
examples.zh: 我把小推车推进去时，「能顺手扶一下门吗」？

examples.en: Could you catch the door? My hands are full and the door is already swinging shut.
examples.zh: 「能顺手扶一下门吗」？我手上都是东西，门已经要合上了。

collocations: could you catch the door for me
could you catch the door please
ask if you could catch the door

words.expression: could you do that a little earlier
words.lemma: could you do that a little earlier
words.zhGloss: 能稍微早点做那件事吗
words.enDefinition: asks someone to carry out an action sooner than planned
acceptedZhAnswers: 能稍微早点做那件事吗
acceptedEnVariants: could you do that a little earlier

examples.en: Could you do that a little earlier so I can bring the forms inside before class?
examples.zh: 「能稍微早点做那件事吗」？这样我能在课前把表格带进去。

examples.en: Could you do that a little earlier if you are already going past the noticeboard at noon?
examples.zh: 如果你中午本来就会经过公告栏，「能稍微早点做那件事吗」？

collocations: could you do that a little earlier today
could you do that a little earlier next time
ask if you could do that a little earlier

words.expression: could you give me an example
words.lemma: could you give me an example
words.enDefinition: A polite request for a particular case that makes an idea easier to understand.
acceptedEnVariants: could you give me an example

examples.en: Could you give me an example of what counts as a large item for collection?
examples.zh: 「你能给我举个例子吗」？回收时什么样的东西算大件？

examples.en: Could you give me an example of the kind of message you want us to send?
examples.zh: 「你能给我举个例子吗」？就说你想让我们发哪种消息。

collocations: could you give me an example of that
