acceptedEnVariants: do you mind if I write on this

examples.en: Do you mind if I write on this before handing it back to the student who made it?
examples.zh: 把它还给制作它的同学之前，「介意我在这上面写字吗」？

examples.en: Do you mind if I write on this? I only need to add one small arrow here.
examples.zh: 「介意我在这上面写字吗」？我只需要在这儿添一个小箭头。

collocations: do you mind if I write on this copy
do you mind if I write on this sheet
ask if you mind if I write on this

words.expression: do you need me the whole time
words.lemma: do you need me the whole time
words.enDefinition: checks whether a helper is required throughout an activity
acceptedEnVariants: do you need me the whole time

examples.en: Do you need me the whole time, or can I leave once the chairs are out?
examples.zh: 「我需要一直在场吗」？还是把椅子摆出来就可以走？

examples.en: Do you need me the whole time when we pack up the display this afternoon together?
examples.zh: 今天下午一起拆展台时，「我需要一直在场吗」？

collocations: do you need me the whole time or just at first
do you need me the whole time today
ask if you need me the whole time

words.expression: do you need this right away
words.lemma: do you need this right away
words.enDefinition: checks whether the requested item or action is urgent
acceptedEnVariants: do you need this right away

examples.en: Do you need this right away, or can I bring it round after my seminar?
examples.zh: 「你马上就需要这个吗」？还是我开完研讨课再送过去？

examples.en: Do you need this right away? I can go and find the right charger now.
examples.zh: 「你马上就需要这个吗」？我现在可以去找合适的充电器。

collocations: do you need this right away or later
do you need this right away today
ask if you need this right away

words.enDefinition: A question checking whether a rule or explanation applies to the case now being discussed.

examples.en: Does that apply here too if we share the kitchen with a different floor?
examples.zh: 如果我们跟另一层的人合用厨房，「这也适用于这里吗」？

examples.en: Does that apply here when the people using the room have an evening booking?
examples.zh: 使用房间的人订的是晚间时段，「这也适用于这里吗」？

collocations: does that apply here as well
does that apply here in our building
ask does that apply here

words.enDefinition: A question checking if the group or rule just mentioned applies to you personally.

examples.en: Does that include me if I'm only helping to carry a few things upstairs?
examples.zh: 如果我只是帮忙把几件东西搬到楼上，「这也包括我吗」？

examples.en: Does that include me too now that I've changed my plans for Friday evening?
examples.zh: 既然我改了周五晚上的安排，「这也包括我吗」？

collocations: does that include me as a volunteer
does that include me this time
does that include me too

words.enDefinition: tells someone not to be overly harsh or ashamed about a mistake

examples.en: Don't beat yourself up over one missed deadline in an otherwise difficult first term.
examples.zh: 第一学期本来就不容易，漏了一个截止日期，「别太责怪自己」。

examples.en: Don't beat yourself up, we can still change the date before people reserve their tickets.
examples.zh: 「别太责怪自己」，大家还没订票，我们还能改日期。

collocations: don't beat yourself up about it
don't beat yourself up over a mistake
remember not to beat yourself up

words.expression: don't make plans on my behalf
words.lemma: don't make plans on my behalf
words.enDefinition: a request not to decide or organize arrangements for you without consulting you
acceptedEnVariants: don't make plans on my behalf

examples.en: “Don't make plans on my behalf,” I told my cousin after she accepted a dinner invite for me.
examples.zh: 表姐替我答应了晚餐邀约，我告诉她：“「别替我做安排」。”

examples.en: When my group picked a time for my rehearsal, I said, “Don't make plans on my behalf.”
examples.zh: 小组替我选了排练时间，我说：“「别替我做安排」。”

collocations: please don't make plans on my behalf
don't make plans on my behalf unless we talk first
next time, don't make plans on my behalf

words.zhGloss: 不用围着我的时间安排
words.enDefinition: a way to tell someone to continue planning without waiting for your availability
acceptedZhAnswers: 不用围着我的时间安排

examples.en: “Don't plan around me,” I said when the study group offered to move the whole session.
examples.zh: 学习小组说可以把整场活动改期，我说：“「不用围着我的时间安排」。”

examples.en: “Don't plan around me. Pick whichever day works for you,” Maya wrote in the picnic chat.
examples.zh: 玛雅在野餐群里写道：“「不用围着我的时间安排」。你们挑方便的日子就好。”

collocations: please don't plan around me
don't plan around me this weekend
don't plan around me if everyone else is free

words.expression: don't put my name down without asking
words.lemma: don't put my name down without asking
words.zhGloss: 没问我之前别替我报名
words.enDefinition: a request not to sign you up or register your interest without permission
acceptedZhAnswers: 没问我之前别替我报名
acceptedEnVariants: don't put my name down without asking

examples.en: “Don't put my name down without asking,” I said when the club passed around the volunteer list.
examples.zh: 社团传看志愿者名单时，我说：“「没问我之前别替我报名」。”

examples.en: When the class discussed extra shifts, I reminded my partner, “Don't put my name down without asking.”
examples.zh: 班上商量加班次时，我提醒搭档：“「没问我之前别替我报名」。”

collocations: please don't put my name down without asking
don't put my name down without asking me first
next time, don't put my name down without asking

words.expression: don't take that as a yes
words.lemma: don't take that as a yes
words.enDefinition: a way to clarify that interest or a tentative comment was not a commitment
acceptedEnVariants: don't take that as a yes

examples.en: “Don't take that as a yes,” I said after telling the group I liked their proposal.
examples.zh: 我跟小组说我喜欢他们的提议，又补了一句：“「先别当我答应了」。”

examples.en: “I might have time, but don't take that as a yes,” Keiko told her partner.
examples.zh: 惠子告诉搭档：“我可能有空，但「先别当我答应了」。”

collocations: please don't take that as a yes
don't take that as a yes just yet
don't take that as a yes from me

words.enDefinition: A direct request to keep an existing complaint or issue open until there has been more action.

examples.en: Please don't close it yet because the booking confirmation still shows our old arrival time.
examples.zh: 「请先别结案」，因为预约确认单上仍是原来的到达时间。

examples.en: I wrote “Please don't close it yet” because we had not received the corrected timetable.
examples.zh: 我在消息里说，我们还没看到更正后的时刻表，「请先别结案」。

collocations: please don't close it yet
tell them don't close it yet
don't close it yet, please

words.enDefinition: Reserve the same room for two groups at the same time

examples.en: Please check both calendars so we don't double-book the room for Thursday afternoon.
examples.zh: 请核对两份日历，以免我们把周四下午「同一个房间同时订给两组」。

examples.en: It's easy to double-book the room when each club keeps its own schedule.
examples.zh: 各社团各管自己的日程时，很容易把「同一个房间同时订给两组」。

collocations: try not to double-book the room
accidentally double-book the room
make sure we don't double-book the room

words.zhGloss: 连续出现的两个相同字母
words.enDefinition: A pair of identical letters next to each other in a written word or name.
acceptedZhAnswers: 连续出现的两个相同字母

examples.en: The name has a double letter in the middle, so please check before you print it.
examples.zh: 这个名字中间「连续出现两个相同字母」，打印前请确认一下。

examples.en: I forgot the double letter when I entered the street name into the map again.
examples.zh: 我再次把街道名输入地图时，忘了那里有「连续出现的两个相同字母」。

collocations: write a double letter
check for a double letter
spell a name with a double letter

words.enDefinition: A disadvantage of a situation or choice under discussion

examples.en: The downside of using two rooms is that we need twice as many volunteers.
examples.zh: 用两个房间「不利的一面」是我们得要两倍的志愿者。

examples.en: Mina pointed out one downside of the shared desk before we moved anything.
examples.zh: 我们还没搬东西，米娜就指出了共用书桌的一个「缺点」。

collocations: the main downside
the downside of that plan
a potential downside

words.zhGloss: 提醒他人留意反复发生的情况
words.enDefinition: To point out that similar problems have occurred more than once so people consider them together.
acceptedZhAnswers: 提醒他人留意反复发生的情况

examples.en: We wanted to draw attention to a pattern of the last shuttle leaving early on Fridays.
examples.zh: 我们想「提醒大家留意反复发生的情况」，周五最后一班接驳车常提前发车。

examples.en: I used the booking records to draw attention to a pattern that individual complaints had missed.
examples.zh: 我用预订记录「提醒大家留意反复发生的情况」，单看一条投诉是发现不了的。

collocations: draw attention to a pattern of delays
draw attention to a pattern in the reports
use records to draw attention to a pattern

words.enDefinition: Set a firm limit on what you are willing to accept

examples.en: We can change the schedule, but we draw the line at asking people to skip class.
examples.zh: 我们可以改日程，但「底线是不能」要求大家逃课。

examples.en: I'm happy to help set up, but I draw the line at staying past midnight.
examples.zh: 我愿意帮忙布置，但我「最多只能待到」午夜。

collocations: draw the line at missing classes
draw the line at losing rehearsal time
draw the line at a late finish

words.enDefinition: Prepare a short list of the choices worth considering further

examples.en: We should draw up a shortlist of venues that both teams can reach after class.
examples.zh: 我们该把两个小组下课后都能去的场地「列成一份备选清单」。

examples.en: Could you draw up a shortlist of ideas that don't need sound equipment for Saturday?
examples.zh: 你能把周六不用音响设备的点子「列成一份备选清单」吗？

collocations: draw up a shortlist of venues
draw up a shortlist together
draw up a shortlist by Friday

words.zhGloss: 在该负责的事上掉链子
words.enDefinition: to make a mistake by failing to handle a responsibility you were expected to manage
acceptedZhAnswers: 在该负责的事上掉链子

examples.en: I knew I could not drop the ball again on sending the final reminder.
examples.zh: 我知道发最后一条提醒是我该做的，不能再「掉链子」了。

examples.en: If we drop the ball on the room booking, the group has nowhere to meet.
examples.zh: 要是我们在订房间这件事上「掉链子」，小组就没地方开会了。

collocations: drop the ball on a task
admit you dropped the ball
apologise for dropping the ball

words.enDefinition: Set a room aside for a particular activity or group

examples.en: Let's earmark a room for interviews so the rest of the group can keep talking.
examples.zh: 我们「留一间房做采访」吧，这样其他人可以继续聊天。

examples.en: We agreed to earmark a room for students who needed somewhere quiet to work.
examples.zh: 我们同意给需要安静地方学习的同学「专门留一间房」。

collocations: earmark a room for interviews
agree to earmark a room
earmark a room for each club

words.zhGloss: 靠行动重新赢得某人的信任
words.enDefinition: to become trusted again by acting dependably over time after letting someone down
acceptedZhAnswers: 靠行动重新赢得某人的信任

examples.en: It takes time to earn back someone's trust when they were counting on you.
examples.zh: 对方原本指望你，这时候「重新赢得对方的信任」需要时间。

examples.en: You cannot earn back someone's trust just by sending a longer message the next day.
examples.zh: 仅仅第二天发条更长的消息，没法「重新赢得对方的信任」。

collocations: work to earn back someone's trust
try to earn back someone's trust
take time to earn back someone's trust

words.zhGloss: 承认自己从前的话说错了
words.enDefinition: to have to admit that an earlier statement, often a confident prediction, was wrong
acceptedZhAnswers: 承认自己从前的话说错了

examples.en: I had to eat my words after our new member finished the design in a day.
examples.zh: 新成员一天就做完了设计，我只好「承认自己之前的话说错了」。

examples.en: You'll have to eat your words if the small theatre sells out again this weekend.
examples.zh: 要是这个周末小剧场又售罄，你就得「承认自己从前的话说错了」。

collocations: have to eat your words
make someone eat their words
be forced to eat your words

words.enDefinition: To move a complaint to a higher level of authority or to the next review stage.

examples.en: I chose to escalate a complaint after receiving the same reply from two different desks.
examples.zh: 在两个服务台都得到同样的答复后，我选择「将投诉升级处理」。

examples.en: The adviser explained when their team might escalate a complaint to someone with more authority.
examples.zh: 顾问解释了他们团队在什么情况下可能会「将投诉升级处理」，交给权限更大的人。

collocations: escalate a complaint to a manager
decide to escalate a complaint
ask how to escalate a complaint

words.enDefinition: Make the amount each person or group has to do more equal

examples.en: We need to even out the workload so nobody spends the whole evening at check-in.
examples.zh: 我们得「把工作量分得更均衡」，免得有人整晚都在签到处。

examples.en: Let's even out the workload by moving one of the interviews to the afternoon pair.
examples.zh: 我们把一场采访交给下午那一组，「让两组工作量更均衡」。

collocations: move tasks around to even out the workload
try to even out the workload
need to even out the workload

words.enDefinition: Used to say that a group stopped speaking, often at the same moment.

examples.en: Everyone went quiet after the question, so I waited to see if anyone would answer.
examples.zh: 问题一提出来，「大家都安静下来了」，我就等着看有没有人回答。

examples.en: Everyone went quiet for a moment before Alex explained what the sign actually meant.
examples.zh: 「大家都安静了一会儿」，然后亚历克斯解释了牌子到底是什么意思。

collocations: everyone went quiet after the question
everyone went quiet for a moment
notice that everyone went quiet

words.enDefinition: to make an offer or gesture showing that you want to end a disagreement

examples.en: Our group chose to extend an olive branch by inviting both organisers to the planning meeting.
examples.zh: 我们小组邀请两名组织者都来开筹备会，以此「主动释放和解信号」。

examples.en: The chair tried to extend an olive branch after the debate over using the room.
examples.zh: 两方就是否使用房间争执后，主席试图「主动释放和解信号」。

collocations: extend an olive branch to someone
try to extend an olive branch
choose to extend an olive branch

words.enDefinition: to start or agree to do something and then neglect to complete it

examples.en: It damages trust if you fail to follow through after volunteering to check the references.
examples.zh: 主动说要核对参考文献，却「没有把答应的事做完」，会损害信任。

examples.en: I did not want to fail to follow through after offering to contact the venue.
examples.zh: 我主动提出联系场地，不希望「到头来没把答应的事做完」。

collocations: sometimes fail to follow through
fail to follow through on a commitment
apologise for failing to follow through

words.enDefinition: To be less satisfactory than what people expected from a service or experience.

examples.en: The tour seemed to fall short of expectations when it ended before the advertised demonstrations.
examples.zh: 导览在宣传过的演示开始前就结束了，似乎「没有达到预期」。

examples.en: Our feedback explained why the new registration system continued to fall short of expectations for evening visitors.
examples.zh: 我们的反馈解释了为什么新报名系统仍「没有达到晚间访客的预期」。

collocations: fall short of expectations on service
consistently fall short of expectations
fall short of expectations in several areas

words.enDefinition: A less preferred choice kept in case the main choice fails

examples.en: We kept the courtyard as a fallback option in case the gym was booked.
examples.zh: 我们把院子留作「备选方案」，以免体育馆已被订走。

examples.en: What's our fallback option if the room we want isn't ready before lunch?
examples.zh: 如果想要的房间午饭前还没准备好，我们「退一步用哪个方案」？

collocations: keep a fallback option
agree on a fallback option
use something as a fallback option

words.enDefinition: Comments about what people experienced and ideas about what could be improved.

examples.en: The venue welcomed feedback and suggestions after the first week of its new booking system.
examples.zh: 新预订系统上线一周后，场馆欢迎大家提供「反馈和建议」。

examples.en: Our group wrote down its feedback and suggestions before speaking to the event organiser.
examples.zh: 和活动组织者沟通之前，我们小组先写下了「反馈和建议」。

collocations: welcome feedback and suggestions
collect feedback and suggestions
respond to feedback and suggestions

words.enDefinition: A particular way for people to send comments or suggestions to an organisation.

examples.en: The venue set up a feedback channel for visitors who had trouble finding accessible seats.
examples.zh: 场馆为找不到无障碍座位的访客设立了一个「反馈渠道」。

examples.en: I asked which feedback channel the club used for comments about its weekly classes.
examples.zh: 我问了俱乐部用哪个「反馈渠道」收集每周课程的意见。

collocations: choose a feedback channel
set up a feedback channel
use the official feedback channel

words.enDefinition: An organisation's last response at a given stage of handling a complaint, often stating its decision and actions.

examples.en: The venue's final response explained who had approved the change to the entrance arrangements.
examples.zh: 场馆在「最终答复」里说明了是谁批准了入口安排的变更。

examples.en: I waited for a final response before telling the group what had been decided about our booking.
examples.zh: 我等到「最终答复」出来，再告诉小组我们的预约是怎么处理的。

collocations: receive a final response
send a final response
wait for the final response

words.enDefinition: Complete the remaining decisions so an arrangement is ready to use

examples.en: We can finalize the plan once the evening team picks which entrance to use.
examples.zh: 等晚上的小组选好用哪个入口，我们就能「敲定方案」。

examples.en: The student groups will meet tomorrow to finalize the plan for their shared performance.
examples.zh: 这些学生小组明天开会「敲定共同表演的方案」。

collocations: help finalize the plan
meet to finalize the plan
wait to finalize the plan

words.enDefinition: a clear response that leaves little doubt that the answer is no

examples.en: The committee finally understood my firm refusal when I said I would not chair the event.
examples.zh: 我说我不会主持活动后，委员会终于明白了我「坚决的拒绝」。

examples.en: After the third reminder, the student sent a firm refusal to the volunteer coordinator.
examples.zh: 收到第三次提醒后，那名学生给志愿者协调员发去消息，作出「坚决的拒绝」。

collocations: respond with a firm refusal
a firm refusal to participate
a polite but firm refusal

words.enDefinition: The time period a person would most like to use

examples.en: We asked everyone to give their first choice of time slot before we drew up the rota.
examples.zh: 排轮班表之前，我们请大家报一下各自「首选的时段」。

examples.en: I got my first choice of time slot because the other group needed the room earlier.
examples.zh: 另一个小组想早点用这个房间，所以我选到了自己「首选的时段」。

collocations: ask for each person's first choice of time slot
get your first choice of time slot
note everyone's first choice of time slot

words.enDefinition: The person, team, or place you should approach first when you need help.

examples.en: The workshop desk was our first point of contact when something went wrong with registration.
examples.zh: 报名出问题时，「我们最先联系的是」工作坊服务台。

examples.en: Could you tell me the first point of contact for problems with evening room bookings?
examples.zh: 请问晚间房间预订出了问题，应该「最先联系谁」？

collocations: ask for the first point of contact
serve as the first point of contact
identify the first point of contact

words.enDefinition: Arrange activities at times that do not interfere with anyone's classes

examples.en: We can fit the plan around classes by offering a morning and an evening session.
examples.zh: 我们可以安排早晚各一场，来「让计划配合大家的课表」。

examples.en: Can we fit the plan around classes before we ask everyone to commit to a date?
examples.zh: 请大家确定日期之前，我们能先「按课表调整计划」吗？

collocations: try to fit the plan around classes
find a way to fit the plan around classes
agree to fit the plan around classes

words.enDefinition: A deadline for completing work that will not change

examples.en: We have a fixed deadline for the poster, but the rehearsal date can change.
examples.zh: 海报有「固定的截止时间」，但排练日期可以改。

examples.en: With a fixed deadline on Friday, both teams had to check their files earlier.
examples.zh: 周五有个「固定截止时间」，两组都得提前检查自己的文件。

collocations: have a fixed deadline
work toward a fixed deadline
agree on a fixed deadline

words.enDefinition: To understand what people are talking about as the exchange continues.

examples.en: I could follow the conversation better once the group switched to a quieter table.
examples.zh: 小组换到更安静的桌子后，我更容易「跟上对话」。

examples.en: It was difficult to follow the conversation because I missed the name of the place.
examples.zh: 我没听到地点名，所以很难「跟上对话」。

collocations: struggle to follow the conversation
easier to follow the conversation
help someone follow the conversation

words.enDefinition: to do or finish what you promised, especially after taking the first step

examples.en: We wanted to follow through on a promise to find a quieter meeting room.
examples.zh: 我们承诺找个更安静的会议室，想「把承诺付诸行动」。

examples.en: It helps to set a deadline when you follow through on a promise to someone.
examples.zh: 要「把对别人的承诺付诸行动」时，定个截止时间会有帮助。

collocations: agree to follow through on a promise
manage to follow through on a promise
fail to follow through on a promise

words.enDefinition: limits permission to the person who received it

examples.en: This copy is for your own use only, so ask before making another one.
examples.zh: 这份「仅限你自己使用」，需要复印的话先问一下。

examples.en: My friend said, "The tool is for your own use only this afternoon."
examples.zh: 朋友说：「那个工具下午仅限你自己使用」。

collocations: give something for your own use only
marked for your own use only
explain it's for your own use only

words.enDefinition: to forgive someone and agree not to keep bringing up what they did

examples.en: I was willing to discuss it, but I wasn't ready to forgive and forget.
examples.zh: 我愿意谈这件事，但还没准备好「原谅并放下旧事」。

examples.en: They eventually chose to forgive and forget after months of avoiding each other on campus.
examples.zh: 他们在校园里互相躲了几个月，最后选择「原谅并放下旧事」。

collocations: be ready to forgive and forget
choose to forgive and forget
decide to forgive and forget

words.enDefinition: From the beginning of something such as a set of directions, a text, or a rehearsal.

examples.en: Can we take it from the top so I can note each change in order?
examples.zh: 我们能「从头开始」吗？我想按顺序记下每处改动。

examples.en: Let's go through it from the top now that everyone can hear us clearly.
examples.zh: 现在大家都能听清我们说话了，我们「从头开始」过一遍吧。

collocations: take it from the top
start from the top
go through it from the top

words.enDefinition: to react as if you are being attacked when someone criticises or questions what you did

examples.en: I tend to get defensive when someone points out a mistake in front of everyone.
examples.zh: 有人当着大家的面指出错误时，我很容易「急于为自己辩解」。

examples.en: I tried not to get defensive when my partner explained why the decision hurt her.
examples.zh: 搭档解释那个决定为什么让她难过时，我尽量不「急于为自己辩解」。

collocations: try not to get defensive
get defensive about criticism
tend to get defensive

words.enDefinition: Ask all the people involved to contribute ideas or feedback

examples.en: We should get everyone's input on the layout before one group makes all the decisions.
examples.zh: 在某一组独自把方案全定了之前，我们应该「征求大家对布局的意见」。

examples.en: Let's wait until tomorrow so we can get everyone's input on the rehearsal order.
examples.zh: 我们等到明天吧，这样就能「征求大家对排练顺序的意见」。

collocations: try to get everyone's input
get everyone's input before deciding
make time to get everyone's input

words.expression: get off on the wrong foot
words.lemma: get off on the wrong foot
words.zhGloss: 一开头就相处得不太顺
words.enDefinition: to begin a relationship or shared activity in an awkward or unfriendly way
acceptedZhAnswers: 一开头就相处得不太顺
acceptedEnVariants: get off on the wrong foot

examples.en: It's easy to get off on the wrong foot when nobody explains how roles were assigned.
examples.zh: 没人解释角色是怎么分配的，就很容易「一开头就相处得不太顺」。

examples.en: We did get off on the wrong foot, but things improved by the second meeting.
examples.zh: 我们的确是「一开头就相处得不太顺」，到第二次会议时情况好转了。

collocations: get off on the wrong foot with someone
seem to get off on the wrong foot
avoid getting off on the wrong foot

words.enDefinition: to obtain a person's agreement before you do something

examples.en: We needed to get someone's permission before taking any chairs from that room.
examples.zh: 我们得「得到相关人员的同意」，才能从那个房间搬走椅子。

examples.en: I wanted to get someone's permission before using their photographs in our display.
examples.zh: 在展览中用别人的照片前，我想先「得到对方的同意」。

collocations: remember to get someone's permission
need to get someone's permission
get someone's permission before using a room

words.enDefinition: To check what actually happened so your account is accurate.

examples.en: We wanted to get the facts straight before saying who had changed the original booking.
examples.zh: 在说是谁改了原预约之前，我们想「先把事实核实清楚」。

examples.en: The organiser checked both schedules to get the facts straight after we raised the issue.
examples.zh: 我们反映问题后，组织者核对了两份日程表，以便「把事实核实清楚」。

collocations: get the facts straight first
take time to get the facts straight
make sure you get the facts straight

words.enDefinition: To explain what happened in an understandable way with relevant details.

examples.en: I tried to give a clear account of what happened from the moment we arrived.
examples.zh: 我试着「把经过说清楚」，从我们抵达时发生的事讲起。

examples.en: The manager asked me to give a clear account before she spoke to the receptionist.
examples.zh: 经理请我先「把经过说清楚」，她再去和接待员谈。

collocations: give a clear account of the incident
give a clear account of what happened
be asked to give a clear account

words.enDefinition: Become slightly more flexible about a particular part of a plan

examples.en: If we give a little on the timing, more students can join after class.
examples.zh: 如果我们「在时间上让一步」，就有更多学生能下课后来参加。

examples.en: Could both groups give a little on the order so everyone can use the main hall?
examples.zh: 两组能不能都「在顺序上让一点步」，这样大家都能用大厅？

collocations: give a little on the schedule
give a little on the layout
ask someone to give a little on timing

words.enDefinition: Mutual willingness to make concessions for an arrangement to work

examples.en: Sharing the studio took some give and take before both groups felt it was fair.
examples.zh: 共用工作室需要双方都「让一点步」，两组才都觉得公平。

examples.en: There was plenty of give and take when we planned a schedule that included everyone.
examples.zh: 为了排出照顾到每个人的时间表，我们商量时「互相作了不少让步」。

collocations: a bit of give and take
involve some give and take
require give and take on both sides

words.enDefinition: to acknowledge the people who deserve recognition for their contribution

examples.en: We should give credit where it's due and thank the volunteers who designed the display.
examples.zh: 我们应该「把功劳归给应得的人」，感谢设计展示台的志愿者。

examples.en: Our editor promised to give credit where it's due when the corrected article came out.
examples.zh: 编辑答应在更正后的报道刊出时「把功劳归给应得的人」。

collocations: always give credit where it's due
make sure to give credit where it's due
give credit where it's due in public

words.enDefinition: Tell one another earlier about a change or upcoming event

examples.en: Let's give each other more notice if we need to change a shift after the rota goes out.
examples.zh: 如果轮班表发出后还要换班，我们就「更早通知彼此」。

examples.en: We agreed to give each other more notice before changing the room for a group meeting.
examples.zh: 我们商定以后要换小组会议的房间时，「提前一点互相通知」。

collocations: agree to give each other more notice
try to give each other more notice
give each other more notice about changes

words.enDefinition: Allow every person to express an opinion that can affect the decision

examples.en: We should give everyone a say before we change how volunteers sign up for shifts.
examples.zh: 改志愿者报名排班的办法之前，我们应该「让每个人都能发表意见」。

examples.en: Let's give everyone a say by hearing from each team before we choose a layout.
examples.zh: 选场地布局之前，我们先听听各组怎么说，「让每个人都能发表意见」。

collocations: try to give everyone a say
give everyone a say in the decision
make time to give everyone a say

words.enDefinition: To share your views or suggestions directly in a face-to-face conversation.

examples.en: I chose to give feedback in person because the manager could see the problem from reception.
examples.zh: 我选择「当面给反馈」，因为经理从接待处就能看到这个问题。

examples.en: Could I give feedback in person after the tour when the front desk is quieter?
examples.zh: 参观结束后，等前台不忙了，我能「当面给反馈」吗？

collocations: prefer to give feedback in person
choose to give feedback in person
ask to give feedback in person

words.enDefinition: asks someone to provide a sign when they are ready

examples.en: Please give me a signal when you want me to open the door.
examples.zh: 要我开门的时候，请「给我个信号」。

examples.en: Can you give me a signal from the other side of the table?
examples.zh: 你能从桌子另一边「给我个信号」吗？

collocations: remember to give me a signal
please give me a signal
give me a signal when you're ready

words.enDefinition: To provide background details so someone can understand a comment or situation.

examples.en: Could you give me some context before I read the message from the organiser?
examples.zh: 我读组织者的消息之前，你能「给我讲讲前因后果」吗？

examples.en: My friend tried to give me some context about the change before everyone else arrived.
examples.zh: 其他人到之前，朋友试着「给我讲讲变更的前因后果」。

collocations: could you give me some context
give me some context before I answer
give me some context for that comment

words.enDefinition: to allow a person to try again after a previous mistake or failure

examples.en: It's easier to give someone another chance when they say what they will actually change.
examples.zh: 别人说清楚自己具体会改什么时，更容易「再给对方一次机会」。

examples.en: It is sometimes fair to give someone another chance after a single honest mistake.
examples.zh: 有时别人只犯了一次无心的错，「再给对方一次机会」才公平。

collocations: decide to give someone another chance
be willing to give someone another chance
choose to give someone another chance

words.expression: give someone the benefit of the doubt
words.lemma: give someone the benefit of the doubt
words.enDefinition: to assume someone is honest or meant well when you are unsure what happened
acceptedEnVariants: give someone the benefit of the doubt

examples.en: I tried to give someone the benefit of the doubt rather than repeating a rumour.
examples.zh: 事还没弄清楚，我试着「先相信对方」，没有转述传闻。

examples.en: It is easier to give someone the benefit of the doubt after hearing their explanation.
examples.zh: 听过对方的解释后，更容易「在事情没弄清前先相信对方」。

collocations: choose to give someone the benefit of the doubt
be willing to give someone the benefit of the doubt
ask others to give someone the benefit of the doubt

words.enDefinition: to mention a mistake with little detail in a way that makes it seem unimportant

examples.en: I did not want to gloss over a mistake that affected the whole volunteer team.
examples.zh: 这个错影响了整个志愿者团队，我不想「轻描淡写地带过」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain what happened rather than gloss over a mistake in the report.
examples.zh: 导师请我们说明发生了什么，别在报告里「轻描淡写地带过错误」。

collocations: try to gloss over a mistake
refuse to gloss over a mistake
apologise without trying to gloss over a mistake

words.expression: go ahead with what we have
words.lemma: go ahead with what we have
words.enDefinition: Continue with an activity using what is already available
acceptedEnVariants: go ahead with what we have

examples.en: If the extra tables don't arrive, we'll go ahead with what we have and run smaller groups.
examples.zh: 如果额外的桌子送不到，我们就「用现有条件照常办」，把每组人数减一点。

examples.en: We agreed to go ahead with what we have once we knew the other club needed their projector.
examples.zh: 知道另一个社团也要用自己的投影仪后，我们商定「就按现有条件继续」。

collocations: decide to go ahead with what we have
willing to go ahead with what we have
agree to go ahead with what we have

words.enDefinition: To review something with another person so that both of you understand it.

examples.en: We could go over it together after the others leave to check nothing is missing.
examples.zh: 其他人走后，我们可以「一起过一遍」，看看有没有遗漏。

examples.en: Could we go over it together before I explain the route to our visitors?
examples.zh: 我给访客说明路线前，我们能「一起过一遍」吗？

collocations: go over it together once more
offer to go over it together
go over it together from the start

words.enDefinition: To use the accepted procedure or contact the people responsible when raising an issue.

examples.en: The club asked us to go through the proper channels so the complaint would reach the right person.
examples.zh: 俱乐部让我们「按正规渠道办理」，这样投诉才能传到负责的人那里。

examples.en: I wanted to go through the proper channels because the desk had no authority over bookings.
examples.zh: 因为服务台无权处理预约问题，我想「按正规渠道办理」。

collocations: ask people to go through the proper channels
go through the proper channels to complain
choose to go through the proper channels

words.enDefinition: A voluntary offer meant to show consideration after someone has experienced a problem or inconvenience.

examples.en: The venue offered a goodwill gesture by arranging an extra guided visit for the group.
examples.zh: 场馆额外给小组安排了一次导览，作为「善意补偿」。

examples.en: As a goodwill gesture, the organiser opened the exhibition early for visitors who had waited yesterday.
examples.zh: 为了做出「善意补偿」，组织者为昨天等过的访客提前开放了展览。

collocations: offer a goodwill gesture
make a goodwill gesture
accept a goodwill gesture

words.enDefinition: a feeling of guilt about something you believe you did wrong

examples.en: I had a guilty conscience after taking credit for an idea my partner came up with.
examples.zh: 搭档想出的点子被我当成自己的功劳，此后我一直「良心不安」。

examples.en: My guilty conscience made it harder to enjoy the celebration at the end of term.
examples.zh: 因为「良心不安」，我没法尽情享受学期末的庆祝活动。

collocations: have a guilty conscience
ease a guilty conscience
act out of a guilty conscience

words.enDefinition: an apology made with little effort, conviction or genuine feeling

examples.en: The team's half-hearted apology made it sound as if nobody wanted to discuss what happened.
examples.zh: 团队「敷衍的道歉」听起来像是谁都不想谈到底发生了什么。

examples.en: I could tell from his half-hearted apology that he wanted to leave the room quickly.
examples.zh: 从他那「敷衍的道歉」里，我听得出他想赶快离开房间。

collocations: give a half-hearted apology
accept a half-hearted apology
sound like a half-hearted apology

words.enDefinition: Take responsibility for the initial attempt before others review or revise

examples.en: I can handle the first pass at the script if Farah checks the timing later.
examples.zh: 如果法拉之后检查时长，我可以「负责第一轮」写稿。

examples.en: Could I handle the first pass on the slides and send them around tomorrow?
examples.zh: 幻灯片我可以「先做第一版」，明天再发给大家吗？

collocations: handle the first pass at the draft
volunteer to handle the first pass
handle the first pass on the captions

words.enDefinition: The agreed time when one person or group takes over from another

examples.en: Let's set a handover time so the second team knows when to arrive.
examples.zh: 我们定个「交接时间」，让第二组知道什么时候到。

examples.en: We moved the handover time to noon so both volunteers could be there.
examples.zh: 我们把「交接时间」改到中午，这样两位志愿者都能到场。

collocations: agree on a handover time
move the handover time
a clear handover time

words.expression: hang on to this for me
words.lemma: hang on to this for me
words.enDefinition: asks someone to keep something until you need it again
acceptedEnVariants: hang on to this for me

examples.en: Can you hang on to this for me until I finish sorting my other things?
examples.zh: 在我把别的东西整理完之前，你能「替我暂时保管这个」吗？

examples.en: Please hang on to this for me until my sister comes back to collect it.
examples.zh: 请「替我暂时保管这个」，等我妹妹回来拿。

collocations: can you hang on to this for me
please hang on to this for me
offer to hang on to this for me

words.enDefinition: expresses willingness to give someone help with what they need

examples.en: I'm happy to help if you need someone to carry the second box.
examples.zh: 如果你还需要人搬第二个箱子，我「乐意帮忙」。

examples.en: My neighbour was happy to help with the bags after I asked.
examples.zh: 我开口后，邻居「乐意帮忙」拎包。

collocations: be happy to help
always happy to help
say you're happy to help

words.zhGloss: 被别的声音盖住而听不清
words.enDefinition: Used to describe speech or other audio which another sound makes hard to hear.
acceptedZhAnswers: 被别的声音盖住而听不清

examples.en: The announcement was hard to hear over the engines of the buses outside the terminal.
examples.zh: 车站外的公交车引擎声太响，「盖住了广播，听不清」。

examples.en: Your directions were hard to hear over the music coming from the other end of the hall.
examples.zh: 大厅另一头的音乐声「盖过了你说的路线，我听不清」。

collocations: hard to hear over the music
hard to hear over traffic
hard to hear over the engines

words.expression: have I got the order right
words.lemma: have i got the order right
words.enDefinition: A question checking whether you have understood or repeated the sequence correctly.
acceptedEnVariants: have I got the order right

examples.en: Have I got the order right if I put the larger box on the table first?
examples.zh: 如果我先把较大的箱子放在桌上，「我把顺序弄对了吗」？

examples.en: Have I got the order right this time, or should we collect the badges first?
examples.zh: 「这次我把顺序弄对了吗」，还是应该先去领徽章？

collocations: have I got the order right this time
have I got the order right for tomorrow
ask have I got the order right

words.enDefinition: To listen to someone's full account before responding or deciding what you think.

examples.en: The manager made time to hear someone out even with another group waiting outside.
examples.zh: 虽说外面还有另一组人在等，经理还是抽空「听一位访客把话说完」。

examples.en: The training asks volunteers to hear someone out before trying to explain the centre's policy.
examples.zh: 培训要求志愿者先「听对方把话说完」，再试着解释中心的规定。

collocations: take the time to hear someone out
be willing to hear someone out
let me hear you out

words.enDefinition: An idea that can help someone deal with a problem or improve how something works.

examples.en: A visitor made a helpful suggestion about making the room numbers easier to read from outside.
examples.zh: 一名访客提出了一个「有帮助的建议」，让大家从门外更容易看清房间号。

examples.en: The receptionist offered a helpful suggestion while the manager was still checking the booking history.
examples.zh: 经理还在查预订记录时，接待员提了一个「有帮助的建议」。

collocations: make a helpful suggestion
offer a helpful suggestion
thank someone for a helpful suggestion

words.enDefinition: to keep feeling angry with a person because of something they did in the past

examples.en: I did not want to hold a grudge over one mistake in our first meeting.
examples.zh: 我不想因为第一次开会的一次失误就「记恨」。

examples.en: It is easy to hold a grudge when nobody ever talks about what went wrong.
examples.zh: 大家始终没谈出了什么差错，就很容易让人「记恨」。

collocations: hold a grudge against someone
refuse to hold a grudge
hold a grudge for years

words.expression: hold off on the final decision
words.lemma: hold off on the final decision
words.enDefinition: Wait before making the choice that settles the matter
acceptedEnVariants: hold off on the final decision

examples.en: We should hold off on the final decision until the evening group has seen both options.
examples.zh: 我们应该「暂缓作出最后决定」，等晚上的小组都看过两个选项。

examples.en: Can we hold off on the final decision until we know how many tables the hall has?
examples.zh: 我们能「暂缓作最后决定」，先弄清大厅里有多少张桌子吗？

collocations: agree to hold off on the final decision
hold off on the final decision until Friday
need to hold off on the final decision

words.enDefinition: to keep a receipt so it can be used later

examples.en: Could you hold on to the receipt until everyone agrees who bought which supplies?
examples.zh: 大家记清是谁买了哪些用品前，你能「先留着收据」吗？

examples.en: Please hold on to the receipt while I check which notebook belongs to me.
examples.zh: 请「先留着收据」，我确认一下哪本笔记本是我的。

collocations: remember to hold on to the receipt
ask someone to hold on to the receipt
hold on to the receipt for now

words.zhGloss: 这个话题待会儿接着说
words.enDefinition: A request to pause and remember what you want to say so you can come back to it.
acceptedZhAnswers: 这个话题待会儿接着说

examples.en: Could you hold that thought while I check who's calling from the front desk?
examples.zh: 我先看看前台是谁打来的电话，你能「待会儿接着说这件事」吗？

examples.en: Hold that thought until we get inside, where I can hear your idea properly.
examples.zh: 「进去再接着说这件事吧」，里面我就能听清你的想法了。

collocations: hold that thought for a moment
hold that thought until I get back
can you hold that thought

words.enDefinition: Do what was agreed even when there is pressure to change

examples.en: Can we hold to what we agreed about quiet setup while the next group is recording?
examples.zh: 隔壁组录制时，我们能「遵守之前的约定」，安静地布置吗？

examples.en: We'll hold to what we agreed and give every group the same number of practice minutes.
examples.zh: 我们会「遵守之前的约定」，给每组同样多的练习时间。

collocations: decide to hold to what we agreed
try to hold to what we agreed
hold to what we agreed about the timing

words.enDefinition: to make sure you answer for your actions and follow through on commitments

examples.en: It helps to hold yourself accountable by setting a date to check your progress.
examples.zh: 定一个日期来查看进展，有助于「要求自己承担责任」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how you hold yourself accountable when a project depends on your part.
examples.zh: 导师问，一个项目离不开你负责的部分时，你怎样「要求自己承担责任」。

collocations: hold yourself accountable for your actions
learn to hold yourself accountable
ways to hold yourself accountable

words.expression: how long will you need it
words.lemma: how long will you need it
words.enDefinition: asks how much time someone wants to use something
acceptedEnVariants: how long will you need it

examples.en: How long will you need it before I lend the same tape to the next group?
examples.zh: 我把同一卷胶带借给下一组之前，「你需要用多久」？

examples.en: How long will you need it? I might have to take it with me after lunch.
examples.zh: 「你需要用多久」？午饭后我可能得带走。

collocations: how long will you need it today
ask how long you will need it
how long will you need it for

words.expression: how much of this do you need
words.lemma: how much of this do you need
words.enDefinition: checks the quantity required from a larger amount of something
acceptedEnVariants: how much of this do you need

examples.en: How much of this do you need? I have to leave some for my roommate later.
examples.zh: 「这个你需要多少」？我得留一些给室友稍后用。

examples.en: How much of this do you need for the display you're putting up in the hallway?
examples.zh: 你在走廊布置的展览，「这个你需要多少」？

collocations: how much of this do you need for today
how much of this do you need right now
ask how much of this you need

words.expression: how specific do I need to be
words.lemma: how specific do i need to be
words.enDefinition: A question asking how much detail the listener expects you to give.
acceptedEnVariants: how specific do I need to be

examples.en: How specific do I need to be when I explain where the keys were found?
examples.zh: 我说明钥匙在哪儿找到时，「需要说得多具体」？

examples.en: How specific do I need to be about the dates when I tell the club?
examples.zh: 我告诉俱乐部时，关于日期「需要说得多具体」？

collocations: how specific do I need to be about dates
how specific do I need to be about my plans
ask how specific do I need to be

words.enDefinition: to upset another person emotionally through something you say or do

examples.en: It is easy to hurt someone's feelings when you joke about their work in public.
examples.zh: 公开拿别人的作品开玩笑，很容易「伤害那个人的感情」。

examples.en: I worried my remark could hurt someone's feelings even if it had sounded harmless to me.
examples.zh: 即使这话听来没什么，我也担心它会「伤害某人的感情」。

collocations: accidentally hurt someone's feelings
not mean to hurt someone's feelings
worry about hurting someone's feelings

words.enDefinition: a comment that causes someone emotional pain or distress

examples.en: His hurtful remark was about my accent, and I remembered it for a long time.
examples.zh: 他那句「伤人的话」是针对我的口音，我记了很久。

examples.en: I asked her to withdraw the hurtful remark before we continued discussing the project.
examples.zh: 项目讨论继续之前，我请她收回那句「伤人的话」。

collocations: make a hurtful remark
apologise for a hurtful remark
take back a hurtful remark

words.enDefinition: acknowledges someone's apology in a positive way without necessarily saying everything is resolved

examples.en: I appreciate the apology, and I'm glad we could talk before seeing the others.
examples.zh: 「谢谢你向我道歉」，也很高兴我们能在见其他人之前谈一谈。

examples.en: I appreciate the apology, though I would still like to discuss what changes next time.
examples.zh: 「谢谢你向我道歉」，不过我还是想谈谈下次要做哪些调整。

collocations: say I appreciate the apology
I appreciate the apology and the explanation
I appreciate the apology you offered

words.enDefinition: a way to acknowledge someone's offer graciously when turning it down

examples.en: “I appreciate the offer, but I already have a lift,” I told my neighbor.
examples.zh: 我对邻居说：“「谢谢你的好意」，不过已经有人顺路载我了。”

examples.en: When the student offered to carry my bag, I said, “I appreciate the offer, but I've got it.”
examples.zh: 那名学生提出帮我提包时，我说：“「谢谢你的好意」，我自己拿就好。”

collocations: I really appreciate the offer
I appreciate the offer to help
I appreciate the offer either way

words.expression: I can help with one part
words.lemma: i can help with one part

acceptedEnVariants: I can help with one part

acceptedEnVariants: I'd prefer not to be tagged

examples.zh: 表姐发布视频时，我说：“「我希望不要标记我」。”

collocations: I'd prefer not to be tagged in the post

I'd prefer not to be tagged in photos

words.expression: I'd prefer not to discuss that in a group

acceptedZhAnswers: 我不太想当着大家讨论这件事
acceptedEnVariants: I'd prefer not to discuss that in a group

examples.zh: 大家提到我的住宿情况时，我告诉主持人：“「我不太想当着大家讨论这件事」。”

examples.zh: 那名学生分享结果时说：“「我不太想当着大家讨论这件事」。”

examples.zh: 团队提议在我住处开会，我说：“「我想把工作和私人生活分开」。”

examples.zh: 话题转到父母身上时，我说：“「我还是不想谈家里的事」。”

words.enDefinition: promises to tell someone once the requested task is complete
acceptedEnVariants: I'll let you know when it's done

examples.en: I'll let you know when it's done so you can come back and check the labels.
examples.zh: 「做完我告诉你」，你就可以回来核对标签。

examples.en: I said, "I'll let you know when it's done," before carrying the supplies into the workshop.
examples.zh: 搬用品进工作间之前，我说：「做完我告诉你」。

collocations: don't worry, I'll let you know when it's done
yes, I'll let you know when it's done
say I'll let you know when it's done

words.enDefinition: a response indicating that you will find another way to handle the situation

examples.en: “I'll make other arrangements,” I told my neighbor when he declined to drive me to campus.
examples.zh: 邻居说不能开车送我去学校，我告诉他：“「我会另作安排」。”

examples.en: When my coworker said she couldn't cover, I replied, “I'll make other arrangements for Friday.”
examples.zh: 同事说不能替班时，我回道：“「周五我会另作安排」。”

collocations: don't worry, I'll make other arrangements
I'll make other arrangements for getting home
I'll make other arrangements if you're unavailable

words.expression: I'll make sure it gets there
words.lemma: i'll make sure it gets there
words.enDefinition: accepts responsibility for getting something to the intended place or person
acceptedEnVariants: I'll make sure it gets there

examples.en: I'll make sure it gets there before the others return to the room this evening.
examples.zh: 「我会确保把它送到」，赶在其他人今晚回到房间之前。

examples.en: My classmate said, "I'll make sure it gets there," when I handed her the spare key.
examples.zh: 我把备用钥匙交给同学时，她说：「我会确保把它送到」。

collocations: say I'll make sure it gets there
don't worry, I'll make sure it gets there
yes, I'll make sure it gets there

words.enDefinition: asks for time to process a difficult event or apology before responding or moving on

examples.en: I'll need some time before I am ready to talk about yesterday's disagreement again.
examples.zh: 「我需要一点时间」，之后才能再谈昨天的争执。

examples.en: I'll need some time to think about what you said before we meet on Friday.
examples.zh: 「我需要一点时间」想想你说的话，周五见面时再谈。

collocations: I'll need some time to think
I'll need some time before we talk
I'll need some time to get used to it

words.enDefinition: a way to limit when you will respond to work or administrative messages

examples.en: “I'll reply during working hours,” the student assistant told the organizers after receiving several late messages.
examples.zh: 接连收到几条深夜消息后，那位学生助理对组织者说：“「我会在工作时间回复」。”

examples.en: Before the weekend, I posted a quick reminder, “I'll reply during working hours.”
examples.zh: 周末前我发了条简短提醒：“「我会在工作时间回复」。”

collocations: I'll reply during working hours tomorrow
I'll reply during working hours on Monday
if it's about the event, I'll reply during working hours

words.expression: I'll take your name off the list
words.lemma: i'll take your name off the list
words.zhGloss: 我会把你的名字从名单上划掉
words.enDefinition: a way to confirm that someone will no longer be listed for an activity
acceptedZhAnswers: 我会把你的名字从名单上划掉
acceptedEnVariants: I'll take your name off the list

examples.en: “I'll take your name off the list,” I told Maya when she withdrew from the workshop.
examples.zh: 玛雅退出工作坊时，我告诉她：“「我会把你的名字从名单上划掉」。”

examples.en: After our captain declined the trip, I replied, “I'll take your name off the list.”
examples.zh: 队长婉拒出游后，我回道：“「我会把你的名字从名单上划掉」。”

collocations: I'll take your name off the list for Saturday
sure, I'll take your name off the list
I'll take your name off the list right away

words.expression: I'll text before coming over next time
words.lemma: i'll text before coming over next time
words.zhGloss: 下次过来之前我会先发消息
words.enDefinition: a promise to give advance notice after someone sets a limit on unexpected visits
acceptedZhAnswers: 下次过来之前我会先发消息
acceptedEnVariants: I'll text before coming over next time

examples.en: “I'll text before coming over next time,” I told my neighbor after interrupting her rehearsal.
examples.zh: 我打断了邻居的排练后，告诉她：“「下次过来之前我会先发消息」。”

examples.en: When my cousin asked for more notice, I said, “I'll text before coming over next time.”
examples.zh: 表姐请我早点打招呼，我说：“「下次过来之前我会先发消息」。”

collocations: sure, I'll text before coming over next time
I promise I'll text before coming over next time
I'll text before coming over next time and wait for a reply

words.expression: I lost my train of thought
words.lemma: i lost my train of thought
words.zhGloss: 我一下子忘了刚才在说什么
words.enDefinition: Used when an interruption or pause makes you forget the idea you were about to continue.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我一下子忘了刚才在说什么
acceptedEnVariants: I lost my train of thought

examples.en: I lost my train of thought when the announcement came on just as I started speaking.
examples.zh: 我刚开口广播就响了，「我一下子忘了刚才在说什么」。

examples.en: I lost my train of thought, so remind me what we were discussing before the call.
examples.zh: 「我一下子忘了刚才在说什么」，提醒我通话前在讨论什么吧。

collocations: I lost my train of thought for a moment
I lost my train of thought halfway through
I lost my train of thought after the interruption

words.expression: I'm afraid I can't make it
words.lemma: i'm afraid i can't make it
words.enDefinition: a polite way to say that you cannot attend something
acceptedEnVariants: I'm afraid I can't make it

examples.en: “I'm afraid I can't make it,” I wrote in the chat for Friday's picnic.
examples.zh: 我在周五野餐的群聊里写道：“「恐怕我去不了」。”

examples.en: “I'm afraid I can't make it this Saturday,” Nia told the rest of the committee.
examples.zh: 妮娅告诉委员会的其他成员：“「这周六恐怕我去不了」。”

collocations: I'm afraid I can't make it tonight
I'm afraid I can't make it in time
I'm afraid I can't make it to dinner

words.zhGloss: 我为刚才的事感到难为情
words.enDefinition: expresses discomfort or shame about an incident, often involving one's own behaviour
acceptedZhAnswers: 我为刚才的事感到难为情

examples.en: I'm embarrassed about what happened when I walked into the wrong workshop and interrupted the speaker.
examples.zh: 我走错了工作坊，还打断了发言的人，「这事让我很难为情」。

examples.en: I'm embarrassed about what happened in front of everyone at yesterday's society meeting.
examples.zh: 昨天在社团会议上当着大伙儿发生的事，「让我很难为情」。

collocations: admit I'm embarrassed about what happened
say I'm embarrassed about what happened
I'm embarrassed about what happened yesterday

words.enDefinition: a friendly way to decline a suggestion to move from your current place

examples.en: “I'm fine where I am,” I told the usher when he offered me a closer seat.
examples.zh: 引座员问我要不要换到更靠前的座位时，我说：“「我待在这里就好」。”

examples.en: When Lee waved me over to the crowded table, I said, “I'm fine where I am.”
examples.zh: 李招手叫我去那张坐满人的桌子，我说：“「我待在这里就好」。”

collocations: honestly, I'm fine where I am
I'm fine where I am for now
thanks, I'm fine where I am

words.zhGloss: 承蒙看重，真是抬举我了
words.enDefinition: expresses pleasure at a compliment, invitation or sign of esteem
acceptedZhAnswers: 承蒙看重，真是抬举我了

examples.en: “I'm flattered, but I'd be happier helping backstage,” said one of the new volunteers.
examples.zh: 一位新志愿者说：“「承蒙看重，真是抬举我了」，不过我更愿意在后台帮忙。”

examples.en: When her classmates suggested she run for president, Maya said, “I'm flattered, but no.”
examples.zh: 同学建议玛雅竞选会长时，她说：“「承蒙看重，真是抬举我了」，不过我还是不参加了。”

collocations: I'm genuinely flattered
I'm flattered by the invitation
I'm flattered that you asked

words.expression: I'm glad you told me before I booked
words.lemma: i'm glad you told me before i booked
words.zhGloss: 还好你在我预订之前告诉了我
words.enDefinition: a way to appreciate an early refusal or change before a booking was made
acceptedZhAnswers: 还好你在我预订之前告诉了我
acceptedEnVariants: I'm glad you told me before I booked

examples.en: When Lee backed out, I replied, “I'm glad you told me before I booked.”
examples.zh: 李决定不去了，我回道：“「还好你在我预订之前告诉了我」。”

examples.en: “I'm glad you told me before I booked,” Mina said when we said we couldn't go.
examples.zh: 我们说周末不能去住度假屋后，米娜说：“「还好你在我预订之前告诉了我」。”

collocations: I'm glad you told me before I booked the room
really, I'm glad you told me before I booked
I'm glad you told me before I booked anything

words.expression: I'm going to say no on this one
words.lemma: i'm going to say no on this one
words.enDefinition: a conversational way to give a clear decision on a particular invitation or request
acceptedEnVariants: I'm going to say no on this one

examples.en: After checking the rehearsal dates, I replied, “I'm going to say no on this one.”
examples.zh: 看过排练日期后，我回道：“「这次我还是说不吧」。”

examples.en: “I'm going to say no on this one,” Ari told the friends planning a surprise performance.
examples.zh: 阿里告诉正筹划惊喜演出的朋友们：“「这次我还是说不吧」。”

collocations: I think I'm going to say no on this one
sorry, I'm going to say no on this one
I'm going to say no on this one for now

words.expression: I'm going to stick with my answer
words.lemma: i'm going to stick with my answer
words.zhGloss: 我还是坚持原来的答复
words.enDefinition: a way to say that your decision will remain the same after another request
acceptedZhAnswers: 我还是坚持原来的答复
acceptedEnVariants: I'm going to stick with my answer

examples.en: “I'm going to stick with my answer,” I told Jo when she offered to change the venue.
examples.zh: 乔说可以换场地，我说：“「我还是坚持原来的答复」。”

examples.en: They brought up the extra shift again, and Pat said, “I'm going to stick with my answer.”
examples.zh: 他们又提起那个额外的班次，帕特说：“「我还是坚持原来的答复」。”

collocations: thanks for asking, but I'm going to stick with my answer
for this month, I'm going to stick with my answer
I'm afraid I'm going to stick with my answer

words.enDefinition: a way to say that you are avoiding an early commitment while considering alternatives

examples.en: “I'm keeping my options open,” I told my classmates when they asked about the summer trip.
examples.zh: 同学问起暑期旅行时，我说：“「我还想保留其他选择」。”

examples.en: In the chat about next year's flats, Lea wrote, “I'm keeping my options open.”
examples.zh: 在聊明年租房的群里，莉娅写道：“「我还想保留其他选择」。”

collocations: I'm keeping my options open for now
for the summer, I'm keeping my options open
I'm keeping my options open until I hear back

words.enDefinition: Say which option currently seems better while leaving room for change

examples.en: I'm leaning toward Tuesday because more people can turn up after that lecture.
examples.zh: 「我比较倾向于」周二，因为那节课下课后能来的人更多。

examples.en: After looking at both designs, I'm leaning toward the one we can put up ourselves.
examples.zh: 看过两个设计后，「我比较倾向于」我们自己就能布置好的那个。

collocations: I'm leaning toward the simpler option
I'm leaning toward keeping it
I'm leaning toward a later start

words.enDefinition: a statement that you will leave if an unwelcome behavior continues

examples.en: “I'm leaving if this continues,” I said when the group kept joking about my refusal.
examples.zh: 大家还在拿我的拒绝开玩笑时，我说：“「再这样下去我就离开」。”

examples.en: When the conversation got personal again, the volunteer told us, “I'm leaving if this continues.”
examples.zh: 谈话又扯到私事时，那位志愿者对我们说：“「再这样下去我就离开」。”

collocations: look, I'm leaving if this continues
honestly, I'm leaving if this continues
I've had enough, and I'm leaving if this continues

words.enDefinition: a way to express unease and withhold agreement

examples.en: “I'm not comfortable with that,” I said when my classmate suggested posting our private chat.
examples.zh: 同学提议把我们的私聊贴出去，我说：“「那样我会不自在」。”

examples.en: When a stranger asked to film me, I replied, “I'm not comfortable with that.”
examples.zh: 一个陌生人问能不能拍我，我回道：“「那样我会不自在」。”

collocations: honestly, I'm not comfortable with that
I'm not comfortable with that arrangement
I'm not comfortable with that at all

words.expression: I'm not committing to a regular slot
words.lemma: i'm not committing to a regular slot
words.zhGloss: 我不承诺固定时段参加
words.enDefinition: a way to make clear that one instance will not become an ongoing booking or duty
acceptedZhAnswers: 我不承诺固定时段参加
acceptedEnVariants: I'm not committing to a regular slot

examples.en: “I'm not committing to a regular slot,” I told the coordinator after helping with check-in once.
examples.zh: 帮忙签到一次后，我告诉协调员：“「我不承诺固定时段参加」。”

examples.en: “I'm not committing to a regular slot,” Luis said when the station asked him to present weekly.
examples.zh: 电台问路易斯能不能每周主持节目，他说：“「我不承诺固定时段参加」。”

collocations: I'm not committing to a regular slot this term
I can try it, but I'm not committing to a regular slot
for now, I'm not committing to a regular slot

words.enDefinition: a way to turn down alcohol during an evening event

examples.en: “I'm not drinking tonight,” I told the server when she came around with a wine list.
examples.zh: 服务员拿来酒单时，我说：“「我今晚不喝酒」。”

examples.en: When my flatmate handed me a beer, I said, “I'm not drinking tonight, thanks.”
examples.zh: 室友递给我一瓶啤酒时，我说：“谢谢，「我今晚不喝酒」。”

collocations: I'm not drinking tonight, thanks
I'm not drinking tonight, but I'll have a soda
say “I'm not drinking tonight” when offered a beer

words.expression: I'm not proud of how I acted
words.lemma: i'm not proud of how i acted
words.zhGloss: 我为自己当时的做法感到惭愧
words.enDefinition: acknowledges that the way one behaved did not meet one's own standards
acceptedZhAnswers: 我为自己当时的做法感到惭愧
acceptedEnVariants: I'm not proud of how I acted

examples.en: I'm not proud of how I acted when we disagreed about the rehearsal space.
examples.zh: 我们对排练场地有分歧时，「我为自己当时的做法感到惭愧」。

examples.en: I'm not proud of how I acted, and I want to hear your side now.
examples.zh: 「我为自己当时的做法感到惭愧」，现在想听听你的看法。

collocations: acknowledge I'm not proud of how I acted
say I'm not proud of how I acted
I'm not proud of how I acted yesterday

words.expression: I'm not up for going out tonight
words.lemma: i'm not up for going out tonight
words.enDefinition: an informal way to say that you do not feel like going out this evening
acceptedEnVariants: I'm not up for going out tonight

examples.en: “I'm not up for going out tonight,” I told my roommates after a long lab session.
examples.zh: 实验课上了很久，我跟室友说：“「我今晚不太想出门」。”

examples.en: In the group chat, Min said, “I'm not up for going out tonight. Have fun, though!”
examples.zh: 敏在群里说：“「我今晚不太想出门」。不过你们玩得开心！”

collocations: I'm really not up for going out tonight
I'm not up for going out tonight after all
I'm just not up for going out tonight

words.expression: I'm okay with a photo, but please don't post it
words.lemma: i'm okay with a photo, but please don't post it
words.zhGloss: 可以拍照，但请别发出去
words.enDefinition: a way to allow a photo while refusing permission for it to be posted
acceptedZhAnswers: 可以拍照，但请别发出去
acceptedEnVariants: I'm okay with a photo, but please don't post it

examples.en: As they set up the camera, I said, “I'm okay with a photo, but please don't post it.”
examples.zh: 大家摆好相机时，我说：“「可以拍照，但请别发出去」。”

examples.en: “I'm okay with a photo, but please don't post it,” Nia told the other volunteers.
examples.zh: 妮娅告诉其他志愿者：“「可以拍照，但请别发出去」。”

collocations: I'm okay with a photo, but please don't post it online
I'm okay with a photo, but please don't post it publicly
just to be clear, I'm okay with a photo, but please don't post it

words.enDefinition: an apology for something you did that hurt another person's feelings

examples.en: I'm sorry I hurt you when I dismissed your suggestion in front of the group.
examples.zh: 我当着小组的面没把你的建议当回事，「抱歉我伤害了你」。

examples.en: I'm sorry I hurt you, and I'll listen if you want to tell me more.
examples.zh: 「抱歉我伤害了你」，如果你愿意多说一点，我会听。

collocations: say I'm sorry I hurt you
I'm sorry I hurt you with that joke
I'm sorry I hurt you yesterday

words.expression: I'm sorry you had to deal with that
words.lemma: i'm sorry you had to deal with that
words.zhGloss: 你还得应付那件事，真不好受
words.enDefinition: expresses sympathy or regret that someone had to handle an unpleasant situation
acceptedZhAnswers: 你还得应付那件事，真不好受
acceptedEnVariants: I'm sorry you had to deal with that

examples.en: I'm sorry you had to deal with that while I was away at the conference.
examples.zh: 我离开去参加会议时，「你还得应付那件事，真不好受」。

examples.en: I'm sorry you had to deal with that on top of finishing your own project.
examples.zh: 你还得完成自己的项目，又得「应付那件事，真不好受」。

collocations: I'm sorry you had to deal with that alone
I'm sorry you had to deal with that on your first day
I'm really sorry you had to deal with that

words.enDefinition: Used when correcting a word or detail you said incorrectly in the first place.

examples.en: I meant to say Thursday when we were discussing which day to move the chairs.
examples.zh: 我们讨论哪天搬椅子时，「我本来想说的是」周四。

examples.en: I meant to say upstairs because the spare tables have already been moved from here.
examples.zh: 「我本来想说的是」楼上，因为备用桌已经从这里搬走了。

collocations: I meant to say Thursday
I meant to say the other one
I meant to say downstairs

words.enDefinition: Used to acknowledge that your interpretation may have been mistaken.

examples.en: I might have misunderstood the last point about sharing the shelf with the other flat.
examples.zh: 关于跟另一户共用架子的最后一点，「我可能理解错了」。

examples.en: I might have misunderstood what you meant when you said everyone could leave early.
examples.zh: 你说大家都能早点走时，「我可能理解错了」你的意思。

collocations: I might have misunderstood the last point
I might have misunderstood your message
I might have misunderstood what you meant

words.enDefinition: Used when you realise you heard different words from the ones someone actually said.

examples.en: I misheard you and wrote down room forty instead of room fourteen on the notice.
examples.zh: 「我听错了你的话」，在通知上写成了四十号房，实际是十四号。

examples.en: I think I misheard you when you said how far the station was from here.
examples.zh: 你说车站离这里多远时，我想「我听错了你的话」。

collocations: I think I misheard you
I misheard you the first time
I misheard you over the noise

words.enDefinition: a way to decline an evening activity because you want a peaceful evening

examples.en: “I need a quiet evening,” I told my neighbors when they invited me upstairs for games.
examples.zh: 邻居邀我上楼玩游戏时，我说：“「我晚上想清静一下」。”

examples.en: Ben turned down the trip to the pub, saying, “I need a quiet evening.”
examples.zh: 本婉拒了去酒吧的邀约，说：“「我晚上想清静一下」。”

collocations: I really need a quiet evening
I need a quiet evening at home
I need a quiet evening after work

words.enDefinition: asks for temporary distance or reduced contact, often after an upsetting interaction

examples.en: I need some space tonight, so let's talk about what happened after class tomorrow.
examples.zh: 今晚「我需要一点独处空间」，发生的事明天下课后再谈吧。

examples.en: I need some space before I can talk calmly about how the meeting went.
examples.zh: 「我需要一点独处空间」，之后才能平静地聊那场会议。

collocations: I need some space for a while
I need some space right now
say I need some space

words.expression: I need to check my schedule first
words.lemma: i need to check my schedule first
words.enDefinition: a way to delay a commitment until you know whether you are available
acceptedEnVariants: I need to check my schedule first
I need to check my timetable first

examples.en: “I need to check my schedule first,” I told my tutor when she suggested a Saturday workshop.
examples.zh: 辅导老师提议周六办工作坊时，我说：“「我得先看看日程」。”

examples.en: When the group asked me to drive, I said, “I need to check my schedule first.”
examples.zh: 小组问我能不能开车，我说：“「我得先看看日程」。”

collocations: I need to check my schedule first, but it sounds fun
let me check my schedule first
I need to check my schedule first before I say yes

words.expression: I need to focus on my own work
words.lemma: i need to focus on my own work
words.enDefinition: a way to decline extra tasks because your own work needs your attention
acceptedEnVariants: I need to focus on my own work

examples.en: “I need to focus on my own work,” I told a classmate who wanted help editing.
examples.zh: 一位同学想请我帮忙编辑，我说：“「我得专心做自己的事」。”

examples.en: When someone suggested extra studio shifts, I said, “I need to focus on my own work.”
examples.zh: 有人提议加几轮工作室值班，我说：“「我得专心做自己的事」。”

collocations: right now, I need to focus on my own work
I need to focus on my own work this week
I need to focus on my own work first

words.expression: I need to keep that evening free
words.lemma: i need to keep that evening free
words.enDefinition: a way to refuse a plan while leaving that evening unbooked
acceptedEnVariants: I need to keep that evening free

examples.en: “I need to keep that evening free,” I said when my classmate suggested tickets for Thursday.
examples.zh: 同学提议买周四的票时，我说：“「那天晚上我得空出来」。”

examples.en: “I need to keep that evening free in case my lab runs late,” said Eli.
examples.zh: 伊莱说：“「那天晚上我得空出来」，以防我在实验室待到很晚。”

collocations: I need to keep that evening free for revision
I need to keep that evening free for now
I need to keep that evening free in case something comes up

words.expression: I need to report a problem
words.lemma: i need to report a problem
words.enDefinition: A way to say you need to tell staff about something that went wrong.
acceptedEnVariants: I need to report a problem

examples.en: I need to report a problem with the room booking for our rehearsal tonight.
examples.zh: 关于我们今晚排练用的房间预订，「我需要反映一个问题」。

examples.en: I need to report a problem with the door scanner before the next group arrives.
examples.zh: 下一组人到之前，「我需要反映一个问题」，是门口刷卡机的故障。

collocations: I need to report a problem with my booking
I need to report a problem with the service
I need to report a problem at the desk

words.enDefinition: acknowledges that one's reaction was more intense than the situation called for

examples.en: I overreacted when you told me the meeting had moved to the smaller room.
examples.zh: 你告诉我会议改到较小的房间时，「我反应过头了」。

examples.en: I overreacted, and I should have waited to hear what the organiser had said.
examples.zh: 「我反应过头了」，我应该先听听组织者是怎么说的。

collocations: admit I overreacted
say I overreacted
I overreacted a little

words.enDefinition: acknowledges that the other person deserves to know why something happened or what you did

examples.en: I owe you an explanation about why your name was missing from the final schedule.
examples.zh: 最终的时间表上为什么没你的名字，「我应该给你一个解释」。

collocations: I owe you an explanation for leaving
I owe you an explanation about the change
say I owe you an explanation

words.enDefinition: says plainly that the speaker wishes they had not made a remark

examples.en: I regret what I said before I had heard your side of the story.
examples.zh: 在听你讲事情经过之前我就说了那番话，「现在我很后悔」。

examples.en: I regret what I said to the volunteers during yesterday's long rehearsal for the event.
examples.zh: 「我后悔说了那番话」，就是昨天排练时我对志愿者说的那些话。

collocations: acknowledge I regret what I said
say I regret what I said
I regret what I said about your work

words.enDefinition: admits that you should have checked a detail before acting or telling someone

examples.en: I should have checked first, as the studio was already booked for the afternoon.
examples.zh: 工作室下午已经有人订了，「我应该先核实一下」。

examples.en: I should have checked first instead of sending everyone to the building we used last week.
examples.zh: 「我应该先核实一下」，而不是让大家都去上周用的那栋楼。

collocations: admit I should have checked first
I should have checked first with the tutor
I should have checked first with you

words.enDefinition: admits that your experience or knowledge should have stopped you from doing something unwise

examples.en: I should have known better than to promise a room before I had booked it.
examples.zh: 房间还没订下来就向大家保证有房间，「我本该知道那样不妥」。

examples.en: I should have known better than to assume the new students had seen the announcement.
examples.zh: 我以为新同学都看过通知，「我本该知道那样不妥」。

collocations: admit I should have known better
I should have known better than to rush
I should have known better than to assume

words.enDefinition: admits that you did not give enough attention to what someone said or advised

examples.en: I should have listened when you warned me the last bus left before eleven.
examples.zh: 你提醒我末班车十一点前就开走，「我当初应该认真听」。

examples.en: I should have listened instead of deciding I knew what the group wanted to do.
examples.zh: 「我当初应该认真听」，不该自认知道大家想怎么做。

collocations: I should have listened to you
I should have listened more carefully
admit I should have listened

words.expression: I should have told you sooner
words.lemma: i should have told you sooner
words.enDefinition: acknowledges that an important thing should have been communicated earlier
acceptedEnVariants: I should have told you sooner

examples.en: I should have told you sooner that the microphone was no longer available for rehearsal.
examples.zh: 麦克风已经没法用来排练了，「我应该早点告诉你」。

examples.en: I should have told you sooner, so you could have made another arrangement for Friday.
examples.zh: 「我应该早点告诉你」，这样你本来可以为周五另作安排。

collocations: admit I should have told you sooner
I should have told you sooner about the change
I should have told you sooner that I couldn't come

words.enDefinition: acknowledges that you regret a remark and believe it was wrong to make it

examples.en: I shouldn't have said that about your draft before hearing why you wrote it that way.
examples.zh: 在听你解释为什么那样写之前，「我不该那样说你的稿子」。

examples.en: I shouldn't have said that, especially in front of everyone else in the study group.
examples.zh: 「那话我不该说」，尤其不该当着学习小组所有人的面说。

collocations: say I shouldn't have said that
admit I shouldn't have said that
I shouldn't have said that in public

words.enDefinition: states that you accept all responsibility for a mistake or outcome

examples.en: I take full responsibility for sending the incorrect schedule to the volunteers on Monday.
examples.zh: 「我承担全部责任」，周一是我把错误的时间表发给了志愿者。

examples.en: I take full responsibility, and I've already arranged a replacement session for the students affected.
examples.zh: 「我承担全部责任」，而且已给受影响的同学安排了补上的场次。

collocations: I take full responsibility for the mistake
I take full responsibility for what happened
say I take full responsibility

words.expression: I think we have a plan
words.lemma: i think we have a plan
words.enDefinition: Indicate that the group seems to have settled what to do
acceptedEnVariants: I think we have a plan

examples.en: I think we have a plan, so I'll book the room and send everyone the details.
examples.zh: 「我想方案定了」，我去订房间，再把细节发给大家。

examples.en: Now that we know who can do each shift, I think we have a plan for Saturday.
examples.zh: 每个班次谁能上都清楚了，「我想周六的方案定了」。

collocations: I think we have a plan for Friday
I think we have a plan that works
I think we have a plan we can all support

words.enDefinition: Used to explain the meaning you originally understood from someone's words or a message.

examples.en: I took it to mean we should wait outside until someone came with the keys.
examples.zh: 「我当时理解成」我们该在外面等，直到有人带钥匙过来。

examples.zh: 下一行单独提到周五上午，所以「我当时理解成」是周四晚上。

collocations: I took it to mean tomorrow
I took it to mean both groups
I took it to mean we should wait

words.expression: I've already given you my answer
words.lemma: i've already given you my answer
words.enDefinition: a firm way to point out that a request has already been answered
acceptedEnVariants: I've already given you my answer

examples.zh: 组织者第三次来问时，我说：“「我已经给过你答复了」。”

examples.en: When my teammate pressed me about taking over, I replied, “I've already given you my answer.”
examples.zh: 队友追问我能不能接手时，我回道：“「我已经给过你答复了」。”

collocations: look, I've already given you my answer
I've already given you my answer about Friday
remember, I've already given you my answer

words.expression: I've got an early start tomorrow
words.lemma: i've got an early start tomorrow
words.enDefinition: an informal reason for declining or leaving an evening plan
acceptedEnVariants: I've got an early start tomorrow

examples.en: “I've got an early start tomorrow,” I said when my friends suggested one more round of games.
examples.zh: 朋友提议再玩一轮时，我说：“「我明早得早起」。”

examples.en: Mo turned down the late film, saying, “I've got an early start tomorrow.”
examples.zh: 莫婉拒了看午夜电影的邀约，说：“「我明早得早起」。”

collocations: I've got an early start tomorrow morning
I've got an early start tomorrow, so I'll head home
I've got an early start tomorrow for work

words.expression: I've got too much on this week
words.lemma: i've got too much on this week
words.enDefinition: an informal way of explaining that you are already too busy this week
acceptedEnVariants: I've got too much on this week

examples.en: “I've got too much on this week,” I told the committee when they asked for another volunteer.
examples.zh: 委员会问还有没有人愿意志愿帮忙，我说：“「我这周事情太多了」。”

examples.en: Ravi turned down the movie invite with a quick “I've got too much on this week.”
examples.zh: 拉维回了句“「我这周事情太多了」”，婉拒了看电影的邀请。

collocations: I'm afraid I've got too much on this week
I've got too much on this week to help
I've just got too much on this week

words.expression: I want to hear the rest
words.lemma: i want to hear the rest
words.enDefinition: Used to encourage someone to finish their story or explanation after a pause or interruption.
acceptedEnVariants: I want to hear the rest

examples.en: I want to hear the rest of the story after you finish answering the door.
examples.zh: 你去开完门回来，「后面的故事我还想听」。

examples.en: I want to hear the rest before we decide which version to put in the newsletter.
examples.zh: 决定把哪个版本放进通讯之前，「后面的内容我还想听」。

collocations: I want to hear the rest of the story
I want to hear the rest first
say I want to hear the rest

words.enDefinition: A conversational way to draw attention to a problem without opening with a formal complaint.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我想提醒您留意一件事

examples.zh: 我想「提醒您留意一件事」，和门外的指示牌有关，以免更多人排错队。

examples.en: I wanted to flag something that several of us noticed during the first session.
examples.zh: 「我想提醒您留意一件事」，第一场活动期间我们几个人都注意到了。

I wanted to flag something before we start
I wanted to flag something that happened

words.enDefinition: admits that one's behaviour was inappropriate, disrespectful or went beyond what was acceptable

examples.en: I was out of line when I criticised your work in front of the whole group.
examples.zh: 我当着整个小组的面批评你的作品，「我那样做过分了」。

examples.en: I was out of line, and you were right to tell me to stop.
examples.zh: 「我那样做过分了」，你让我停下来是对的。

collocations: admit I was out of line
say I was out of line
I was out of line yesterday

words.enDefinition: Used to clarify that words you repeated came from another person and were not your own statement.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我刚才引用的是别人的话

examples.zh: 我说小房间不适合办活动时，「刚才引用的是别人的话」。

examples.en: I was quoting someone else from the meeting, so let me explain what I actually think.
examples.zh: 「我刚才引用的是会上别人的话」，让我说说自己实际是怎么想的。

explain that I was quoting someone else

examples.en: I was thinking aloud about the seating, so there's no need to move anything yet.
examples.zh: 座位的事「我只是边想边说」，先不用挪东西。

examples.en: I was thinking aloud when I mentioned closing the side entrance after six tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我提到明天六点后关侧门时，「只是边想边说」。

collocations: I was thinking aloud about the layout
say I was thinking aloud
I was thinking aloud at the time

words.expression: I was told someone would call me
words.lemma: i was told someone would call me
words.zhGloss: 之前有人说会给我打电话
words.enDefinition: Used to remind someone that you were promised a phone call about an issue.
acceptedZhAnswers: 之前有人说会给我打电话
acceptedEnVariants: I was told someone would call me

examples.en: I was told someone would call me yesterday about the booking, but nobody rang.
examples.zh: 「之前有人说昨天会给我打电话」谈预订的事，但没人打来。

examples.zh: 关于投诉的事，「之前有人说会给我打电话」，等主管周一回来再打。

collocations: I was told someone would call me back
I was told someone would call me today
I was told someone would call me about the review

words.expression: I was wondering if you could
words.lemma: i was wondering if you could
words.enDefinition: introduces a request in a tentative and polite manner
acceptedEnVariants: I was wondering if you could

examples.en: I was wondering if you could check our bags while I find the missing notebook.
examples.zh: 「想问你能不能」帮忙看一下包，我去找不见的笔记本。

examples.en: I was wondering if you could hand this folder to my friend when she gets here.
examples.zh: 「想问你能不能」等我朋友到的时候，把这个文件夹交给她。

I was wondering if you could hold this

words.enDefinition: A way to tell someone that you had more to say when they took over the conversation.

examples.en: I wasn't finished when the others moved on to deciding what to bring on Saturday.

I wasn't finished speaking
tell them I wasn't finished

words.expression: I won't answer if you keep pushing
words.lemma: i won't answer if you keep pushing
words.zhGloss: 你再逼问我就不回答了

acceptedEnVariants: I won't answer if you keep pushing

examples.zh: 采访者重复问那个私人的问题后，我说：“「你再逼问我就不回答了」。”

examples.zh: 乔再次问起那条消息时，安娜说：“「你再逼问我就不回答了」。”

examples.zh: 同学说清楚他想保留隐私后，我说：“「我不会再问了」。”

examples.en: After Jo turned down the offer for a second time, I told her, “I won't ask again.”
examples.zh: 乔第二次拒绝了我的提议，我告诉她：“「我不会再问了」。”

I understand, and I won't ask again
I won't ask again about the trip

words.enDefinition: a way to say that you cannot host a gathering or event
acceptedEnVariants: I won't be able to host

examples.en: When asked about the reception, Nia replied, “I won't be bringing a guest this time.”
examples.zh: 被问到招待会的安排时，妮娅回复道：“「这次我不会带客人来」。”

I won't be bringing a guest after all

examples.zh: 小组完成编辑后，我写道：“「我今晚不会看消息」。周一见！”

acceptedEnVariants: I won't be staying for dinner

I won't be staying for dinner after the meeting

words.enDefinition: a clear way to say that you will not participate in an activity

examples.zh: 报名表传到我这儿时，我对队长说：“「我就不参加了」。”

examples.en: “I won't be taking part in the exhibition,” Jia wrote on the club's event form.
examples.zh: 佳在社团的活动表上写道：“「我就不参加展览了」。”

collocations: I won't be taking part this year
I won't be taking part in the competition
I won't be taking part in the discussion

words.expression: I won't hold it against you
words.lemma: i won't hold it against you
words.enDefinition: reassures someone that a past mistake will not affect how you judge or treat them
acceptedEnVariants: I won't hold it against you

examples.en: “I won't know until next week,” Ana said when her roommate asked if she was free Monday.
examples.zh: 室友问安娜周一有没有空，她说：“「我下周才会知道」。”

I won't stay overnight after the party

acceptedEnVariants: I won't try to change your mind

examples.zh: 组织者听完我的顾虑后说：“「我不会劝你改主意」。”

about the trip, I won't try to change your mind

words.enDefinition: says that you would consider another person's reaction understandable in the circumstances

I wouldn't blame you for leaving
I wouldn't blame you if you said no

collocations: I'd like to make a complaint about the service
I'd like to make a complaint in person
I'd like to make a complaint about the way I was treated

words.expression: I'd like to speak to the manager
words.lemma: i'd like to speak to the manager
words.enDefinition: A polite direct request to speak to the person responsible for a service.
acceptedEnVariants: I'd like to speak to the manager

examples.en: I'd like to speak to the manager about the way our group was treated yesterday.
examples.zh: 「我想和经理谈谈」我们小组昨天受到的对待。

examples.en: I'd like to speak to the manager in private about what happened at the entrance.
examples.zh: 关于入口发生的事，「我想和经理私下谈谈」。

collocations: I'd like to speak to the manager about this

I'd like to speak to the manager in private

examples.zh: 「如果大家都支持这个安排」，我们可以把活动移到院子里。

examples.zh: 「如果大家都同意改排练时间」，我就订晚一点的时段。

try it if everyone's on board

if I'm following you right

examples.zh: 今天下午「如果不太麻烦的话」，你能把折叠桌搬到外面吗？

ask if it isn't too much trouble

words.expression: if that's all right with you
words.lemma: if that's all right with you
words.enDefinition: asks for agreement before you carry out a suggested action
acceptedEnVariants: if that's all right with you

examples.en: I'll use the empty shelf if that's all right with you while I sort these folders.
examples.zh: 整理这些文件夹时，「如果你没意见的话」，我就用这个空架子。

examples.en: We can leave the bags by the chair if that's all right with you for now.
examples.zh: 「如果你没意见的话」，我们暂时把包放在椅子旁边。

collocations: only if that's all right with you
go ahead if that's all right with you
stay a bit if that's all right with you
