words.enDefinition: Introduce what to do if there is less time than needed

examples.en: We'll leave the second round for Friday if we're short on time after the main rehearsal.
examples.zh: 主排练后「如果时间不够」，我们就把第二轮留到周五。

examples.en: If we're short on time, we can ask just one person from each team to speak.
examples.zh: 「如果时间不够」，我们可以每组只请一个人发言。

collocations: skip the optional section if we're short on time
meet online if we're short on time
start there if we're short on time

words.expression: if you need an answer now, it's no
words.lemma: if you need an answer now, it's no
words.zhGloss: 如果现在就得答复，那我只能说不
words.enDefinition: a way to decline when someone cannot wait for a later decision
acceptedZhAnswers: 如果现在就得答复，那我只能说不
acceptedEnVariants: if you need an answer now, it's no

examples.en: “If you need an answer now, it's no,” I told the team before the roster deadline.
examples.zh: 提交名单的截止时间快到了，我对队里说：“「如果现在就得答复，那我只能说不」。”

examples.en: When the ticket office called, I said, “If you need an answer now, it's no.”
examples.zh: 售票处打来电话时，我说：“「如果现在就得答复，那我只能说不」。”

collocations: look, if you need an answer now, it's no
if you need an answer now, I'm afraid it's no
if you need an answer now, it's a no from me

words.enDefinition: makes a request conditional on someone already going that way

examples.en: Could you take this folder downstairs if you're headed that way after class today?
examples.zh: 今天下课后，「如果你正好往那边去」，能把这个文件夹带到楼下吗？

examples.en: Could you drop these keys off if you're headed that way later this afternoon?
examples.zh: 今天下午晚些时候，「如果你正好往那边去」，能把钥匙顺路送过去吗？

collocations: if you're headed that way anyway
take it along if you're headed that way
only if you're headed that way

words.expression: I'll come to that in a minute
words.lemma: i'll come to that in a minute
words.enDefinition: Used to tell someone that you will deal with the point they raised shortly.
acceptedEnVariants: I'll come to that in a minute

examples.en: I'll come to that in a minute when I explain why the main entrance is closed.
examples.zh: 「我马上会讲到那一点」，会解释正门为什么关闭。

examples.en: I'll come to that in a minute after everyone has written down the contact number.
examples.zh: 等大家记下联系电话后，「我马上会讲到那一点」。

collocations: I'll come to that in a minute when we get to the dates
say I'll come to that in a minute
promise I'll come to that in a minute

words.enDefinition: A polite way to tell someone that there is a problem before giving details.

examples.en: I'm afraid there's a problem with the guest list for this afternoon's public talk.
examples.zh: 「恐怕出了点问题」，是今天下午公开讲座的宾客名单。

examples.en: I'm afraid there's a problem with this room because none of the microphones are working.
examples.zh: 这个房间「恐怕出了点问题」，因为几个麦克风全都不能用。

collocations: I'm afraid there's a problem with the booking
I'm afraid there's a problem with the equipment
I'm afraid there's a problem with today's schedule

words.expression: I'm not satisfied with the response
words.lemma: i'm not satisfied with the response
words.enDefinition: A direct but polite way to say an answer has not addressed your concern adequately.
acceptedEnVariants: I'm not satisfied with the response

examples.en: I'm not satisfied with the response because it doesn't address why our booking was changed.
examples.zh: 「我对这个答复不满意」，因为它没说明为什么改了我们的预约。

examples.en: I'm not satisfied with the response so far, especially about the directions we were given.
examples.zh: 「我对目前的答复不满意」，尤其是有关当时给我们的指引那部分。

collocations: I'm not satisfied with the response I received
I'm not satisfied with the response so far
tell them I'm not satisfied with the response

words.enDefinition: To make a service more useful, reliable, or satisfactory for the people who use it.

examples.en: The team asked what it could do to improve the service for people arriving alone.
examples.zh: 团队问，能为独自前来的访客做些什么来「改进服务」。

examples.en: We suggested signs near both entrances to improve the service for first-time visitors next term.
examples.zh: 我们建议两个入口都设指示牌，为下学期第一次来的访客「改进服务」。

collocations: take steps to improve the service
use feedback to improve the service
look for ways to improve the service

words.enDefinition: Used to introduce what someone receives for doing or giving something

examples.en: I offered to take the early shift in exchange for their help packing up.
examples.zh: 我提出负责早班，「换他们」帮忙收拾。

examples.en: We could lend them our stands in exchange for an extra half hour of practice.
examples.zh: 我们可以借支架给他们，「换取」额外半小时的练习时间。

collocations: offer help in exchange for a later shift
agree to something in exchange for equipment
share access in exchange for help

words.enDefinition: considering what happened with knowledge that was not available at the time

examples.en: In hindsight, I should have asked why the group preferred the original plan for the event.
examples.zh: 「事后回看」，我本该问问小组为什么更喜欢原来的活动计划。

examples.en: It was a poor decision in hindsight, but we had only a minute to choose.
examples.zh: 「事后回看」，这个决定不妥，但当时我们只有一分钟来选。

collocations: seem obvious in hindsight
in hindsight it makes sense
recognise something in hindsight

words.enDefinition: Using the way you naturally express an idea without repeating someone else's exact wording.

examples.en: I'll explain it in my own words so you can check what I understood.
examples.zh: 我会「用我自己的话」解释一下，你看看我理解得对不对。

examples.en: I tried to repeat the instructions in my own words while we walked home.
examples.zh: 走回家时，我试着「用我自己的话」复述那些指示。

collocations: explain it in my own words
say it in my own words
repeat the directions in my own words

words.enDefinition: Using ordinary words that a person without specialist knowledge can understand.

examples.en: Could you explain it in plain language before we share it with the rest of the group?
examples.zh: 发给小组其他人前，你能「用通俗的话」解释一下吗？

examples.en: I asked for the rule in plain language because the notice used several technical terms.
examples.zh: 通知用了几个专业术语，所以我请对方「用通俗的话」讲讲这条规定。

collocations: say it in plain language
explain something in plain language
rewrite it in plain language

words.enDefinition: Kept available for later instead of being used right away

examples.en: We can keep the smallest room in reserve in case we run out of space.
examples.zh: 我们可以把最小的房间「留作备用」，以免地方不够。

examples.en: If both groups have enough people, let's keep two volunteers in reserve for tonight.
examples.zh: 两组人手如果都够，我们就给晚上的活动「留两位志愿者备用」。

collocations: keep a room in reserve
hold equipment in reserve
have some supplies in reserve

words.enDefinition: A question used to ask someone to explain the particular meaning of an expression in context.

examples.en: In what sense is the new room better if it fits fewer people than before?
examples.zh: 新房间能容纳的人少些，「在哪方面」说它更好呢？

examples.en: Could you explain in what sense this door is the main entrance for visitors?
examples.zh: 你能解释一下「在哪种意义上」这扇门算访客的正门吗？

collocations: in what sense is it different
in what sense do you mean it
ask in what sense

words.enDefinition: Extra trouble, delay, or difficulty caused by a situation.

examples.en: The change caused inconvenience for visitors who had already arranged transport to the old venue.
examples.zh: 变更给已经安排好交通前往原场馆的访客造成了「不便」。

examples.en: We mentioned the inconvenience of coming back a second time to collect the same pass.
examples.zh: 我们提到，为领取同一张通行证再跑一趟很「不便」。

collocations: cause inconvenience
avoid unnecessary inconvenience
acknowledge the inconvenience

words.enDefinition: Information about progress provided while work on a matter is still continuing.

examples.en: I asked for an interim update while the venue was still checking the booking records.
examples.zh: 场馆还在核查预约记录时，我请他们给一份「阶段性进展说明」。

examples.en: The complaints officer sent an interim update to explain why the review was taking longer.
examples.zh: 投诉处理专员发来「阶段性进展说明」，解释这次复核为何耗时更久。

collocations: send an interim update
request an interim update
provide an interim update

words.expression: is it all right if I stay a bit longer
words.lemma: is it all right if i stay a bit longer
words.enDefinition: asks whether remaining in a place for longer is acceptable
acceptedEnVariants: is it all right if I stay a bit longer

examples.en: Is it all right if I stay a bit longer to finish putting these books away before lunch?
examples.zh: 午饭前我想把这些书收好，「我可以多待一会儿吗」？

examples.en: Is it all right if I stay a bit longer, or do you need to lock up now?
examples.zh: 「我可以多待一会儿吗」？还是你现在需要锁门？

collocations: so is it all right if I stay a bit longer
is it all right if I stay a bit longer today
ask if it is all right if I stay a bit longer

words.expression: is it okay if I do it later
words.lemma: is it okay if i do it later
words.enDefinition: asks for permission to complete a requested task later
acceptedEnVariants: is it okay if I do it later

examples.en: Is it okay if I do it later after I take these books back to the library?
examples.zh: 我把这些书还到图书馆之后再做，「晚点做可以吗」？

examples.en: Is it okay if I do it later? I promised to help my roommate with something first.
examples.zh: 「我晚点做可以吗」？我答应先帮室友做点事。

collocations: is it okay if I do it later this evening
ask if it is okay if I do it later
is it okay if I do it later today

words.expression: is it okay to use my own
words.lemma: is it okay to use my own
words.enDefinition: asks whether you may use your own item instead
acceptedEnVariants: is it okay to use my own

examples.en: Is it okay to use my own for the drawing? The pencils on the table are blunt.
examples.zh: 这幅画「可以用我自己的吗」？桌上的铅笔都钝了。

examples.en: Is it okay to use my own if it does the same job as the one provided?
examples.zh: 如果和你们提供的那个功能一样，「可以用我自己的吗」？

collocations: is it okay to use my own here
is it okay to use my own for this
ask if it is okay to use my own

words.enDefinition: checks whether a single item meets the other person's need

examples.en: Is one enough, or would you like two copies for your group?
examples.zh: 「一个够吗」？还是你希望给你们组两份？

examples.en: Is one enough to hold the doors, or should I get another?
examples.zh: 用来挡门，「一个够吗」？还是我再拿一个？

collocations: is one enough for the group
is one enough for each table
ask if one is enough

words.enDefinition: A question asking whether your summary represents the other person's meaning adequately and fairly.

examples.en: Is that a fair summary of your point about why we should start with the chairs?
examples.zh: 关于为什么应该先搬椅子，你的看法我「这样概括准确吗」？

examples.en: Is that a fair summary of what happened before the others came into the room?
examples.zh: 其他人进房间前发生的事，「这样概括准确吗」？

collocations: is that a fair summary of your point
is that a fair summary of what happened
ask is that a fair summary

words.expression: is that a zero or the letter O
words.lemma: is that a zero or the letter o
words.enDefinition: A question for telling the similar-looking digit 0 and letter O apart in a written string.
acceptedEnVariants: is that a zero or the letter O

examples.en: Is that a zero or the letter O at the end of the reference number?
examples.zh: 查询编号最后一位「是零还是字母 O」？

examples.en: Is that a zero or the letter O beside the first dash in the code?
examples.zh: 代码里第一道短横线旁边「是零还是字母 O」？

collocations: is that a zero or the letter O in your code
ask is that a zero or the letter O
is that a zero or the letter O at the end

words.expression: is that all you need me to do
words.lemma: is that all you need me to do
words.enDefinition: checks whether the task just described is the whole request
acceptedEnVariants: is that all you need me to do

examples.en: Is that all you need me to do, or should I check the other boxes as well?
examples.zh: 「我只需要做这些吗」？还是也要核对剩下的箱子？

examples.en: Is that all you need me to do before we return everything to the group that lent it?
examples.zh: 把东西都还给借给我们的那组之前，「我只需要做这些吗」？

collocations: so is that all you need me to do
is that all you need me to do today
ask if that is all you need me to do

words.expression: is that one word or two
words.lemma: is that one word or two
words.zhGloss: 那是一个词还是两个词
words.enDefinition: A question asking whether something should be written together or with a space.
acceptedZhAnswers: 那是一个词还是两个词
acceptedEnVariants: is that one word or two

examples.en: Is that one word or two when I write the club name on the sign?
examples.zh: 我把俱乐部名写到指示牌上时，「那是一个词还是两个词」？

examples.en: Is that one word or two in the name of the meeting room upstairs?
examples.zh: 楼上会议室的名字里，「那是一个词还是两个词」？

collocations: is that one word or two on the label
is that one word or two in writing
ask is that one word or two

words.enDefinition: A question checking whether something just mentioned is the one already discussed.

examples.en: Is that the same one that had a yellow sticker on the lid yesterday?
examples.zh: 「那是同一个吗」，就是昨天盖子上贴着黄色贴纸的那个？

examples.en: Is that the same one you set aside for me after the meeting last week?
examples.zh: 「那是同一个吗」，就是上周开完会你给我留的那个？

collocations: is that the same one you showed me earlier
is that the same one on the list
is that the same one as before

words.enDefinition: A question asking whether a letter in a word or name should be uppercase.

examples.en: Is that with a capital M when I write the name on the envelope?
examples.zh: 我在信封上写名字时，「M 要用大写吗」？

examples.en: Is that with a capital at the start, or should I copy the lowercase version?
examples.zh: 「那里要用大写字母开头吗」，还是我照抄小写的版本？

collocations: is that with a capital at the start
is that with a capital M
ask is that with a capital

words.enDefinition: A question checking whether a word or name is written with a hyphen.

examples.en: Is there a hyphen between the two words on the name tag you ordered?
examples.zh: 你订的名牌上，两个词「中间有连字符吗」？

examples.en: Is there a hyphen in the street name, or do I write it as one word?
examples.zh: 街道名里「有连字符吗」，还是应该连起来写成一个词？

collocations: is there a hyphen between the words
is there a hyphen in the name
ask is there a hyphen

words.expression: is there a limit on how many I can take
words.lemma: is there a limit on how many i can take
words.enDefinition: asks whether there is a maximum number of items you may take
acceptedEnVariants: is there a limit on how many I can take

examples.en: Is there a limit on how many I can take? Our group needs enough paper for five sketches.
examples.zh: 「我最多能拿几个」？我们组得拿够五张草图用的纸。

examples.en: Is there a limit on how many I can take from that stack beside the printer?
examples.zh: 打印机旁那摞材料，「我最多能拿几个」？

collocations: ask if there is a limit on how many I can take
is there a limit on how many I can take today
is there a limit on how many I can take at once

words.expression: is this space free to use
words.lemma: is this space free to use
words.enDefinition: asks whether an area is available for someone to use
acceptedEnVariants: is this space free to use

examples.en: Is this space free to use while our group waits for its classroom to open?
examples.zh: 我们的教室还没开门，等着时「这片地方可以用吗」？

examples.en: Is this space free to use, or is somebody coming back with their books later?
examples.zh: 「这片地方可以用吗」？还是待会儿有人要带着书回来？

collocations: is this space free to use now
is this space free to use for a while
ask if this space is free to use

words.enDefinition: to deliver a formal apology, often on behalf of an organisation or publicly

examples.en: The society chose to issue an apology after leaving two volunteers off the programme.
examples.zh: 节目单漏了两名志愿者的名字，社团决定「发表正式道歉」。

examples.en: The department agreed to issue an apology when it discovered the notice had misled students.
examples.zh: 系里发现通知误导了学生，同意「发表正式道歉」。

collocations: issue an apology promptly
issue an apology to those affected
decide to issue an apology

words.enDefinition: informally explains that you forgot something you had intended to do or remember

examples.en: I meant to return the key yesterday, but it slipped my mind after class.
examples.zh: 我本来打算昨天还钥匙，可一下课「我一时忘了」。

examples.en: It slipped my mind that I'd promised to bring the markers for our poster session.
examples.zh: 「我一时忘了」答应过要带海报展示用的记号笔。

collocations: admit it slipped my mind
it completely slipped my mind
it slipped my mind after class

words.enDefinition: Used to report an uncertain impression of what words someone said.

examples.en: It sounded like you said fifteen minutes, but I couldn't tell over the announcement.
examples.zh: 「听起来你像是在说」十五分钟，但广播太响，我不敢确定。

examples.en: It sounded like you said north gate, so I wanted to check before we started walking.
examples.zh: 「听起来你像是在说」北门，所以出发走过去之前我想确认一下。

collocations: it sounded like you said Tuesday
it sounded like you said the other entrance
it sounded like you said something else

words.expression: it was kind of you to ask
words.lemma: it was kind of you to ask
words.enDefinition: a warm way to acknowledge an invitation or request before declining
acceptedEnVariants: it was kind of you to ask
that's very kind of you to ask

examples.en: “It was kind of you to ask,” she said, handing back the dinner invitation.
examples.zh: 她把晚餐邀请函还了回去，说：“「谢谢你特地来问我」。”

examples.en: “It was kind of you to ask, but I won't be joining the panel.”
examples.zh: “「谢谢你特地来问我」，不过我不会参加这场座谈。”

collocations: open with “it was kind of you to ask”
it's really kind of you to ask
it was kind of you to ask me

words.enDefinition: acknowledges that your treatment of another person was unjust or unreasonable

examples.en: It was unfair of me to blame you for a decision the committee made together.
examples.zh: 决定是委员会一起做的，我却怪你，「那样做对你不公平」。

examples.en: It was unfair of me to expect you to stay late without asking you first.
examples.zh: 没先问你就指望你多留一会儿，「那样做对你不公平」。

collocations: it was unfair of me to assume
it was unfair of me to say that
admit it was unfair of me

words.enDefinition: promises or assures someone that a mistake or problem will not be repeated

examples.en: I've corrected the invitation list, and it won't happen again at the next meeting.
examples.zh: 我已更正邀请名单，下次开会「不会再发生这种事了」。

examples.en: It won't happen again now that both of us will check the room booking.
examples.zh: 现在我们两个人都会核对房间预约，「不会再发生这种事了」。

collocations: promise it won't happen again
say it won't happen again
make sure it won't happen again

words.expression: it's hard to plan around that
words.lemma: it's hard to plan around that
words.zhGloss: 遇到这种情况很难安排
words.enDefinition: Used to explain that a problem or uncertainty makes it difficult to organise your own plans.
acceptedZhAnswers: 遇到这种情况很难安排
acceptedEnVariants: it's hard to plan around that

examples.en: When the last bus leaves at different times each day, it's hard to plan around that.
examples.zh: 每天末班车的发车时间都不同，「遇到这种情况很难安排」。

examples.en: I told the desk that it's hard to plan around that when several people need a lift.
examples.zh: 我跟服务台说，好几个人都指望搭车，「遇到这种情况很难安排」。

collocations: say it's hard to plan around that
it's hard to plan around that much uncertainty
explain why it's hard to plan around that

words.enDefinition: Used to tell someone that you have brought the same issue to someone's attention before.

examples.en: I've already raised this with reception, but the details on the notice are still wrong.
examples.zh: 「我已经向接待处反映过这件事」，但通知上的信息仍然有误。

examples.en: I've already raised this once, so could you check who was supposed to reply to me?
examples.zh: 「我已经反映过这件事」，能麻烦您查一下本来该由谁回复我吗？

collocations: I've already raised this with reception
I've already raised this once
I've already raised this by phone

words.expression: jump in if I'm missing something
words.lemma: jump in if i'm missing something
words.zhGloss: 我有遗漏的话就请补充
words.enDefinition: An invitation for people to interrupt briefly if important information is being left out.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我有遗漏的话就请补充
acceptedEnVariants: jump in if I'm missing something

examples.en: Jump in if I'm missing something important as I explain the directions to everyone.
examples.zh: 我在给大家说明路线时，「我有遗漏的话就请补充」。

examples.en: Jump in if I'm missing something about the timings when I repeat the plan.
examples.zh: 我复述计划时，「如果我漏了什么时间点，就请补充」。

collocations: jump in if I'm missing something important
jump in if I'm missing something about the timings
tell the others to jump in if I'm missing something

words.enDefinition: An opening that signals you want to ask something briefly without taking much time.

examples.en: Just a quick question before you leave, what time does the last bus go?
examples.zh: 你走之前，「我就问一句」，最后一班车几点发车？

examples.en: Just a quick question about this step, should I leave the space under my name blank?
examples.zh: 关于这一步「我就问一句」，名字下面那格需要留空吗？

collocations: just a quick question about the date
just a quick question before you leave
just a quick question about this step

words.expression: just leave it where you found it
words.lemma: just leave it where you found it
words.enDefinition: asks someone to leave an item in its original place afterward
acceptedEnVariants: just leave it where you found it

examples.en: You can read the booklet, but just leave it where you found it when you're done.
examples.zh: 这本小册子可以看，「用完就放回原处」。

examples.en: My roommate said, "Just leave it where you found it," when I borrowed the spare adapter.
examples.zh: 我借备用转换插头时，室友说：「用完就放回原处」。

collocations: use it and just leave it where you found it
say just leave it where you found it
please just leave it where you found it

words.expression: just tell me what needs doing
words.lemma: just tell me what needs doing
words.enDefinition: expresses willingness to help once the other person specifies the task
acceptedEnVariants: just tell me what needs doing

examples.en: Just tell me what needs doing and I'll get started while you sort those papers.
examples.zh: 「就告诉我该做什么」，你整理文件时我就能动手。

examples.en: I said, "Just tell me what needs doing," when I arrived to help set up chairs.
examples.zh: 我到场帮忙摆椅子时说：「就告诉我该做什么」。

collocations: go ahead and just tell me what needs doing
ask them to just tell me what needs doing
please just tell me what needs doing

words.enDefinition: grants or requests an exception that will not usually be repeated

examples.en: You can borrow it just this once because yours doesn't arrive until tomorrow.
examples.zh: 你的明天才送到，这次可以借给你，「就这一次」。

examples.en: We agreed to leave the boards overnight just this once after the rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练后我们同意把板子在这儿放一晚，「就这一次」。

collocations: allow it just this once
say yes just this once
ask for it just this once

words.enDefinition: Avoid booking a period so it can be used if needed

examples.en: Could we keep a slot open on Thursday for anyone who misses the main rehearsal?
examples.zh: 星期四能「留个空档」给错过主要排练的人吗？

examples.en: We agreed to keep a slot open in the afternoon for the second group's setup.
examples.zh: 我们同意下午「留一个空档」给第二组做布置。

collocations: keep a slot open for volunteers
keep a slot open on Friday
agree to keep a slot open

words.zhGloss: 让两种方案都还有机会
words.enDefinition: Avoid ruling out either of two possibilities while gathering more information
acceptedZhAnswers: 让两种方案都还有机会

examples.en: Let's keep both options alive until we know which volunteers can help with setup.
examples.zh: 我们「先把两个选项都留着」，等知道哪些志愿者能来布置再定。

examples.en: We can keep both options alive by asking both groups about their plans for Friday.
examples.zh: 我们可以问问两组周五怎么安排，这样「两种方案都还有机会」。

collocations: try to keep both options alive
agree to keep both options alive
keep both options alive until Friday

words.enDefinition: A request to tell you when there are changes or progress on a matter.

examples.en: Could you keep me updated while your team checks what happened to our room booking?
examples.zh: 你们团队核查我们的房间预订时，「有进展请告诉我」，可以吗？

examples.en: Please keep me updated on the review so I know when to tell the rest of our group.
examples.zh: 关于复核的事，「有进展请告诉我」，我好知道什么时候通知小组其他人。

collocations: please keep me updated
keep me updated on any progress
keep me updated by email

words.enDefinition: to do what you told another person you would do

examples.en: You can keep your word by sending the corrected timetable before noon as you promised.
examples.zh: 按约定在中午前发出更正后的时间表，就能「说到做到」。

examples.en: In a group project, you have to keep your word if you want people to trust you.
examples.zh: 做小组项目时，如果想让别人信任你，就得「说到做到」。

collocations: always keep your word
promise to keep your word
learn to keep your word

words.enDefinition: A failure to share enough information with the people who need it.

examples.en: Our complaint focused on the lack of communication about the move to a different building.
examples.zh: 我们的投诉主要是说换楼的事情「沟通不足」。

examples.en: The lack of communication between the two desks meant we had to explain the issue twice.
examples.zh: 两个服务台之间「沟通不足」，我们不得不把问题说两遍。

collocations: complain about a lack of communication
a lack of communication between teams
explain a lack of communication

words.enDefinition: to react angrily toward someone through strong criticism, harsh words or physical action

examples.en: I watched him lash out at someone who had only offered help with the rehearsal.
examples.zh: 我看到他「猛地冲别人发泄怒气」，而那人只是主动说可以帮忙排练。

examples.en: When I feel cornered, I try to pause before I lash out at someone.
examples.zh: 觉得被逼到没退路时，我会先停一下，免得「猛地冲别人发泄怒气」。

collocations: lash out at someone in frustration
want to lash out at someone
verbally lash out at someone

words.enDefinition: To use complaints to understand what went wrong and improve future service.

examples.en: The centre held a meeting to learn from complaints about changes to its weekend classes.
examples.zh: 中心开了会，要「从投诉中吸取教训」，这些投诉涉及周末课程的变动。

examples.en: The manager said we should learn from complaints about directions before planning the next event.
examples.zh: 经理说，规划下次活动前，应该「从指引方面的投诉中吸取教训」。

collocations: seek to learn from complaints
use meetings to learn from complaints
help staff learn from complaints

words.enDefinition: To pause between comments so that other people have an opportunity to speak.

examples.en: It's helpful to leave a gap after asking a question on a crowded call.
examples.zh: 通话人多时，提问后「留出开口的空当」有助于别人回应。

examples.en: Please leave a gap between stories so anyone who wants to can join the conversation.
examples.zh: 每讲完一个故事，请「留出开口的空当」，让想参与的人也能说话。

collocations: leave a gap for someone to speak
leave a gap after a question
leave a gap before moving on

words.enDefinition: Keep a task without a named person responsible for doing it

examples.en: We may leave a task unassigned for now while we wait for two people to reply.
examples.zh: 等那两位回复的这段时间，我们可以「先不把某项任务分给具体的人」。

examples.en: Let's avoid having to leave a task unassigned by checking who is coming on Saturday.
examples.zh: 我们先确认周六谁会来，免得有「某项任务没人负责」。

collocations: leave a task unassigned for now
agree to leave a task unassigned
be careful not to leave a task unassigned

words.enDefinition: Keep enough of something available for the people using it afterwards

examples.en: Take what you need for your display, but please leave enough for the others as well.
examples.zh: 展示需要的你拿就好，也请「给其他人留足」。

examples.en: We can use some of the spare paper if we leave enough for the others.
examples.zh: 如果能「给其他人留够」，我们可以用一些备用的纸。

collocations: remember to leave enough for the others
make sure we leave enough for the others
try to leave enough for the others

words.enDefinition: To give a simpler version by not including the smaller or less important points.

examples.en: I'll leave out the details for now and just give you the three main points.
examples.zh: 我先「略去细节」，只跟你讲三个要点。

examples.en: My neighbour chose to leave out the details until we had agreed where to start.
examples.zh: 在我们确定从哪里开始前，邻居选择先「略去细节」。

collocations: leave out the details for now
leave out the details of each step
choose to leave out the details

words.enDefinition: to unexpectedly leave someone without the support they need in a difficult situation

examples.en: I promised not to leave someone in the lurch again on the day of a presentation.
examples.zh: 我答应，下次演示当天不会再把「需要帮忙的人丢下不管」。

examples.en: Cancel early if you must, so you don't leave someone in the lurch at the last minute.
examples.zh: 非取消不可的话就早点说，别到了最后一刻「丢下需要帮忙的人不管」。

collocations: leave someone in the lurch at the last minute
refuse to leave someone in the lurch
apologise for leaving someone in the lurch

words.zhGloss: 给对方留出拒绝的余地
words.enDefinition: to make a request in a way that allows the other person to say no comfortably
acceptedZhAnswers: 给对方留出拒绝的余地

examples.en: The tutor asked us to leave someone room to decline when inviting them to speak.
examples.zh: 辅导老师提醒我们，邀请别人发言时要「给对方留出拒绝的余地」。

examples.en: A private invitation can leave someone room to decline without explaining themselves to the group.
examples.zh: 私下邀请能「给对方留出拒绝的余地」，对方不用当着大家解释。

collocations: leave someone room to decline an invitation
leave someone room to decline without explanation
always leave someone room to decline

words.enDefinition: Keep a particular part of a proposal undecided for now

examples.en: Let's leave that point open until we know how many people will sign up.
examples.zh: 等知道几个人报名，我们再决定，「那一点先不定」。

examples.en: We agreed to leave that point open and settle the rest of the plan today.
examples.zh: 我们同意「暂不定那一点」，今天把计划的其余部分定下来。

collocations: let's leave that point open
leave that point open until Friday
leave that point open for now

words.enDefinition: asks someone to avoid changing the current state of something

examples.en: Could you leave this as it is while I check the position of the other chairs?
examples.zh: 我核对另外几把椅子的位置时，「这个能先保持原样」吗？

examples.en: Please leave this as it is until we know whether the labels need changing.
examples.zh: 请「先让这个保持原样」，等我们确认标签要不要换。

collocations: please leave this as it is
can we leave this as it is
decide to leave this as it is

words.enDefinition: to stop carrying anger or bitterness about unfair treatment in the past

examples.en: It took me a while to let go of resentment after being left out of decisions.
examples.zh: 之前做决定没算上我，我过了好一阵子才「放下积怨」。

examples.en: Our conversation helped me let go of resentment about how the project had ended.
examples.zh: 那次谈话让我能「放下积怨」，不再纠结项目是怎么收场的。

collocations: find it hard to let go of resentment
learn to let go of resentment
help someone let go of resentment

words.expression: let me check I've got this right
words.lemma: let me check i've got this right
words.zhGloss: 让我确认一下有没有理解对
words.enDefinition: Used when you want to repeat details in your own words to check your understanding.
acceptedZhAnswers: 让我确认一下有没有理解对
acceptedEnVariants: let me check I've got this right
let me check I got this right

examples.en: Let me check I've got this right before I put the dates on our calendar.
examples.zh: 「让我确认一下有没有理解对」，然后再把日期记到日历上。

examples.en: Let me check I've got this right, two people on each side of the display?
examples.zh: 「让我确认一下有没有理解对」，展台两边各站两个人？

collocations: let me check I've got this right first
let me check I've got this right before we go
say let me check I've got this right

words.enDefinition: A request to continue until you have finished what you are saying.

examples.en: Please let me finish before we decide who should meet the visitors downstairs tonight.
examples.zh: 决定今晚谁去楼下接访客之前，「请让我说完」。

examples.en: Let me finish this point, and then we can talk about what you would change.
examples.zh: 「让我先讲完这一点」，然后我们再谈你想改什么。

collocations: let me finish my sentence
let me finish this point
please let me finish

words.expression: let me go back a step
words.lemma: let me go back a step
words.enDefinition: Used when a speaker wants to return to an earlier stage of an explanation.
acceptedEnVariants: let me go back a step

examples.en: Let me go back a step and explain why we need two separate lists tonight.
examples.zh: 「让我退回去说上一步」，解释为什么今晚需要两个名单。

examples.en: Let me go back a step before I show you where the map changes colour.
examples.zh: 给你看地图颜色在哪里变化之前，「让我退回去说上一步」。

collocations: let me go back a step to the beginning
let me go back a step before I explain
say let me go back a step

words.expression: let me read that back to you
words.lemma: let me read that back to you
words.zhGloss: 让我把记下的内容读给你核对
words.enDefinition: Used before repeating what you wrote down to give the other person a chance to check it.
acceptedZhAnswers: 让我把记下的内容读给你核对
acceptedEnVariants: let me read that back to you

examples.en: Let me read that back to you to check I wrote the house number down correctly.
examples.zh: 「让我把记下的内容读给你核对」，看看我有没有把门牌号记对。

examples.en: Let me read that back to you before I put the address on the envelope.
examples.zh: 我把地址写到信封上之前，「让我把记下的内容读给你核对」。

collocations: let me read that back to you once
let me read that back to you for confirmation
say let me read that back to you

words.enDefinition: a conversational way to suggest closing a topic without further discussion

examples.en: After we each explained our choice, Maya said, “Let's leave it there and get lunch.”
examples.zh: 我们各自解释了自己的选择后，玛雅说：“「我们就说到这里吧」，去吃午饭。”

examples.en: “Let's leave it there,” our tutor said when the conversation returned to the same complaint.
examples.zh: 话题又转回同一条抱怨时，辅导老师说：“「我们就说到这里吧」。”

collocations: let's leave it there for now
I think let's leave it there
let's leave it there and move on

words.zhGloss: 我们待会儿再回来说这点
words.enDefinition: A suggestion to return to a particular topic later in the same conversation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们待会儿再回来说这点

examples.en: Let's come back to that after Rosa arrives, because she knows where the keys are kept.
examples.zh: 罗莎到了以后，「我们再回来说这点」吧，她知道钥匙放在哪儿。

examples.en: Let's come back to that in a moment when we've agreed how to get there.
examples.zh: 等确定怎么去那里以后，「我们待会儿再回来说这点」。

collocations: let's come back to that after the break
let's come back to that in a moment
let's come back to that when everyone is here

words.enDefinition: Write down the issues the group still needs to settle

examples.en: Can we list the outstanding points so people know what is still open for discussion?
examples.zh: 我们能「列出还没谈妥的事」吗？这样大家知道还有什么可以商量。

examples.en: Let's list the outstanding points before the room closes and we have to leave.
examples.zh: 趁房间还没关，我们先「列出未决事项」再走。

collocations: list the outstanding points in the notes
ask someone to list the outstanding points
agree to list the outstanding points

words.enDefinition: To stop following the sequence or meaning of a conversation or explanation.

examples.en: I began to lose the thread when the directions switched from street names to landmarks.
examples.zh: 路线说明从街名转到地标时，我有点「跟不上对方的思路」了。

examples.en: It's easy to lose the thread if three people tell the same story at once.
examples.zh: 三个人同时讲同一件事，很容易「跟不上谈话的思路」。

collocations: lose the thread of a story
lose the thread halfway through
lose the thread of an explanation

words.enDefinition: to become angry suddenly and stop speaking or behaving calmly

examples.en: It is easy to lose your temper when the same equipment keeps going missing.
examples.zh: 同一件器材总是不见，很容易让人「发脾气」。

examples.en: I knew you were frustrated, but I did not expect you to lose your temper.
examples.zh: 我知道你很烦，但没想到你会「发脾气」。

collocations: lose your temper with someone
try not to lose your temper
be quick to lose your temper

words.enDefinition: a method of making a decision by choosing an option that receives more than half of the relevant votes

examples.en: The club chose the earlier start time by majority vote after discussing both options.
examples.zh: 社团讨论两个选项后，通过「多数表决」选择了较早的开始时间。

examples.en: We agreed to decide by majority vote if neither schedule suited the whole group.
examples.zh: 如果两个日程都无法兼顾全组，我们商定采用「多数表决」。

collocations: approve a plan by majority vote
decide by majority vote
require a majority vote

words.enDefinition: Accept giving up part of what you wanted during a discussion

examples.en: I'm willing to make a concession on the rehearsal date if we keep both sessions.
examples.zh: 如果两场都能保留，我愿意在排练日期上「作出让步」。

examples.en: We can make a concession on the room layout if they bring more chairs.
examples.zh: 如果他们能多带些椅子，我们可以在场地布局上「让一步」。

collocations: make a concession on timing
be willing to make a concession
ask the other side to make a concession

words.enDefinition: Decide together instead of leaving the choice to just one side

examples.en: Let's make a joint decision about which parts of the display need to stay up overnight.
examples.zh: 展示里哪些东西要留到第二天，我们来「一起作决定」吧。

examples.en: Both teams wanted to make a joint decision on how to share the bigger rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 两个小组都想「一起决定」怎么共用大一点的排练室。

collocations: agree to make a joint decision
ready to make a joint decision
meet to make a joint decision

words.enDefinition: Create a schedule that shares out shifts or recurring duties

examples.en: Could we make a rota so everyone knows which morning they are doing check-in?
examples.zh: 我们能「编一张轮班表」，让每个人知道自己哪个早上负责签到吗？

examples.en: We should make a rota before asking the volunteers to pick a weekend shift.
examples.zh: 让志愿者选周末班次之前，我们应该「编一张轮班表」。

collocations: make a rota for volunteers
make a rota for the month
make a rota together

words.enDefinition: to draw a conclusion without enough evidence in a way that treats someone unfairly

examples.en: I did not want to make an unfair assumption about why he missed the meeting.
examples.zh: 我不想因为他没来开会就「对他妄下判断」。

examples.en: The tutor reminded us not to make an unfair assumption based on one quiet lesson.
examples.zh: 导师提醒我们，别因为有人一节课上没怎么说话就「对人妄下判断」。

collocations: avoid making an unfair assumption
make an unfair assumption about someone
apologise for making an unfair assumption

words.enDefinition: to do something for a person to compensate for disappointing or inconveniencing them

examples.en: I wanted to make it up to someone after forgetting their shift at the student café.
examples.zh: 我忘了帮人在学生咖啡厅顶班，想「做点事补偿对方」。

examples.en: You can make it up to someone by offering to cover a different shift next week.
examples.zh: 你可以主动提出下周替另一个班，「做点事补偿对方」。

collocations: want to make it up to someone
try to make it up to someone
offer to make it up to someone

words.expression: make the best use of what we have
words.lemma: make the best use of what we have
words.enDefinition: Get as much practical value as possible from available resources
acceptedEnVariants: make the best use of what we have

examples.en: Let's make the best use of what we have instead of borrowing another projector.
examples.zh: 我们「好好利用现有的资源」吧，先不用再借一台投影仪。

examples.en: With one room left, we'll make the best use of what we have by sharing it.
examples.zh: 只剩一个房间，我们会共用它，「善用手头的资源」。

collocations: try to make the best use of what we have
ways to make the best use of what we have
help us make the best use of what we have

words.enDefinition: to cause tension or discomfort between people who are interacting

examples.en: I worried that bringing up the old email would make things awkward before the meeting.
examples.zh: 我怕开会前提起那封旧邮件会「让场面变得尴尬」。

examples.en: You can apologise without going into details that might make things awkward for the group.
examples.zh: 你可以道歉，细节就不用说了，免得「让小组里的场面变得尴尬」。

collocations: try not to make things awkward
worry about making things awkward
make things awkward for someone

words.enDefinition: Assign duties according to people's skills, experience, or interests

examples.en: We tried to match people to roles based on what each volunteer wanted to learn.
examples.zh: 我们根据每位志愿者想学什么，尽量「给他们安排合适的分工」。

examples.en: Could we match people to roles before we decide who will need any practice time?
examples.zh: 我们能先「给大家安排适合的分工」，再看哪些人需要练习时间吗？

collocations: match people to roles based on experience
find a way to match people to roles
match people to roles that suit them

words.enDefinition: politely asks permission to enter a room or other place

examples.en: May I come in while you are packing, or should I wait outside?
examples.zh: 你在收东西时，「我可以进来吗」？还是该在外面等？

examples.en: May I come in? I left my notebook on the sill near your chair.
examples.zh: 「我可以进来吗」？我把笔记本落在你座位旁的窗台上了。

collocations: may I come in now
may I come in for a moment
ask if I may come in

words.enDefinition: A position or solution between two opposing views or preferences

examples.en: Keeping the talk online and moving the discussion outside gave us a middle ground.
examples.zh: 讲座仍在线上，讨论改到室外，这就是我们的「折中方案」。

examples.en: Keeping one late session was a middle ground between holding none and holding two.
examples.zh: 在一场晚场都不开和开两场之间，保留一场是个「折中方案」。

collocations: find a middle ground
look for a middle ground
offer a middle ground

words.enDefinition: The smallest number of people required for an activity or task

examples.en: We set a minimum headcount for the trip before asking anyone to sign up.
examples.zh: 让大家报名之前，我们先定了出行的「最低人数」。

examples.en: The workshop won't go ahead if we don't reach the minimum headcount by Monday.
examples.zh: 到周一如果还凑不够「最低人数」，工作坊就不开了。

collocations: set a minimum headcount
reach the minimum headcount
check the minimum headcount

words.enDefinition: Information that can leave people with a false impression of what is available or will happen.

examples.en: I reported misleading information on the poster because it made the evening class sound free.
examples.zh: 海报让人以为晚间课免费，所以我反映了这条「容易引起误解的信息」。

examples.en: The centre took down the notice after visitors complained that it contained misleading information.
examples.zh: 访客投诉通知上有「容易引起误解的信息」，中心随后撤下了通知。

collocations: correct misleading information
complain about misleading information
remove misleading information from a notice

words.enDefinition: Something you consider essential when choosing between possible options

examples.en: A quiet corner is a must-have for the students recording interviews.
examples.zh: 对于要录采访的同学，安静的角落是「必不可少的」。

examples.en: An outlet near each table was a must-have when we planned the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们筹办工作坊时，每张桌子附近有插座是「必不可少的」。

collocations: an absolute must-have
a must-have for our project
a list of must-haves

words.enDefinition: Suitable enough for each side to agree to the same arrangement

examples.en: We finally found a mutually acceptable time for the two teams to swap rooms.
examples.zh: 我们终于找到一个「双方都能接受的」时段，让两个小组交换房间。

examples.en: Both clubs wanted a mutually acceptable way to divide the setup and cleanup.
examples.zh: 两个社团都想找个「双方都能接受的」办法，分配布置和收拾工作。

collocations: a mutually acceptable time
a mutually acceptable solution
find mutually acceptable terms

words.enDefinition: a direct way to repeat a refusal after being asked again

examples.en: “My answer is still no,” I said after the committee made another appeal for volunteers.
examples.zh: 委员会又一次请大家自愿帮忙时，我说：“「我的答复仍然是拒绝」。”

examples.en: When my neighbors offered to drive if I changed plans, I replied, “My answer is still no.”
examples.zh: 邻居说如果我改变计划就可以开车载我，我回道：“「我的答复仍然是拒绝」。”

collocations: after thinking about it, my answer is still no
on that point, my answer is still no
thanks for asking, but my answer is still no

words.enDefinition: a brief polite expression of regret, often used in a professional exchange

examples.en: My apologies for sending the invitation to the wrong group yesterday afternoon.
examples.zh: 「抱歉」，昨天下午我把邀请发错了群。

examples.en: My apologies. I misread the time and arrived after the demonstration had already finished.
examples.zh: 「抱歉」。我看错了时间，到的时候演示已经结束了。

collocations: my apologies for the oversight
my apologies for the delay
my apologies for the confusion

words.enDefinition: a direct way to say that you do not discuss your personal money matters

examples.en: “My finances are private,” I said when a classmate asked how much my parents sent me.
examples.zh: 同学问我父母给我寄多少钱，我说：“「我的财务状况是私事」。”

examples.en: At dinner, Eli said, “My finances are private,” after someone asked how much he had saved.
examples.zh: 吃晚饭时，有人问伊莱存了多少钱，他说：“「我的财务状况是私事」。”

collocations: my finances are private, thanks
I'd rather not say, as my finances are private
my finances are private, even among friends

words.zhGloss: 我手头的事已经排满了
words.enDefinition: an idiomatic way to say that you already have enough obligations
acceptedZhAnswers: 我手头的事已经排满了

examples.en: “My plate is full,” I said when the editor proposed a second article for this issue.
examples.zh: 编辑提议我再给这期写一篇文章，我说：“「我手头的事已经排满了」。”

examples.en: When the club asked for a substitute treasurer, I replied, “My plate is full right now.”
examples.zh: 社团问有没有人能临时代任财务负责人时，我回道：“「我现在手头的事已经排满了」。”

collocations: my plate is full this semester
my plate is full at the moment
honestly, my plate is full

words.expression: narrow it down to two options
words.lemma: narrow it down to two options
words.enDefinition: Reduce the choices under consideration until only two remain
acceptedEnVariants: narrow it down to two options

examples.en: Let's narrow it down to two options before we ask the volunteers to vote on a time.
examples.zh: 请志愿者投票选时间前，我们先把范围「缩小到两个选项」。

examples.en: We can narrow it down to two options if we rule out rooms too small for six desks.
examples.zh: 排除摆不下六张桌子的房间，就能把范围「缩小到两个选项」。

collocations: can we narrow it down to two options
help us narrow it down to two options
narrow it down to two options by Friday

words.enDefinition: Comments pointing out problems, dissatisfaction, or aspects that could be improved.

examples.en: The manager received negative feedback about the new check-in system after Saturday's event.
examples.zh: 周六的活动结束后，经理收到了关于新签到系统的「负面反馈」。

examples.en: The venue thanked our group for the negative feedback and asked for a specific example.
examples.zh: 场馆感谢我们小组给出「负面反馈」，并请我们举个具体例子。

collocations: receive negative feedback
respond to negative feedback
take negative feedback seriously

words.enDefinition: The choice considered most suitable after the preferred choice

examples.en: If the hall is already taken, the courtyard is our next best option.
examples.zh: 如果大厅已经被订了，院子就是我们「仅次于首选的方案」。

examples.en: We picked the next best option instead of waiting another week for the large room.
examples.zh: 我们选了「次优方案」，省得为了大一点的房间再等一周。

collocations: choose the next best option
settle for the next best option
decide on the next best option

words.enDefinition: a reassuring response that removes any expectation that the other person give a reason

examples.en: “No explanation needed,” I told my roommate when she turned down the dinner invitation.
examples.zh: 室友婉拒晚餐邀请时，我对她说：“「不用解释」。”

examples.en: When Jo apologized for being unavailable, I replied, “No explanation needed. I'll ask someone else.”
examples.zh: 乔为抽不开身道歉时，我回道：“「不用解释」。我会问问其他人。”

collocations: no explanation needed at all
no explanation needed, honestly
no explanation needed, thanks for letting me know

words.enDefinition: a friendly expression showing or asking that there be no lasting anger after a disagreement

examples.en: No hard feelings. I know the room mix-up was hard for everyone to sort out.
examples.zh: 「我没往心里去」。我知道房间弄混了，大家都不好处理。

examples.en: We agreed there were no hard feelings after talking about how the schedule had changed.
examples.zh: 我们谈过时间表怎么改的，确认「彼此都没往心里去」。

collocations: there are no hard feelings
hope there are no hard feelings
say no hard feelings

words.enDefinition: reassures someone that you do not think an apology is necessary

examples.en: No need to apologize, we still had enough chairs before the other students arrived.
examples.zh: 「不用道歉」，其他同学到之前，椅子还是够的。

examples.en: No need to apologize for asking twice because the instructions were hard to hear.
examples.zh: 刚才说明没听清，多问一遍也「不用道歉」。

collocations: say no need to apologize
there is no need to apologize
no need to apologize for asking

words.expression: no one got back to me
words.lemma: no one got back to me
words.enDefinition: A conversational way to say that no one replied or contacted you again after you reached out.
acceptedEnVariants: no one got back to me

examples.en: I left my number with the desk on Monday, but no one got back to me.
examples.zh: 我周一把电话号码留给了服务台，但「没有人给我回音」。

examples.en: No one got back to me after I asked who could correct the booking error.
examples.zh: 我问谁能改正预订错误后，「没有人给我回音」。

collocations: no one got back to me about it
no one got back to me after my call
still no one got back to me

words.enDefinition: A way to say that the expected written entry for a complaint cannot be found.

examples.en: The new receptionist found no record of the complaint I made at the desk yesterday.
examples.zh: 新接待员查过后说，「没有我昨天在服务台提出的投诉记录」。

examples.en: I kept my copy after hearing that there was no record of the complaint on file.
examples.zh: 听说档案里「没有这次投诉的记录」后，我保留了自己的副本。

collocations: find no record of the complaint
have no record of the complaint
say there is no record of the complaint

words.enDefinition: No clear desire for one choice over the other choices

examples.en: I have no strong preference about the room, as long as we can all fit.
examples.zh: 只要地方坐得下所有人，我对用哪个房间「没有特别偏好」。

examples.en: Kim had no strong preference between the two layouts and let us choose.
examples.zh: 金对两种布局「没有特别偏好」，就让我们选了。

collocations: have no strong preference
no strong preference either way
no strong preference about the format

words.enDefinition: a statement presented as an apology that fails to express regret or recognise wrongdoing

examples.en: Several students called the statement a non-apology because it ignored the mistake entirely.
examples.zh: 几名学生说，那份声明是「没有实际道歉的说法」，因为根本没提到过错。

examples.en: His non-apology left the volunteers feeling that their concerns still had not been addressed.
examples.zh: 他那番「没有实际道歉的说法」让志愿者觉得，他们担心的问题仍未得到回应。

collocations: dismiss something as a non-apology
issue a non-apology
a carefully worded non-apology

words.enDefinition: Below the quality that should normally be provided or accepted.

examples.en: The manager agreed the cleaning was not up to standard after seeing the room herself.
examples.zh: 经理亲自看过房间后，承认清洁「不符合应有的标准」。

examples.en: I told the dentist's office that its appointment reminders were not up to standard.
examples.zh: 我告诉牙科诊所，他们的预约提醒「不符合应有的标准」。

collocations: clearly not up to standard
still not up to standard
not up to standard for public use

words.enDefinition: A way to say that what you received differs from what someone agreed to provide.

examples.en: This is not what I was promised when I booked a quiet study room.
examples.zh: 这「和答应我的不一样」，我订的是安静的自习室。

examples.en: I explained that the earlier time was not what I was promised at reception.
examples.zh: 我解释说，这个更早的时间「和接待处答应我的不一样」。

collocations: that's not what I was promised
this is not what I was promised
clearly not what I was promised

words.enDefinition: Write down which cases are handled differently under an arrangement

examples.en: Please note the exceptions before we tell the group that all shifts end at five.
examples.zh: 我们告诉小组各班次都五点结束前，请先「记下例外情况」。

examples.en: I'll note the exceptions for volunteers who can only help during the first hour.
examples.zh: 对于只能在头一小时帮忙的志愿者，我会「记下这些特殊安排」。

collocations: remember to note the exceptions
note the exceptions in the schedule
note the exceptions to the general rule

words.zhGloss: 请把这件事记入我的记录
words.enDefinition: A request to add the information just given to the written record for your appointment or case.
acceptedZhAnswers: 请把这件事记入我的记录

examples.en: Could you note this on my record so I don't have to explain it again?
examples.zh: 您能「把这件事记入我的记录」吗？这样我就不用再解释一遍了。

examples.en: Please note this on my record because the appointment was cancelled before I called today.
examples.zh: 今天我打电话之前，预约已经取消了，「请把这件事记入我的记录」。

collocations: please note this on my record
ask someone to note this on my record
could you note this on my record

words.expression: now I see what you mean
words.lemma: now i see what you mean
words.zhGloss: 现在我明白你的意思了
words.enDefinition: Used to show that additional information helped you understand the speaker's earlier point.
acceptedZhAnswers: 现在我明白你的意思了
acceptedEnVariants: now I see what you mean

examples.en: Now I see what you mean about putting all the signs at the same height.
examples.zh: 关于所有指示牌都放同一高度的事，「现在我明白你的意思了」。

examples.en: Now I see what you mean about folding the cloth before putting it away.
examples.zh: 关于把布叠好再收起来的事，「现在我明白你的意思了」。

collocations: now I see what you mean about the timing
now I see what you mean by that
say now I see what you mean

words.enDefinition: warmly gives permission for the action someone just asked about

examples.en: Of course you can. The space beside my folder is free right now.
examples.zh: 「当然可以」。我文件夹旁边那块地方现在空着。

examples.en: I said, "Of course you can," when she asked to borrow the smaller scissors.
examples.zh: 她问能不能借小一点的剪刀，我说：「当然可以」。

collocations: say of course you can
of course you can use it
of course you can stay

words.enDefinition: To suggest a way of dealing with a problem that can realistically work in the circumstances.

examples.en: Could you offer a practical solution for people who cannot return to the centre tomorrow?
examples.zh: 您能为明天没法再来中心的人「提出一个可行的解决办法」吗？

examples.en: The adviser said she could offer a practical solution once we explained what our group needed.
examples.zh: 顾问说，只要说明我们小组需要什么，她就可以「提出一个可行的解决办法」。

collocations: try to offer a practical solution
be able to offer a practical solution
ask someone to offer a practical solution

words.enDefinition: To provide a reason that helps someone understand what happened or why a decision was made.

examples.en: The organiser called to offer an explanation after we waited at the entrance for twenty minutes.
examples.zh: 我们在入口等了二十分钟后，组织者打电话「给出解释」。

examples.en: Can you offer an explanation for why our appointment was removed from the schedule yesterday?
examples.zh: 我们的预约昨天被从日程里删掉了，您能「给出解释」吗？

collocations: offer an explanation for a delay
call to offer an explanation
be able to offer an explanation

words.enDefinition: Agree to something provided one particular requirement is met

examples.en: I'll take the later shift on one condition — someone else has to stack the chairs.
examples.zh: 我上晚一点的班，「但有一个条件」。得由别人来叠放椅子。

examples.en: We can share the space on one condition — the path between the tables stays clear.
examples.zh: 我们可以共用场地，「但有一个条件」。桌子之间得留一条畅通的过道。

collocations: agree on one condition
say yes on one condition
I'd do it on one condition

words.enDefinition: Used when action will follow confirmation from each group member

examples.en: I'll book the van once everyone's confirmed that they can help with pickup on Thursday.
examples.zh: 「等所有人确认」周四能来帮忙取货，我就去订车。

examples.en: We can publish the schedule once everyone's confirmed which shift they want to take.
examples.zh: 「等所有人确认」各自想上哪个班，我们就能发布排班表了。

collocations: book the room once everyone's confirmed
send the final copy once everyone's confirmed
start once everyone's confirmed

words.enDefinition: An opening for giving a particular case that illustrates what you just said.

examples.en: One example would be the smaller gate, which is only open during the afternoon.
examples.zh: 「举个例子就是」那个小门，它只在下午开放。

examples.en: One example would be leaving the large pans on the lower shared shelf after cooking.
examples.zh: 「举个例子就是」做完饭后，把大锅放在下面的共用架子上。

collocations: one example would be the side gate
one example would be the kitchen list
say one example would be

words.enDefinition: A problem that occurred on one occasion and is not expected to recur.

examples.en: We thought it was a one-off problem until three more rooms had the same booking error.
examples.zh: 又有三间房出现同样的预订错误前，我们还以为这是「只发生一次的问题」。

examples.en: If it was a one-off problem, we can simply make another booking for next week.
examples.zh: 如果这是「只发生一次的问题」，我们直接为下周重新预订就行。

collocations: treat it as a one-off problem
check if it was a one-off problem
a minor one-off problem

words.enDefinition: Used to say that people should speak one after another so they can be heard.

examples.en: We need to speak one person at a time or the driver won't hear anyone.
examples.zh: 我们得「一次一个人说」，不然司机谁的话都听不清。

examples.en: One person at a time, please, so I can write down each person's address correctly.
examples.zh: 请「一次一个人说」，这样我能把每个人的地址记对。

collocations: let's speak one person at a time
ask for one person at a time
one person at a time, please

words.enDefinition: An arrangement with a single person assigned to each activity station

examples.en: We only need one person per station if we put the instructions on each table.
examples.zh: 如果我们把操作说明放在各桌，「每个点位一个人」就够了。

examples.en: Let's assign one person per station and ask the rest to help with the queue.
examples.zh: 我们安排「每个点位一个人」，请其他人帮忙维持队伍。

collocations: assign one person per station
need one person per station
have at least one person per station

words.expression: one thing before we move on
words.lemma: one thing before we move on
words.zhGloss: 接着说之前还有一件事
words.enDefinition: A short way to introduce a remaining point before people switch topics or start something new.
acceptedZhAnswers: 接着说之前还有一件事
acceptedEnVariants: one thing before we move on

examples.en: One thing before we move on to the next room, where should I return this key?
examples.zh: 「去下一个房间前还有一件事」，我该去哪里还这把钥匙？

examples.en: One thing before we move on, are there any extra places for Friday's trip yet?
examples.zh: 「接着说之前还有一件事」，周五的出行现在还有空位吗？

collocations: one thing before we move on to the next topic
one thing before we move on to the next item
mention one thing before we move on

words.expression: one way to do it would be
words.lemma: one way to do it would be
words.enDefinition: Introduce a possible method in a discussion about how to proceed
acceptedEnVariants: one way to do it would be

examples.en: One way to do it would be to keep the morning free and rehearse after lunch.
examples.zh: 「一种做法是」上午留空，午饭后再排练。

examples.en: One way to do it would be to sort the donations before we call the volunteers in.
examples.zh: 「一种做法是」先把捐赠物品分类，再请志愿者进来。

collocations: one way to do it would be to take turns
one way to do it would be online
one way to do it would be to share the work

words.enDefinition: Separately, saying or dealing with each word before moving on to the next one.

examples.en: Please say it one word at a time while I type the street name into the app.
examples.zh: 我把街道名输进应用时，请「一个词一个词地说」。

examples.en: She read the address one word at a time because our phone connection was weak.
examples.zh: 我们的电话信号弱，所以她「一个词一个词地」念地址。

collocations: say it one word at a time
read it one word at a time
repeat it one word at a time

words.enDefinition: State that a decision requires consent from everyone in the group

examples.en: We'll change the rehearsal date only if we all agree on a new one by Friday.
examples.zh: 「只有大家都在周五前同意新日期」，我们才改排练日期。

examples.en: Let's change the seating layout only if we all agree on where to put the spare tables.
examples.zh: 「只有大家都同意」备用桌子摆在哪里，我们才换座位布局。

collocations: go ahead only if we all agree
change the plan only if we all agree
share notes only if we all agree

words.enDefinition: limits permission to the time when the speaker is present

examples.en: You can use the scissors only while I'm here to show you how.
examples.zh: 剪刀「只在我在场时可以」用，我可以示范给你看。

examples.en: My friend said, "You can use my tablet, but only while I'm here."
examples.zh: 朋友说：「你可以用我的平板，但只在我在场时可以」。

collocations: you can use it only while I'm here
say only while I'm here
allow it only while I'm here

words.enDefinition: Say that some of the same times are free for everyone

examples.en: Let's see when our schedules overlap before we suggest any dates for the handover.
examples.zh: 提交接日期之前，我们先看看「大家什么时候都有空」。

examples.en: Tuesday is the one day when our schedules overlap enough for a full rehearsal.
examples.zh: 只有周二「大家的共同空档」够排练一整场。

collocations: see when our schedules overlap
find a time when our schedules overlap
check whether our schedules overlap

words.enDefinition: to need to apologise to someone because of something you have done

examples.en: You owe someone an apology if you blame them for a decision they never made.
examples.zh: 如果你把别人没做的决定怪到对方头上，就「欠那个人一个道歉」。

examples.en: It's easy to know you owe someone an apology and still put it off.
examples.zh: 知道自己「欠某人一个道歉」，却还是一拖再拖，这种事并不少见。

collocations: realise you owe someone an apology
admit you owe someone an apology
feel you owe someone an apology

words.enDefinition: to admit that you have done something wrong, especially after keeping quiet about it

examples.en: I decided to own up when our tutor asked who had deleted the shared table.
examples.zh: 导师问是谁删了共享表格，我决定「坦白承认过错」。

examples.en: The team agreed it was better to own up than let someone else be blamed.
examples.zh: 队友们认为，最好「坦白承认过错」，免得其他人背锅。

collocations: own up to a mistake
own up to what you did
decide to own up

words.enDefinition: Agreement on some parts of a discussion while other parts remain unresolved

examples.en: We reached partial agreement because both teams accepted the date but disagreed on the venue.
examples.zh: 我们「谈妥了部分事项」，两个小组同意这个日期，对场地还有分歧。

examples.en: Our partial agreement covers both morning shifts and leaves the afternoon open for discussion.
examples.zh: 我们「只谈妥了部分安排」，上午两个班次定了，下午的还要商量。

collocations: reach partial agreement
record a partial agreement
a partial agreement on scheduling

words.enDefinition: Used when a review supports some parts of a complaint and does not support the others.

examples.en: Our complaint was partly upheld because only one of the two concerns was supported by the records.
examples.zh: 我们的投诉「部分成立」，因为记录只支持两个问题中的一个。

examples.en: The note said “Partly upheld” and explained which part of our complaint the review accepted.
examples.zh: 通知写着「部分成立」，并说明复核认可了投诉中的哪一部分。

collocations: a partly upheld complaint
a status of partly upheld
a decision marked partly upheld

words.enDefinition: To give someone the opportunity to continue speaking after taking a turn yourself.

examples.en: I'll pass it back to you once I've explained why the first time won't work.
examples.zh: 解释完为什么第一个时间不合适，我就「再请你接着说」。

examples.en: Let me state the new date before I pass it back to you to finish.
examples.zh: 让我先说一下新日期，然后「再请你接着说」，把话说完。

collocations: I'll pass it back to you
pass it back to you after one point
pass it back to you to finish

words.enDefinition: to tell another person something someone asked you to relay

examples.en: Could you pass on a message to the person collecting the room keys?
examples.zh: 你能帮我给收房间钥匙的人「转达一条消息」吗？

examples.en: I promised to pass on a message if I saw my neighbour downstairs.
examples.zh: 我答应，如果在楼下见到邻居，就「转达一条消息」。

collocations: offer to pass on a message
ask someone to pass on a message
agree to pass on a message

words.enDefinition: To share feedback you received with someone else who can consider or act on it.

examples.en: The receptionist offered to pass on feedback about the late opening to the manager.
examples.zh: 接待员表示，会把大家对延迟开门的「反馈转达给」经理。

examples.en: Could you pass on feedback from people who had to wait outside this morning?
examples.zh: 今早有人一直在门外等，您能把他们的「反馈转达」一下吗？

collocations: pass on feedback to management
pass on feedback from visitors
agree to pass on feedback

words.enDefinition: Informal, especially in British English, for being sent from person to person without getting help.

examples.en: I felt passed from pillar to post when three different offices told me to call elsewhere.
examples.zh: 三个办公室都让我打别处的电话，我觉得自己「被来回推诿」。

examples.en: We were passed from pillar to post while trying to find out who had cancelled our booking.
examples.zh: 我们想弄清谁取消了预约，却「被来回推诿」。

collocations: feel you've been passed from pillar to post
get passed from pillar to post
tired of being passed from pillar to post

words.enDefinition: The person responsible for making decisions about a place, event, or service.

examples.en: I asked to speak to the person in charge after the desk closed without serving us.
examples.zh: 服务台还没轮到我们就关了，我要求见「负责人」。

examples.en: The person in charge explained why our group had been asked to leave the hall early.
examples.zh: 「负责人」解释了为什么有人让我们小组提前离开大厅。

collocations: speak to the person in charge
ask for the person in charge
find the person in charge

words.enDefinition: Introduce a new arrangement gradually instead of all at once

examples.en: We agreed to phase it in by trying the new rota on Thursdays first.
examples.zh: 我们说好先在周四试试新的轮班表，再「逐步引入」这套安排。

examples.en: Could we phase it in over three meetings so volunteers can get used to it?
examples.zh: 我们能用三次会议「逐步引入」这项安排，让志愿者有时间适应吗？

collocations: agree to phase it in
phase it in over several weeks
decide whether to phase it in

words.expression: pick me up on your way
words.lemma: pick me up on your way
words.enDefinition: asks someone to collect you while already travelling somewhere
acceptedEnVariants: pick me up on your way

examples.en: Could you pick me up on your way to the park if there is room?
examples.zh: 如果车上有空位，你去公园时能「路上顺便接我」吗？

examples.en: Can you pick me up on your way back from the library this evening, please?
examples.zh: 你今晚从图书馆回来时，能「路上顺便接我」吗？

collocations: can you pick me up on your way
could you pick me up on your way
pick me up on your way home

words.enDefinition: to collect one additional copy of something at the same time

examples.en: Could you pick up an extra copy of the worksheet for the person beside me?
examples.zh: 你能帮坐我旁边的同学「顺便多领一份」练习单吗？

examples.en: I offered to pick up an extra copy because my roommate was still at lunch.
examples.zh: 室友还在吃午饭，我主动说可以「顺便多领一份」。

collocations: offer to pick up an extra copy
ask someone to pick up an extra copy
remember to pick up an extra copy

words.enDefinition: a request to respect the response you have given instead of pressing for a different one

examples.en: “Please accept my answer,” I told the organizer after declining the volunteer role a second time.
examples.zh: 第二次婉拒志愿者岗位后，我对组织者说：“「请接受我的答复」。”

examples.en: When the group asked me to justify my decision, I said, “Please accept my answer.”
examples.zh: 小组要求我解释自己的决定，我说：“「请接受我的答复」。”

collocations: please accept my answer and move on
for now, please accept my answer
please accept my answer without asking me to reconsider

words.enDefinition: a polite, often formal way of asking someone to accept that you are sorry

examples.en: Please accept my apologies for sending the room number before I had checked the booking.
examples.zh: 我没核对预约就发了房间号，「请接受我的歉意」。

examples.en: Please accept my apologies for the delay in replacing the equipment we borrowed last month.
examples.zh: 我们上个月借的器材迟迟没有换好，「请接受我的歉意」。

collocations: please accept my apologies for the delay
please accept my apologies for the error
please accept my apologies for any inconvenience

words.expression: please ask me before borrowing it
words.lemma: please ask me before borrowing it
words.enDefinition: a request to get your permission each time before borrowing an item
acceptedEnVariants: please ask me before borrowing it

examples.en: As I handed over the adapter, I said, “Next time, please ask me before borrowing it.”
examples.zh: 我递过转接头时说：“「下次借用之前请先问我」。”

examples.en: “Please ask me before borrowing it,” I told my roommate after finding my bike outside.
examples.zh: 我在外面找到自行车后对室友说：“「借用之前请先问我」。”

collocations: next time, please ask me before borrowing it
even if I'm out, please ask me before borrowing it
please ask me before borrowing it again

words.enDefinition: a request to keep a message with its original recipient

examples.en: “Please don't forward my message,” I wrote after sending my friend the details privately.
examples.zh: 我私下把事情经过发给朋友后，又写道：“「请别转发我的消息」。”

examples.en: I told the tutor why I would be absent and added, “Please don't forward my message.”
examples.zh: 我告诉辅导老师我缺席的原因，又补了一句：“「请别转发我的消息」。”

collocations: please don't forward my message to the class
please don't forward my message outside this chat
please don't forward my message without checking with me

words.expression: please don't include that in the notes
words.lemma: please don't include that in the notes
words.zhGloss: 请别把那件事记进笔记
words.enDefinition: a request to omit something from written notes or a meeting record
acceptedZhAnswers: 请别把那件事记进笔记
acceptedEnVariants: please don't include that in the notes

examples.en: “Please don't include that in the notes,” I told our secretary after mentioning a private detail.
examples.zh: 我提到一件私事后告诉我们的秘书：“「请别把那件事记进笔记」。”

examples.en: When the tutor reached for her pen, I said, “Please don't include that in the notes.”
examples.zh: 辅导老师伸手拿笔时，我说：“「请别把那件事记进笔记」。”

collocations: please don't include that in the notes for the whole group
just one thing: please don't include that in the notes
please don't include that in the notes you circulate

words.zhGloss: 请别把我的位置发到网上
words.enDefinition: a request not to share where you are in a public or online post
acceptedZhAnswers: 请别把我的位置发到网上

examples.en: “Please don't post my location,” I told Jo when she started tagging people at the festival.
examples.zh: 乔在庆典上开始标记参与的人时，我说：“「请别把我的位置发到网上」。”

examples.en: When we took photos near my flat, I texted, “Please don't post my location.”
examples.zh: 我们在我住处附近拍照时，我发了条消息：“「请别把我的位置发到网上」。”

collocations: please don't post my location in your story
please don't post my location while I'm here
also, please don't post my location

words.enDefinition: a request not to save a screenshot of a private chat

examples.en: Before sharing the news in our private chat, I wrote, “Please don't screenshot this conversation.”
examples.zh: 我在私聊里说这件事之前，先写了句：“「请别截这段聊天的图」。”

examples.en: “Please don't screenshot this conversation,” Dara wrote before explaining why she had left the group.
examples.zh: 达拉在解释退群原因之前写道：“「请别截这段聊天的图」。”

collocations: hey, please don't screenshot this conversation
if possible, please don't screenshot this conversation
please don't screenshot this conversation or send it around

words.expression: please don't share my contact details
words.lemma: please don't share my contact details
words.zhGloss: 请别把我的联系方式给别人
words.enDefinition: a request to keep your contact details from being passed on
acceptedZhAnswers: 请别把我的联系方式给别人
acceptedEnVariants: please don't share my contact details

examples.en: “Please don't share my contact details,” I told the coordinator after signing the volunteer form.
examples.zh: 签完志愿者表格后，我对协调员说：“「请别把我的联系方式给别人」。”

examples.en: My flatmate could reach me by email, but I added, “Please don't share my contact details.”
examples.zh: 室友可以发邮件联系我，但我补了一句：“「请别把我的联系方式给别人」。”

collocations: please don't share my contact details outside the group
please don't share my contact details without asking
just to be clear, please don't share my contact details

words.expression: please don't use my project as an example
words.lemma: please don't use my project as an example
words.zhGloss: 请别拿我的项目当范例
words.enDefinition: a request not to present your work to others as a sample
acceptedZhAnswers: 请别拿我的项目当范例
acceptedEnVariants: please don't use my project as an example

examples.en: “Please don't use my project as an example,” I emailed the tutor before the workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊开始前，我给辅导老师发邮件说：“「请别拿我的项目当范例」。”

examples.en: When the class collected sample posters, I replied, “Please don't use my project as an example.”
examples.zh: 班上收集海报范例时，我回道：“「请别拿我的项目当范例」。”

collocations: please don't use my project as an example in class
please don't use my project as an example without asking
for this workshop, please don't use my project as an example

words.enDefinition: a direct request to be forgiven for something the speaker did

examples.en: Please forgive me for sharing your draft without asking whether it was ready to circulate.
examples.zh: 我没问你的草稿能不能传就分享出去了，「请原谅我」。

examples.en: Please forgive me for being careless with something you trusted me to look after.
examples.zh: 你信任我，托我保管的东西我没照看好，「请原谅我」。

collocations: please forgive me for the mistake
please forgive me if I upset you
say please forgive me

words.enDefinition: A request for the person you are listening to to continue what they were saying.

examples.en: Please go on with your story now that everybody has finished finding a seat.
examples.zh: 大家现在都坐好了，「请接着说」你的故事。

examples.en: Please go on where you left off before we had to move the chairs.
examples.zh: 刚才我们要挪椅子，你就停了下来，「请接着说」吧。

collocations: please go on with your story
please go on where you left off
say please go on

words.expression: please keep me out of the photo
words.lemma: please keep me out of the photo
words.enDefinition: a request to be excluded from a photograph
acceptedEnVariants: please keep me out of the photo

examples.en: “Please keep me out of the photo,” I told the volunteer taking pictures at lunch.
examples.zh: 志愿者在午餐时拍照，我说：“「请别把我拍进去」。”

examples.en: When the photographer lifted her camera, I stepped sideways and said, “Please keep me out of the photo.”
examples.zh: 摄影师举起相机时，我往旁边挪了一步，说：“「请别把我拍进去」。”

collocations: please keep me out of the photo for the newsletter
please keep me out of the photo this time
if you can, please keep me out of the photo

words.enDefinition: a request for someone to knock before entering a room you are using

examples.en: “Please knock before coming in,” I told my new flatmate when we discussed sharing the house.
examples.zh: 谈起合住的习惯时，我告诉新室友：“「进来之前请先敲门」。”

examples.en: When my cousin opened my door during class, I said, “Please knock before coming in.”
examples.zh: 表姐在我上课时打开我的房门，我说：“「进来之前请先敲门」。”

collocations: if the door is closed, please knock before coming in
please knock before coming in next time
even if I'm expecting you, please knock before coming in

words.expression: please leave me out of it
words.lemma: please leave me out of it
words.enDefinition: a request not to involve you in a situation or disagreement
acceptedEnVariants: please leave me out of it

examples.en: “Please leave me out of it,” I told my roommates when they started arguing again.
examples.zh: 室友又吵起来时，我说：“「请别把我牵扯进去」。”

examples.en: When one side asked me to pick a winner, I said, “Please leave me out of it.”
examples.zh: 一方要我评谁更有理时，我说：“「请别把我牵扯进去」。”

collocations: please leave me out of it this time
if there's a dispute, please leave me out of it
whatever you decide, please leave me out of it

words.expression: please leave my name out of it
words.lemma: please leave my name out of it
words.zhGloss: 请别在这件事里提我的名字
words.enDefinition: a request to discuss or report something without identifying you
acceptedZhAnswers: 请别在这件事里提我的名字
acceptedEnVariants: please leave my name out of it

examples.en: “Please leave my name out of it,” I told the editor before describing our housing concerns.
examples.zh: 我在说起我们的住宿困扰之前，告诉编辑：“「请别在这件事里提我的名字」。”

examples.en: When my teammate offered to give feedback, I said, “Please leave my name out of it.”
examples.zh: 队友说可以帮忙转达意见，我说：“「请别在这件事里提我的名字」。”

collocations: if it comes up, please leave my name out of it
please leave my name out of it entirely
for now, please leave my name out of it

words.expression: please let me know what you find
words.lemma: please let me know what you find
words.enDefinition: A polite request for someone to share the results after they check something for you.
acceptedEnVariants: please let me know what you find

examples.en: Please let me know what you find after checking which entrance was open that morning.
examples.zh: 麻烦核查当天上午哪个入口开放，「查到什么请告诉我」。

examples.en: Please let me know what you find when you review the notes from our call.
examples.zh: 麻烦看一下我们通话的记录，「查到什么请告诉我」。

collocations: please let me know what you find in the records
please let me know what you find when you check
please let me know what you find about the booking

words.expression: please let me make my own decision
words.lemma: please let me make my own decision
words.enDefinition: a request to retain control over a choice that concerns you
acceptedEnVariants: please let me make my own decision

examples.en: “Please let me make my own decision,” I told my friends while choosing a room.
examples.zh: 挑房间时，我对朋友说：“「请让我自己做决定」。”

examples.en: When my cousin kept recommending one course, I said, “Please let me make my own decision.”
examples.zh: 表姐一再推荐同一门课，我说：“「请让我自己做决定」。”

collocations: I appreciate the advice, but please let me make my own decision
about this, please let me make my own decision
listen, please let me make my own decision

words.enDefinition: a direct request to stop making the same suggestion or asking the same question

examples.en: “Please stop asking,” I said after my classmate brought up the spare ticket for the third time.
examples.zh: 同学第三次提起那张多出来的票时，我说：“「请别再问了」。”

examples.en: When the conversation returned to my grades, I told my friend, “Please stop asking.”
examples.zh: 话题又转回我的成绩时，我对朋友说：“「请别再问了」。”

collocations: please stop asking me to reconsider
please stop asking about my grades
I said no, so please stop asking

words.expression: please take me off the guest list
words.lemma: please take me off the guest list
words.zhGloss: 请把我从来宾名单上划掉
words.enDefinition: a request to remove your name from a list of people expected at an event
acceptedZhAnswers: 请把我从来宾名单上划掉
acceptedEnVariants: please take me off the guest list

examples.en: “Please take me off the guest list,” I wrote after the reception was moved to Thursday.
examples.zh: 招待会改到周四后，我写道：“「请把我从来宾名单上划掉」。”

examples.en: “Please take me off the guest list for the awards dinner,” Dara told the organizer.
examples.zh: 达拉告诉组织者：“「请把我从颁奖晚宴的来宾名单上划掉」。”

collocations: please take me off the guest list for Friday
could you please take me off the guest list
please take me off the guest list before it goes out

words.enDefinition: to show another person which items they should move

examples.en: Could you point out what needs moving before I start clearing the smaller shelf?
examples.zh: 我开始清理小一点的架子前，你能「指出哪些东西需要挪」吗？

examples.en: I asked my neighbour to point out what needs moving in the crowded hallway.
examples.zh: 我请邻居在挤满东西的走廊里「指出哪些东西需要挪」。

collocations: offer to point out what needs moving
ask someone to point out what needs moving
please point out what needs moving

words.enDefinition: to show or say that you think someone is to blame for a problem

examples.en: I did not want to point the finger until we knew why the booking disappeared.
examples.zh: 在弄清预约为什么不见了之前，我不想「指责任何人」。

examples.en: It is easy to point the finger at one person when a group project fails.
examples.zh: 小组项目失败时，很容易就「指责某个人」。

collocations: point the finger at someone
refuse to point the finger
quick to point the finger

words.enDefinition: a considerate response that says no to an invitation or request

examples.en: A polite refusal was enough when my classmate offered me a seat near the front.
examples.zh: 同学说可以把靠前的座位让给我时，「礼貌地拒绝」就够了。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to rewrite the text as a polite refusal of the invitation.
examples.zh: 辅导老师请我们改写这条消息，写成对邀请「礼貌的拒绝」。

collocations: respond with a polite refusal
accept a polite refusal
a brief polite refusal

words.enDefinition: Combine the supplies each person has for the group to use

examples.en: If we pool our supplies, we should have enough paper and tape for every table.
examples.zh: 如果把「物资凑到一起共用」，每张桌子应该都有够用的纸和胶带。

examples.en: We decided to pool our supplies before the workshop instead of asking everyone to bring scissors.
examples.zh: 我们决定在工作坊开始前「把物资集中起来共用」，不用让每个人都自带剪刀。

collocations: agree to pool our supplies
decide to pool our supplies
pool our supplies for the workshop

words.enDefinition: Service that is unhelpful, unreliable, or below a reasonable level of quality.

examples.en: Several visitors mentioned poor service after their questions were ignored at the front desk.
examples.zh: 前台没人理会他们的问题，好几位访客提到了「服务差」。

examples.en: The survey asked students to give a specific example if they had received poor service.
examples.zh: 调查请遇到过「服务差」的学生举个具体例子。

collocations: complain about poor service
experience poor service
a pattern of poor service

words.enDefinition: Comments expressing satisfaction or appreciation for something that went well.

examples.en: I gave positive feedback about the way the receptionist helped our group find another room.
examples.zh: 接待员帮我们小组找到了另一个房间，我就此给了「正面反馈」。

examples.en: The team received positive feedback after changing the way visitors were greeted at the entrance.
examples.zh: 改变了在入口迎接访客的方式后，团队收到了「正面反馈」。

collocations: give positive feedback
receive positive feedback
share positive feedback with the team

words.zhGloss: 避免同样的事再次发生
words.enDefinition: To take action to stop a problem that already happened from recurring.
acceptedZhAnswers: 避免同样的事再次发生

examples.en: The coordinator changed the reminder email to prevent it from happening again at the next workshop.
examples.zh: 协调员改了提醒邮件，以「避免下次工作坊再发生同样的事」。
