examples.zh: 来访时，我们在服务台有了一段「令人不快的经历」，之后我给场馆写了信。

examples.en: The manager asked what had made our first appointment such an unpleasant experience for everyone.
examples.zh: 经理问，第一次预约为什么成了大家一段「令人不快的经历」。

collocations: have an unpleasant experience
report an unpleasant experience
turn into an unpleasant experience

words.enDefinition: Used to say that an expectation is unfair or unrealistic in the circumstances.

examples.en: It seems unreasonable to expect visitors to wait outside when they booked a specific time.
examples.zh: 访客都约了具体时间，「还要求他们在外面等不合理」。

examples.en: I think it is unreasonable to expect people to come back without giving them a date.
examples.zh: 我觉得，「不给具体日期就要求人家再来不合理」。

collocations: unreasonable to expect visitors to wait
unreasonable to expect an immediate answer
seem unreasonable to expect

words.enDefinition: an apology with no qualifications, reservations or excuses attached

examples.en: The editor made an unreserved apology for naming the wrong person in the campus article.
examples.zh: 校园报道写错了人名，编辑作了「毫无保留的道歉」。

examples.en: Her unreserved apology did more to ease the tension than the committee's original statement.
examples.zh: 和委员会最初的声明相比，她「毫无保留的道歉」更能缓解紧张气氛。

collocations: make an unreserved apology
offer an unreserved apology
issue an unreserved apology

words.enDefinition: Open to consideration instead of already decided or fixed

examples.en: The room is booked, but the format of the session is still up for discussion.
examples.zh: 房间已经订了，不过活动怎么开展还是「可以商量的」。

examples.en: Which sections are up for discussion before we send the program to the printer?
examples.zh: 把节目单送印之前，哪些部分还「可以商量」？

collocations: still up for discussion
put something up for discussion
the format is up for discussion

words.expression: up to the person who owns it
words.lemma: up to the person who owns it
words.enDefinition: says the decision belongs to the person owning the item
acceptedEnVariants: up to the person who owns it

examples.en: It's up to the person who owns it whether we can use this table for our display.
examples.zh: 能不能用这张桌子做展示，「由物主决定」。

examples.en: I said it was up to the person who owns it when we found the spare cables.
examples.zh: 找到多出来的线时，我说能不能用「由物主决定」。

collocations: it's up to the person who owns it
say it's up to the person who owns it
leave it up to the person who owns it

words.enDefinition: An advantage of a situation or choice under discussion

examples.en: The upside of rotating teams is that everyone gets to meet new partners.
examples.zh: 轮换分组「有利的一面」是每个人都能认识新搭档。

examples.en: One upside of starting later is that people can attend their tutorials first.
examples.zh: 晚点开始的一个「好处」是大家能先去上辅导课。

collocations: the main upside
see an upside
the upside of starting early

words.expression: use it for as long as you need
words.lemma: use it for as long as you need
words.enDefinition: allows someone to keep using an item until they finish
acceptedEnVariants: use it for as long as you need

examples.en: You can use it for as long as you need while you're working on the model today.
examples.zh: 今天做模型时，这个你「需要用多久就用多久」。

examples.en: She said, "Use it for as long as you need. I'll pick it up another time."
examples.zh: 她说：「需要用多久就用多久」。我改天来拿。

collocations: you can use it for as long as you need
please use it for as long as you need
feel free to use it for as long as you need

words.enDefinition: A complaint made by speaking to someone rather than submitting it in writing.

examples.en: I made a verbal complaint at reception after the guide left our group behind.
examples.zh: 导游没等我们小组就走了，我在接待处做了「口头投诉」。

examples.en: The manager recorded a verbal complaint from a student who could not attend the evening appointment.
examples.zh: 经理记录了一名无法参加晚间预约的学生提出的「口头投诉」。

collocations: make a verbal complaint
receive a verbal complaint
record a verbal complaint

words.enDefinition: asks someone ahead of you to stop or slow down

examples.en: Could you wait up for me by the stairs while I close this bag?
examples.zh: 我把包拉上时，你能在楼梯旁「等等我」吗？

examples.en: Please wait up for me until I have found both of my gloves again.
examples.zh: 请「等等我」，等我把两只手套都找齐。

collocations: can you wait up for me
wait up for me a second
please wait up for me

words.enDefinition: Used to say that something or someone took more time to arrive than you had anticipated.

examples.en: We waited longer than expected at reception even though we had booked a time in advance.
examples.zh: 我们虽然提前预约了时间，还是在接待处「等得比预期久」。

examples.en: I waited longer than expected for a reply, so I checked whether my message had arrived.
examples.zh: 回复「等了比预期更久」，所以我查了一下对方有没有收到消息。

collocations: waited longer than expected for a reply
waited longer than expected at the desk
waited longer than expected to be seen

words.zhGloss: 缓和或收回先前的言论
words.enDefinition: to soften, qualify or partially withdraw something you previously said
acceptedZhAnswers: 缓和或收回先前的言论

examples.en: The chair tried to walk back a remark about cancelling the student event that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午，主席试图「缓和先前的言论」，他说过要取消学生活动。

examples.en: It was difficult to walk back a remark that everyone had already quoted in the group chat.
examples.zh: 大家已经在群聊里引用过那句话，很难再「收回先前的言论」。

collocations: try to walk back a remark
publicly walk back a remark
walk back a remark made earlier

words.enDefinition: a firm way to take a subject off the table for the present conversation

examples.en: “We aren't discussing that today,” the chair said when someone raised another student's personal situation.
examples.zh: 有人提起另一名学生的私事时，主持人说：“「我们今天不谈那件事」。”

examples.en: When the group brought up the argument again, Jo said, “We aren't discussing that today.”
examples.zh: 小组又提起那场争执时，乔说：“「我们今天不谈那件事」。”

collocations: I'm afraid we aren't discussing that today
just to be clear, we aren't discussing that today
we aren't discussing that today in this group

words.zhGloss: 我们俩刚才同时开口了
words.enDefinition: Used to acknowledge that two speakers started talking at the same time.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们俩刚才同时开口了

examples.en: I think we both spoke at once when the receptionist paused to check our booking.
examples.zh: 接待员停下来核查预约时，我想「我们俩刚才同时开口了」。

examples.en: We both spoke at once, so I didn't hear what you asked about tomorrow.
examples.zh: 「我们俩刚才同时开口了」，所以我没听到你问明天的什么事。

collocations: we both spoke at once just then
I think we both spoke at once
laugh because we both spoke at once

words.zhGloss: 我们把彼此的意思弄岔了
words.enDefinition: An informal way to say two people misunderstood each other or received conflicting messages.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们把彼此的意思弄岔了

examples.en: We got our wires crossed because you thought I was bringing the stand tonight.
examples.zh: 你以为我今晚会带架子过来，看来「我们把彼此的意思弄岔了」。

examples.en: I think we got our wires crossed about who was meeting the visitors at the door.
examples.zh: 我觉得关于谁去门口接访客，「我们把彼此的意思弄岔了」。

collocations: I think we got our wires crossed
we got our wires crossed about the date
explain how we got our wires crossed

words.enDefinition: A reply reassuring someone that their concern will receive careful attention.

examples.en: We take this seriously and will speak to the people who worked at the desk.
examples.zh: 「我们很重视这件事」，会找当时在服务台值班的人沟通。

examples.en: Please know that we take this seriously, especially when several visitors had the same experience.
examples.zh: 请放心，「我们很重视这件事」，尤其是有几位访客遇到了同样的问题。

collocations: we take this seriously and will check
tell the visitor we take this seriously
please know we take this seriously

words.enDefinition: Used to say that people did not inform your group before making a decision or change.

examples.en: We weren't told in advance that we'd need to collect our passes at another building.
examples.zh: 「事先没人告诉我们」要去另一栋楼领通行证。

examples.en: I said we weren't told in advance that the shuttle would stop running before the concert ended.
examples.zh: 我说，「事先没人告诉我们」接驳车会在音乐会结束前停运。

collocations: we weren't told in advance about the closure
we weren't told in advance that it had changed
explain that we weren't told in advance

words.expression: we won't bring it up again unless you do
words.lemma: we won't bring it up again unless you do
words.zhGloss: 你不主动提，我们就不会再提
words.enDefinition: a promise not to raise a sensitive subject unless the other person chooses to
acceptedZhAnswers: 你不主动提，我们就不会再提
acceptedEnVariants: we won't bring it up again unless you do

examples.en: “We won't bring it up again unless you do,” I reassured Jo after the meeting.
examples.zh: 会后我宽慰乔：“「你不主动提，我们就不会再提」。”

examples.en: Lee asked us to stop, so we said, “We won't bring it up again unless you do.”
examples.zh: 李请我们打住，于是我们说：“「你不主动提，我们就不会再提」。”

collocations: don't worry, we won't bring it up again unless you do
we promise we won't bring it up again unless you do
in the group, we won't bring it up again unless you do

words.enDefinition: Consider the advantages and drawbacks of the choices before deciding

examples.en: We should weigh up the options once we know which practice rooms are available.
examples.zh: 等知道哪些排练室有空，我们再「权衡各种方案」。

examples.en: Let's weigh up the options with everyone present, including the two people joining remotely.
examples.zh: 我们等人齐了再「权衡各种方案」，也算上那两位远程参加的人。

collocations: take time to weigh up the options
weigh up the options carefully
weigh up the options together

words.enDefinition: Used when the two speakers are apparently discussing different subjects or examples.

examples.en: I think we're talking about different things because I meant the key for the cupboard.
examples.zh: 我指的是柜子的钥匙，看来「我们说的不是一回事」。

examples.en: We're talking about different things, since I meant the cloth we use for the kitchen table.
examples.zh: 「我们说的不是一回事」，我指的是厨房餐桌上用的那块布。

collocations: I think we're talking about different things
realise we're talking about different things
explain that we're talking about different things

words.zhGloss: 我们在从哪些选项中选
words.enDefinition: Ask what the possible choices are before making a selection
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们在从哪些选项中选

examples.en: We've heard several ideas today, so what are we choosing between for the first event?
examples.zh: 今天听到了好几个点子，那第一场活动「我们到底在从哪些选项里选」？

examples.en: Before I vote, what are we choosing between for the order of the short talks?
examples.zh: 在我投票之前，能说说短讲顺序「我们有哪些备选」吗？

collocations: what are we choosing between for the venue
what are we choosing between this time
what are we choosing between exactly

words.enDefinition: A question asking which thing, person, or earlier statement someone has in mind.

examples.en: What are you referring to when you say we need the old one back?
examples.zh: 你说我们得把旧的拿回来，「你指的是什么」？

examples.en: What are you referring to on this list when you mention the spare equipment?
examples.zh: 你提到备用设备时，「指的是这份清单上的哪一项」？

collocations: what are you referring to on this list
what are you referring to exactly
ask what are you referring to

words.enDefinition: A question asking for the next step, line, or event immediately following the one just mentioned.

examples.en: What comes right after that step where you check the number on the back?
examples.zh: 查背面数字那一步，「之后紧接着是什么」？

examples.en: Could you show me what comes right after that in the instructions on the box?
examples.zh: 你能给我看看包装盒的说明里，「那之后紧接着是什么」吗？

collocations: what comes right after that step
ask what comes right after that
show me what comes right after that

words.enDefinition: Used when asking what qualifies as a particular kind of thing under a description or rule.

examples.en: We asked what counts as a guest when people from other flats come over for dinner.
examples.zh: 其他公寓的人来吃饭时，我们问「什么样的人算客人」。

examples.en: Could you explain what counts as enough notice for changing the rehearsal time with everyone?
examples.zh: 需要跟大家改排练时间时，你能解释一下「提前多久通知算够」吗？

collocations: what counts as a guest
what counts as a large item
ask what counts as enough notice

words.expression: what does that mean in practice
words.lemma: what does that mean in practice
words.enDefinition: A question asking how an idea, instruction, or rule works in a real situation.
acceptedEnVariants: what does that mean in practice

examples.en: What does that mean in practice for people who share the kitchen with another flat?
examples.zh: 和另一户合用厨房的人「实际会怎么做」？

examples.en: What does that mean in practice if we all need to collect our keys separately?
examples.zh: 如果我们得各自领钥匙，「具体到实际是怎样的」？

collocations: what does that mean in practice for us
what does that mean in practice here
ask what does that mean in practice

words.enDefinition: A question asking what full name or phrase a letter or abbreviation represents.

examples.en: What does that stand for in the message you sent about tomorrow's rehearsal time?
examples.zh: 你发的明天排练时间的消息里，「这是哪几个词的缩写」？

examples.en: What does that stand for on the board where the old room number was written?
examples.zh: 以前板上写旧房间号的地方，「现在的字母是哪几个词的缩写」？

collocations: what does that stand for on the form
what does that stand for in this list
ask what does that stand for

words.enDefinition: Ask for another possibility after discussing one or more ideas

examples.en: The lecture hall has no free slots, so what else could work for our rehearsal?
examples.zh: 报告厅没有空档，那我们的排练「还有什么可行的方案」？

examples.en: If we can't move the furniture, what else could work for the group photo?
examples.zh: 如果家具不能挪，拍集体照「还有什么可行的方案」？

collocations: what else could work for Friday
ask what else could work
think about what else could work

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to identify the particular changes they just referred to.

examples.en: What exactly changed in the instructions for returning dishes to the shared kitchen this week?
examples.zh: 这周把盘子放回共用厨房的说明「具体有什么变动」？

examples.en: What exactly changed between the message I saw and the one sent out this morning?
examples.zh: 我看到的消息和今天上午发的那条，内容「具体有什么变动」？

collocations: what exactly changed on the form
what exactly changed since yesterday
ask what exactly changed

words.enDefinition: A question asking what an organisation does once you have made a complaint.

examples.en: Could you explain what happens after I complain about the way the booking was handled?
examples.zh: 如果我投诉预订的处理方式，您能解释一下「投诉之后会怎样」吗？

examples.en: I need to know what happens after I complain before I speak for the group.
examples.zh: 在代表小组发言前，我得知道「投诉之后会怎样」。

collocations: explain what happens after I complain
tell me what happens after I complain
ask what happens after I complain

words.enDefinition: An opening for restating the question you had intended when someone answered a different point.

examples.en: What I was asking was whether the second key still opens the door downstairs.
examples.zh: 「我刚才问的是」，第二把钥匙还能不能打开楼下的门。

examples.en: What I was asking was how we would explain the change to visitors arriving late.
examples.zh: 「我刚才问的是」，我们会怎么跟迟到的访客解释这一变更。

collocations: what I was asking was whether
what I was asking was how
what I was asking was about the time

words.enDefinition: A question asking what evidence or reasoning led someone to make a particular statement.

examples.en: What makes you say that the keys have to stay in this drawer overnight?
examples.zh: 「你为什么这么说」，觉得钥匙晚上得留在这个抽屉里？

examples.en: What makes you say that the new labels will confuse people using the washing machines?
examples.zh: 「你为什么觉得」新标签会让用洗衣机的人看不明白？

collocations: what makes you say that about the room
what makes you say that now
ask what makes you say that

words.enDefinition: Ask which consideration the other person thinks is most important

examples.en: What matters most to you when we decide how to share the booth on Friday?
examples.zh: 我们决定周五怎么共用展台时，「你最看重什么」？

examples.en: Before we compare rooms, tell me what matters most to you when you run a workshop.
examples.zh: 比较场地前，先告诉我办工作坊时「你最看重什么」。

collocations: what matters most to you about this plan
ask what matters most to you
tell me what matters most to you

words.expression: what part do you want me to handle
words.lemma: what part do you want me to handle
words.enDefinition: asks which piece of work the other person wants done
acceptedEnVariants: what part do you want me to handle

examples.en: What part do you want me to handle while you finish the labels for the other table?
examples.zh: 你给另一张桌子做完标签之前，「你想让我负责哪一段」？

examples.en: What part do you want me to handle? I can prepare the chairs or collect the folders.
examples.zh: 「你想让我负责哪一段」？我可以摆椅子，也可以收文件夹。

collocations: what part do you want me to handle first
what part do you want me to handle today
ask what part you want me to handle

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone for the general type of thing, activity, or situation they mean.

examples.en: What sort of thing do you have in mind for the space near the door?
examples.zh: 对于门边那块地方，「你想放什么样的东西」？

examples.en: I asked what sort of thing would count as an extra task for the volunteers.
examples.zh: 我问，「什么样的事情」算志愿者的额外任务。

collocations: what sort of thing do you have in mind
ask what sort of thing
what sort of thing would count

words.enDefinition: A question asking what actions people have carried out so far to deal with a problem.

examples.en: Could you tell me what steps have been taken to correct the information on the notice?
examples.zh: 请问为了修正通知上的信息，「已经采取了哪些措施」？

examples.en: The group asked what steps have been taken since its complaint about the entrance signs.
examples.zh: 小组询问，投诉入口的指示牌之后，「已经采取了哪些措施」。

collocations: ask what steps have been taken
explain what steps have been taken
find out what steps have been taken

words.enDefinition: A question asking what information or assumptions supported an estimate, judgement, or claim already mentioned.

examples.en: What was that based on, the number of people invited or the people who replied?
examples.zh: 「那是根据什么得出的」，是受邀人数还是已经回复的人数？

examples.en: The estimate seemed too high, so I asked, “What was that based on?” as we walked out.
examples.zh: 估算看起来偏高，所以我们边走出去，我边问「那是根据什么得出的」？

collocations: what was that based on at the time
what was that based on exactly
ask what was that based on

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to repeat the ending of what they just said.

examples.en: What was the last part of the address you gave me for the rehearsal tonight?
examples.zh: 你刚给了我今晚排练的地址，「最后那部分是什么」？

examples.en: What was the last part again before everyone started talking at the same time?
examples.zh: 大家一起开口之前那句，「最后那部分是什么」来着？

collocations: what was the last part of that
what was the last part again
ask what was the last part

words.enDefinition: invites someone to say what kind of help would be useful

examples.en: What would make this easier for you while I have both hands free anyway?
examples.zh: 反正我这会儿能腾出双手，「怎么做会容易些」？

examples.en: She asked, "What would make this easier?" when she saw the piles of books.
examples.zh: 看到那几摞书时，她问：「怎么做会容易些」？

collocations: ask what would make this easier
what would make this easier for you
think about what would make this easier

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to describe the details of a proposed idea or situation.

examples.en: What would that look like on the day if we meet people at two entrances?
examples.zh: 如果我们在两个入口接人，「当天具体会是什么样」？

examples.en: What would that look like for someone who has never been to our building?
examples.zh: 对从没来过这栋楼的人来说，「具体会是什么样」？

collocations: what would that look like on the day
what would that look like for us
ask what would that look like

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to explain how two points, events, or ideas are related.

examples.en: What's the connection between the extra keys and the change to the guest list?
examples.zh: 多出来的钥匙和宾客名单的改动，「这之间有什么关系」？

examples.en: What's the connection here between how many people came and which door was open?
examples.zh: 来的人数和开的是哪扇门，「这之间有什么关系」？

collocations: what's the connection between the two
what's the connection here
ask what's the connection

words.expression: when can I expect a response
words.lemma: when can i expect a response
words.zhGloss: 我大概什么时候能收到答复
words.enDefinition: A question asking for an estimate of when someone will answer a message or complaint.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我大概什么时候能收到答复
acceptedEnVariants: when can I expect a response

examples.en: When can I expect a response to my complaint about the closing time last Friday?
examples.zh: 关于上周五关门时间的投诉，「我大概什么时候能收到答复」？

examples.en: When can I expect a response from the manager about the issue we discussed this morning?
examples.zh: 关于今天上午谈到的问题，「我大概什么时候能收到经理的答复」？

collocations: when can I expect a response to my complaint
when can I expect a response about this
when can I expect a response from your team

words.expression: when do you need it back
words.lemma: when do you need it back
words.enDefinition: asks when borrowed material must be handed back to the owner
acceptedEnVariants: when do you need it back

examples.en: When do you need it back? I can come back to this room again after lunch.
examples.zh: 「你需要我什么时候还」？午饭后我可以再来这儿。

examples.en: When do you need it back if I take it upstairs to show my group first?
examples.zh: 如果我先拿上楼给组员看看，「你需要我什么时候还」？

collocations: when do you need it back this week
ask when you need it back
when do you need it back by

words.expression: when would you like it by
words.lemma: when would you like it by
words.zhGloss: 你希望最迟什么时候拿到
words.enDefinition: asks what latest time is acceptable for doing a task
acceptedZhAnswers: 你希望最迟什么时候拿到
acceptedEnVariants: when would you like it by

examples.en: When would you like it by if I'm making you a spare copy of the map?
examples.zh: 如果我多复印一份地图给你，「你希望最迟什么时候拿到」？

examples.en: When would you like it by? I can leave it on the shelf after class.
examples.zh: 「你希望最迟什么时候拿到」？我下课后可以放在架子上。

collocations: when would you like it by today
when would you like it by this week
ask when you would like it by

words.enDefinition: indicates that a requested action is possible at a convenient time

examples.en: Could you show her the poster when you get a chance after the meeting?
examples.zh: 开完会，能「等你有空的时候」把海报给她看看吗？

examples.en: Please put my notebook back on the shelf when you get a chance today.
examples.zh: 今天「等你有空的时候」，请帮我把笔记本放回书架。

collocations: check it when you get a chance
bring it back when you get a chance
take a look when you get a chance

words.enDefinition: An opening used to repeat a word or phrase you want the speaker to explain.

examples.en: When you say upstairs, do you mean the first landing or the floor above it?
examples.zh: 「你说楼上的时候」，指的是第一处楼梯平台，还是再上一层？

examples.en: When you say the next meeting, are you talking about Friday or next week?
examples.zh: 「你说下次碰面的时候」，指的是周五还是下周？

collocations: when you say upstairs
when you say it's close
when you say the next meeting

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to show the point where your interpretation or reasoning became incorrect.

examples.en: Where did I go wrong when I tried to repeat the directions from the map?
examples.zh: 我试着复述地图上的路线时，「哪里理解错了」？

examples.en: Where did I go wrong in my explanation of which drawer the keys belong in?
examples.zh: 我说明钥匙该放哪个抽屉时，「哪里理解错了」？

collocations: where did I go wrong in my explanation
where did I go wrong this time
ask where did I go wrong

words.enDefinition: asks where the recipient wants you to leave something

examples.en: Where should I leave it if the desk is closed by the time I arrive?
examples.zh: 如果我到的时候服务台已经关了，「我该把它放哪儿」？

examples.en: Where should I leave it after I bring it back from the room upstairs?
examples.zh: 我把它从楼上的房间拿回来之后，「该把它放哪儿」？

collocations: where should I leave it for you
where should I leave it after class
ask where I should leave it

words.enDefinition: A question a speaker asks when trying to remember where they paused or were interrupted.

examples.en: Where was I before the delivery driver called about the boxes we were expecting?
examples.zh: 送货司机打电话问我们等的箱子之前，「我刚刚说到哪儿了」？

examples.en: Where was I again before we stopped to let those people walk past us?
examples.zh: 我们停下来让那些人先过去之前，「我刚刚说到哪儿了」？

collocations: where was I before the break
where was I again
ask where was I

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to identify a particular thing among several possibilities.

examples.en: Which one do you mean, the big box by the door or the smaller one?
examples.zh: 「你指的是哪一个」，门边的大箱子还是小一点的那个？

examples.en: Which one do you mean on the map when you say the main staircase?
examples.zh: 你说主楼梯时，「指的是地图上的哪一个」？

collocations: which one do you mean on the shelf
which one do you mean on the map
ask which one do you mean

words.expression: which one do you want me to bring
words.lemma: which one do you want me to bring
words.enDefinition: asks which one of several items the other person wants
acceptedEnVariants: which one do you want me to bring

examples.en: Which one do you want me to bring from the two folders next to the printer upstairs?
examples.zh: 楼上打印机旁的两个文件夹，「你想让我带哪一个」？

examples.en: Which one do you want me to bring? There are three folding chairs in the spare room.
examples.zh: 「你想让我带哪一个」？备用间里有三把折叠椅。

collocations: which one do you want me to bring downstairs
which one do you want me to bring today
ask which one you want me to bring

words.expression: which part are you talking about
words.lemma: which part are you talking about
words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to point out the section or stage they mean.
acceptedEnVariants: which part are you talking about

examples.en: Which part are you talking about when you say the video was hard to follow?
examples.zh: 你说视频很难看懂，「说的是哪一部分」？

examples.en: Which part are you talking about, the first paragraph or the note at the bottom?
examples.zh: 「你说的是哪一部分」，第一段还是底部的注释？

collocations: which part are you talking about in the instructions
which part are you talking about exactly
ask which part are you talking about

words.zhGloss: 你刚才重读的是哪个词
words.enDefinition: A question asking which word in a phrase someone emphasised to convey their meaning.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你刚才重读的是哪个词

examples.en: Which word did you stress when you told us to leave the small room unlocked?
examples.zh: 你让我们别锁小房间时，「刚才重读的是哪个词」？

examples.en: Which word did you stress in that sentence about who should bring the blue box?
examples.zh: 你说该由谁带蓝箱子那句话里，「重读的是哪个词」？

collocations: which word did you stress in that sentence
ask which word did you stress
which word did you stress when you repeated it

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to identify the person currently being discussed.

examples.en: Who are we talking about when you mention the person who opened the hall first?
examples.zh: 你说最早开大厅的那个人，「我们说的是谁」？

examples.en: Who are we talking about here, your flatmate or the person from the upstairs flat?
examples.zh: 「我们说的是谁」，你的室友还是住楼上的那个人？

collocations: who are we talking about here
who are we talking about in this story
ask who are we talking about

words.enDefinition: A question used to find the person or department responsible for receiving and handling complaints.

examples.en: Could you tell me who deals with complaints about bookings at the sports centre?
examples.zh: 关于体育中心的预约问题，请问「谁负责处理投诉」？

examples.en: I asked who deals with complaints because the instructor was unable to change the arrangement herself.
examples.zh: 因为教练自己无法更改安排，我就问了「谁负责处理投诉」。

collocations: ask who deals with complaints
find out who deals with complaints
tell me who deals with complaints

words.expression: who should I give it to
words.lemma: who should i give it to
words.enDefinition: checks who is meant to receive the item you are carrying
acceptedEnVariants: who should I give it to

examples.en: Who should I give it to once I've picked it up from the front desk?
examples.zh: 我从前台领到以后，「该把它交给谁」？

examples.en: Who should I give it to? Both groups asked me whether it was for them.
examples.zh: 「我该把它交给谁」？两个组都问我是不是给他们的。

collocations: who should I give it to when I get there
who should I give it to after lunch
ask who I should give it to

words.enDefinition: to start again while agreeing not to count earlier mistakes against someone

examples.en: We agreed to wipe the slate clean before choosing roles for the new project.
examples.zh: 选新项目的分工前，我们同意「把过往清零，从头来过」。

examples.en: The committee wanted to wipe the slate clean after the new members heard both sides.
examples.zh: 新会员听过双方说法后，委员会希望「把过往清零，从头来过」。

collocations: agree to wipe the slate clean
want to wipe the slate clean
try to wipe the slate clean

words.enDefinition: To ask for a complaint you made to be taken out of the process before it proceeds further.

examples.en: I chose to withdraw a complaint after the centre showed me the corrected schedule for our tour.
examples.zh: 中心给我看了更正后的导览日程后，我选择「撤回投诉」。

examples.en: The adviser explained how to withdraw a complaint if we no longer wanted it reviewed.
examples.zh: 顾问解释了，如果我们不想再复核，可以怎么「撤回投诉」。

collocations: choose to withdraw a complaint
ask how to withdraw a complaint
decide not to withdraw a complaint

words.enDefinition: Without being given a clear reason for a decision or change.

examples.en: The shuttle route was changed without a clear reason during the first week of term.
examples.zh: 开学第一周接驳车改了线路，却「没有给出明确的理由」。

examples.en: We were turned away without a clear reason even after showing the receptionist our passes.
examples.zh: 即使出示了通行证，接待员仍不让我们进去，也「没有给出明确的理由」。

collocations: cancelled without a clear reason
changed without a clear reason
turned away without a clear reason

words.enDefinition: describes taking responsibility or explaining what happened without trying to avoid blame

examples.en: She explained why the tickets were missing without making excuses for how she handled them.
examples.zh: 她解释了票为什么不见了，「没有为自己的处理方式找借口」。

examples.en: I wanted to apologise without making excuses for forgetting the equipment we needed that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午要用的器材我忘了带，我想道歉，「不为自己找借口」。

collocations: apologise without making excuses
take responsibility without making excuses
explain without making excuses

words.enDefinition: Do different parts of the same job at the same time

examples.en: We can work in parallel if one team sorts the files while the other writes.
examples.zh: 如果一组整理文件，另一组同时写作，我们就能「并行工作」。

examples.en: Let's work in parallel so the design doesn't have to wait for the room layout.
examples.zh: 我们「同时开展工作」吧，这样做设计就不用等场地布局定下来。

collocations: allow two teams to work in parallel
work in parallel on separate sections
plan to work in parallel

words.expression: would it be okay if I
words.lemma: would it be okay if i
words.enDefinition: introduces a polite question asking permission for a proposed action
acceptedEnVariants: would it be okay if I

examples.en: Would it be okay if I left my bag beside this empty chair for a minute?
examples.zh: 「我把包放在空椅子旁一会儿，可以吗」？

examples.en: Would it be okay if I used the small table to finish cutting my poster today?
examples.zh: 「我用小桌子剪完海报，可以吗」？

collocations: would it be okay if I stayed
would it be okay if I used yours
would it be okay if I left it here

words.expression: would it help if I took one
words.lemma: would it help if i took one
words.enDefinition: offers to carry one item to make someone's task easier
acceptedEnVariants: would it help if I took one

examples.en: Would it help if I took one of the folders while you open the cupboard door?
examples.zh: 你打开柜门时，「要我帮你拿一个文件夹吗」？

examples.en: Would it help if I took one? You look like you need a free hand here.
examples.zh: 「要我帮你拿一个吗」？看起来你这会儿得腾出一只手。

collocations: would it help if I took one of the bags
ask if it would help if I took one
would it help if I took one downstairs

words.expression: would you help me carry these
words.lemma: would you help me carry these
words.zhGloss: 能帮我搬一下这些东西吗
words.enDefinition: asks someone to carry several things together with you
acceptedZhAnswers: 能帮我搬一下这些东西吗
acceptedEnVariants: would you help me carry these

examples.en: Would you help me carry these to the side hall where our group is meeting?
examples.zh: 「能帮我搬一下这些东西吗」？我们组在侧厅聚。

examples.en: Would you help me carry these? The books are heavier than I thought they would be.
examples.zh: 「能帮我搬一下这些东西吗」？这些书比我预想的沉。

collocations: would you help me carry these boxes
would you help me carry these downstairs
ask if you would help me carry these

words.expression: would you let me know when it arrives
words.lemma: would you let me know when it arrives
words.enDefinition: asks someone to inform you when an expected item arrives
acceptedEnVariants: would you let me know when it arrives

examples.en: Would you let me know when it arrives? The equipment bag should have a blue label on it.
examples.zh: 「到了能告诉我吗」？器材包上应该贴了张蓝色标签。

examples.en: Would you let me know when it arrives so I can be downstairs before the driver leaves?
examples.zh: 「到了能告诉我吗」？这样我能赶在司机离开前下楼。

collocations: would you let me know when it arrives please
ask if you would let me know when it arrives
would you let me know when it arrives downstairs

words.zhGloss: 介意帮我拿一下这个吗
words.enDefinition: asks someone to hold an item for a short time
acceptedZhAnswers: 介意帮我拿一下这个吗

examples.en: Would you mind holding this while I use both hands to close the suitcase?
examples.zh: 我得用两只手合上行李箱，「介意帮我拿一下这个吗」？

examples.en: Would you mind holding this for a second? I can't reach my key otherwise.
examples.zh: 「介意帮我拿一下这个吗」？不然我够不着钥匙。

collocations: would you mind holding this for me
would you mind holding this for a second
would you mind holding this while I get ready

words.enDefinition: asks someone informally to move a short distance backwards

examples.en: Would you mind scooting back so we can reach the handle on the cupboard?
examples.zh: 「介意往后挪一点吗」？我们想够到柜门的把手。

examples.en: Would you mind scooting back? We need enough space to turn the cart around.
examples.zh: 「介意往后挪一点吗」？我们得留够空间把推车转过来。

collocations: would you mind scooting back a little
would you mind scooting back in your chair
ask if you would mind scooting back

words.expression: would you mind watering the plants
words.lemma: would you mind watering the plants
words.zhGloss: 介意帮我给植物浇水吗
words.enDefinition: asks someone to water plants on your behalf
acceptedZhAnswers: 介意帮我给植物浇水吗
acceptedEnVariants: would you mind watering the plants

examples.en: Would you mind watering the plants while I take the cleaning supplies back downstairs?
examples.zh: 我把清洁用具拿回楼下时，「介意帮我给植物浇水吗」？

examples.en: Would you mind watering the plants on Sunday if you are going out onto the balcony anyway?
examples.zh: 周日如果你正好要去阳台，「介意帮我给植物浇水吗」？

collocations: would you mind watering the plants this weekend
would you mind watering the plants while I'm away
ask if you would mind watering the plants

words.expression: would you move it somewhere else
words.lemma: would you move it somewhere else
words.enDefinition: asks someone to move something away from its present location
acceptedEnVariants: would you move it somewhere else

examples.en: Would you move it somewhere else while I clear the space nearest the front door?
examples.zh: 我把最靠近前门的那块地方腾空时，「能把它移到别处吗」？

examples.en: Would you move it somewhere else? This shelf is already full of equipment for class.
examples.zh: 「能把它移到别处吗」？这个架子已经堆满了上课用的器材。

collocations: would you move it somewhere else please
would you move it somewhere else for now
ask if you would move it somewhere else

words.expression: would you rather I left it here
words.lemma: would you rather i left it here
words.zhGloss: 你更希望我把它留这儿吗
words.enDefinition: asks if leaving something in its present location is preferred
acceptedZhAnswers: 你更希望我把它留这儿吗
acceptedEnVariants: would you rather I left it here

examples.en: Would you rather I left it here, or should I take it down to the entrance?
examples.zh: 「你更希望我把它留这儿吗」？还是该拿到入口那儿？

examples.en: Would you rather I left it here until the others have finished using the table today?
examples.zh: 直到今天其他人用完桌子，「你更希望我把它留这儿吗」？

collocations: would you rather I left it here until lunch
ask if you would rather I left it here
would you rather I left it here for you

words.enDefinition: Make a written note of the arrangements the group has accepted

examples.en: Could someone write down what we agreed about the rehearsal order before we move on?
examples.zh: 继续往下谈之前，能有人「记下商定的排练顺序」吗？

examples.en: Let's write down what we agreed so students who missed the meeting can check the details.
examples.zh: 我们「把共识写下来」吧，这样错过会议的同学也能核对细节。

collocations: remember to write down what we agreed
write down what we agreed at the meeting
write down what we agreed about timing

words.enDefinition: an apology communicated in writing, such as in a formal letter, email or statement

examples.en: The volunteers received a written apology from the committee after the incident was reviewed.
examples.zh: 复核那件事后，志愿者收到了委员会的「书面道歉」。

examples.en: A written apology reached everyone who had received the incorrect notice about the closure.
examples.zh: 收到错误闭馆通知的每个人都拿到了「书面道歉」。

collocations: send a written apology
receive a written apology
request a written apology

words.enDefinition: Details someone gives you that turn out to be incorrect.

examples.en: I was given the wrong information about the time of the last guided tour.
examples.zh: 别人告诉我的最后一场导览的时间是「错误信息」。

examples.en: Our group missed the introduction because we received the wrong information about where to meet.
examples.zh: 我们收到的集合地点是「错误信息」，所以小组错过了开场介绍。

collocations: give someone the wrong information
receive the wrong information
correct wrong information

words.enDefinition: a way to suggest another person when you cannot commit to helping

examples.en: “You can ask someone else,” I told the coordinator when she needed a volunteer today.
examples.zh: 协调员当天需要一名志愿者，我说：“「你可以问问别人」。”

examples.en: “You can ask someone else if you need a decision sooner,” Nia told her lab partner.
examples.zh: 妮娅对实验搭档说：“如果你得早点定下来，「你可以问问别人」。”

collocations: feel free to ask someone else
you can ask someone else on the team
you can ask someone else in the meantime

words.expression: you can borrow it until five
words.lemma: you can borrow it until five
words.enDefinition: a way to agree to lend something while specifying when it must be returned
acceptedEnVariants: you can borrow it until five

examples.en: “You can borrow it until five,” I told Jay when he asked for my calculator.
examples.zh: 杰伊来借计算器时，我说：“「你可以借用到五点」。”

examples.en: When Nia asked about my tripod, I said, “You can borrow it until five.”
examples.zh: 妮娅问能不能借我的三脚架，我说：“「你可以借用到五点」。”

collocations: sure, you can borrow it until five
just so you know, you can borrow it until five
I need it this evening, so you can borrow it until five

words.expression: you can email me, but please don't call
words.lemma: you can email me, but please don't call
words.zhGloss: 可以给我发邮件，但请别打电话
words.enDefinition: a way to allow contact by email while asking someone not to phone
acceptedZhAnswers: 可以给我发邮件，但请别打电话
acceptedEnVariants: you can email me, but please don't call

examples.en: “You can email me, but please don't call,” I told the coordinator before my afternoon lab.
examples.zh: 下午上实验课前，我告诉协调员：“「可以给我发邮件，但请别打电话」。”

examples.en: When the club asked how to reach me, I replied, “You can email me, but please don't call.”
examples.zh: 社团问怎么联系我，我回道：“「可以给我发邮件，但请别打电话」。”

collocations: you can email me, but please don't call during class
for updates, you can email me, but please don't call
you can email me, but please don't call after six

words.enDefinition: a way to make clear that participation or agreement is optional

examples.en: I offered my neighbor a lift, then added, “You can say no if you'd rather walk.”
examples.zh: 我提出开车送邻居，又补了一句：“如果你更想走路，「你可以拒绝」。”

examples.en: “You can say no,” Sam told the new member before handing over the volunteer form.
examples.zh: 萨姆把志愿者表格交给新成员前，说：“「你可以拒绝」。”

collocations: it's completely fine, you can say no
you can always say no
of course you can say no

words.expression: you don't have to decide today
words.lemma: you don't have to decide today
words.enDefinition: a way to give someone more time to make a choice
acceptedEnVariants: you don't have to decide today

examples.en: “You don't have to decide today,” the coordinator said when I asked about weekly volunteering.
examples.zh: 我问起每周做志愿服务的事，协调员说：“「你不用今天就决定」。”

examples.en: When I offered Mei the spare room, I added, “You don't have to decide today.”
examples.zh: 我说可以把空房间给梅住，又补了一句：“「你不用今天就决定」。”

collocations: don't worry, you don't have to decide today
take a look first, you don't have to decide today
you don't have to decide today if you need longer

words.expression: you don't have to forgive me
words.lemma: you don't have to forgive me
words.enDefinition: acknowledges that the other person is under no obligation to forgive after an apology
acceptedEnVariants: you don't have to forgive me

examples.en: You don't have to forgive me, but I wanted you to hear me acknowledge the mistake.
examples.zh: 「你不必原谅我」，但我想让你亲耳听到我承认过错。

examples.en: You don't have to forgive me right now, and I won't bring it up again tonight.
examples.zh: 现在「你不必原谅我」，今晚我也不会再提这事。

collocations: you don't have to forgive me today
you don't have to forgive me right away
say you don't have to forgive me

words.enDefinition: gives someone friendly permission to use an item of yours

examples.en: You're welcome to use mine while I'm waiting for the others to arrive here.
examples.zh: 我在这儿等其他人来的时候，「你可以用我的」。

examples.en: You're welcome to use mine if the charger on your desk doesn't reach the outlet.
examples.zh: 你的充电器够不着插座的话，「你可以用我的」。

collocations: of course you're welcome to use mine
you're welcome to use mine for now
remember you're welcome to use mine

words.enDefinition: A way to invite someone to continue speaking, often by reminding them about their previous point.

examples.en: You were saying something about the side entrance before the coach drove past us.
examples.zh: 长途车从我们旁边开过去之前，「你刚才说到」侧门的事。

examples.en: You were saying we should meet by the smaller sign before the call dropped.
examples.zh: 电话断线前，「你刚才说到」我们该在小一点的牌子旁碰面。

collocations: you were saying something about the schedule
you were saying before the interruption
you were saying we should

words.enDefinition: The way you describe or explain what happened, especially when others have a different account.

examples.en: The manager said she wanted to hear your side of the story before reaching a decision.
examples.zh: 经理说，她想先听听「你对事情经过的说法」，再做决定。

examples.en: You can tell your side of the story before the group meets with the organiser tomorrow.
examples.zh: 明天小组和组织者见面前，你可以先讲讲「你对事情经过的说法」。

collocations: hear your side of the story
tell your side of the story
ask for your side of the story

words.zhGloss: 你的声音听起来闷闷的
words.enDefinition: Used to tell someone that their voice sounds covered or less clear than usual.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你的声音听起来闷闷的

examples.en: Your voice sounds muffled over the phone, especially when you turn away from it.
examples.zh: 电话里「你的声音听起来闷闷的」，特别是你转身背对手机的时候。

examples.en: Your voice sounds muffled through the door, so let me know when you're inside.
examples.zh: 隔着门「你的声音听起来闷闷的」，你进来后跟我说一声吧。

collocations: your voice sounds muffled over the phone
tell them your voice sounds muffled
your voice sounds muffled through the door
